OtySmPTC5o.one_liner: Proves expected tabular TD updates strictly decrease the stationary-weighted absolute Bellman error, yielding convergence and a trust-region interpretation.
OtySmPTC5o.problem: The expected TD update is not the negative gradient of any global objective, even in the tabular setting, which limits optimization-based interpretation and analysis of TD.
OtySmPTC5o.method: They show that an expected single-state tabular TD update strictly decreases the stationary-weighted absolute Bellman error whenever that state's Bellman error is nonzero, for any step size in (0,1]. They derive convergence under standard cumulative-step-size conditions and a finite-sample bound for sampled TD under independent sampling, and write each expected update as the solution of a trust-region subproblem for a linear model of the absolute Bellman error.
OtySmPTC5o.key_idea: Use the stationary-weighted absolute Bellman error as a global descent measure that every single-state expected TD update strictly reduces.
OtySmPTC5o.evidence: Theory only: a monotone descent theorem, convergence under standard cumulative-step-size conditions, a finite-sample bound under independent sampling, and a trust-region interpretation.
OtySmPTC5o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the descent theorem is simple, technically sound, and gives a clear optimization perspective on expected tabular TD, in a well-written paper.
OtySmPTC5o.main_concern: Applicability beyond the tabular setting is unclear, and one reviewer argues the main descent theorem is a special case of an existing residual inequality by Frommer and Szyld.

kmfNwHyohD.one_liner: Data engine that decomposes images into concept trees to build multi-reference image generation data, yielding RefTree-480K and RefTree-Bench.
kmfNwHyohD.problem: Open-weight image generation models lag proprietary ones on multi-reference generation, especially as the number of references grows and they form hierarchical dependencies.
kmfNwHyohD.method: RefTree recursively decomposes target images into trees of visual concepts, and collaborative agents extract the concepts as reference images, verify consistency, and compose reference-grounded prompts via bottom-up merging, without closed-source models. This yields RefTree-480K (480K verified samples, 3.72M reference images, up to 20 references per sample) and RefTree-Bench with tree-derived fine-grained visual rubrics.
kmfNwHyohD.key_idea: Recursively decompose a real target image into a concept tree, extract and verify leaves as reference images, and merge prompts bottom-up to form training samples.
kmfNwHyohD.evidence: Models fine-tuned on RefTree-480K are evaluated on four public benchmarks and RefTree-Bench, with data-source ablations and a comparison to human ratings (per reviewers).
kmfNwHyohD.claimed_gains: Reports the best open-weight performance across four public benchmarks and RefTree-Bench and matching Nano Banana Pro on two public benchmarks, without numeric scores in the available abstract.
kmfNwHyohD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the scalable data construction without closed models and the tree-based evaluation that traces which reference failed are valuable, and that the dataset is large and varied with strong open-model results.
kmfNwHyohD.main_concern: The contributions of the tree structure and of each agent are not disentangled by ablation, so gains may come from data volume, more references, or diversity rather than the tree design.

cRvwvthrBO.one_liner: Proves the VC dimension of margin contrastive learning is O(n/alpha^2) with a matching lower bound, removing a log factor
cRvwvthrBO.problem: Alon et al. (2024) left open whether their O(n log(n)/alpha^2) VC dimension bound for contrastive learning with a margin could be improved.
cRvwvthrBO.method: The paper proves that for any margin alpha in (0,1) the VC dimension of triplet contrastive learning with d-dimensional Euclidean embeddings is O(n/alpha^2), and gives a matching Omega(n/alpha^2) lower bound. Reviewers describe a Gaussian projection that turns the margin constraint into a one-dimensional weak classification advantage.
cRvwvthrBO.key_idea: Gaussian projection reduces each high-dimensional margin triplet constraint to a one-dimensional weak classification advantage, which removes the log n factor from the VC bound.
cRvwvthrBO.evidence: Theoretical proofs of matching upper and lower bounds; a reviewer notes the experiments only show one training method on random triplets.
cRvwvthrBO.claimed_gains: VC dimension O(n/alpha^2), improving the previous O(n log(n)/alpha^2) bound, with a matching Omega(n/alpha^2) lower bound.
cRvwvthrBO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it resolves a clearly posed open question with matching upper and lower bounds and a short, elegant proof.
cRvwvthrBO.main_concern: The improvement is only a log n factor in a triplet setting far from practice (many negatives, parameterized encoders), and the experiments do not test the worst-case theorem.

bm3NOmiwlx.one_liner: Proves curriculum learning that recursively decomposes long semiautomaton simulation into short blocks gives subpolynomial supervision complexity.
bm3NOmiwlx.problem: The theory of when and why decomposing a problem into parts yields more efficient learning than solving it directly is poorly understood.
bm3NOmiwlx.method: Studies learning to simulate semiautomata over T steps with a curriculum that recursively decomposes long sequences into shorter sub-problems, learns them and composes the solutions, in an SFT-inspired model (interactive intermediate-state feedback) and an RLVR-inspired model (verifier feedback), using multiscale boosting per reviews.
bm3NOmiwlx.key_idea: Recursively learn short-block predictors and compose them into longer ones, using boosting at each scale to prevent error accumulation, under interactive or verifier feedback.
bm3NOmiwlx.evidence: Theorems for semiautomaton simulation in an SFT-style and an RLVR-style feedback model, with experiments mentioned by reviewers.
bm3NOmiwlx.claimed_gains: In the SFT-style setting the curriculum learns from 2^(O~(sqrt(log T))) tokens of supervision, subpolynomial in T, versus the Omega(T) token barrier for direct simulation; the RLVR-style result is cut off in the abstract.
bm3NOmiwlx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives an interesting and substantial set of theoretical results on how compositional curricula improve dependence on computation length, with the RLVR result possibly relevant to LLM post-training.
bm3NOmiwlx.main_concern: The feedback models grant strong structure (oracle queries on intermediate states, uniform short-block coverage), so query complexity may not equal real supervision cost, and the presentation relies heavily on the appendix.

w54AHTqSLe.one_liner: Treats the denoiser at each noise scale as a self-map; memorization is the critical scale where an example's mode vanishes.
w54AHTqSLe.problem: Diffusion models are usually viewed as stochastic processes, leaving no geometric account of how duplication, overfitting and outliers produce memorization.
w54AHTqSLe.method: At each fixed noise scale sigma the denoiser is analyzed as a deterministic self-map whose fixed points are critical points of the smoothed data density and whose attractors are its modes; the critical scale sigma_c is the largest scale at which an example is retained, extended to image-caption pairs for conditional models.
w54AHTqSLe.key_idea: Memorized examples keep their own mode under stronger smoothing, so the largest noise scale at which a sample remains an attractor of the denoiser self-map measures memorization.
w54AHTqSLe.evidence: Theory for the exact empirical denoiser, controlled CIFAR-10 experiments on duplication, rarity and overfitting, and Stable Diffusion detection of memorized and partially memorized examples (70 MV, 24 TV and 94 control prompts per a review).
w54AHTqSLe.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says sigma_c tracks memorization and identifies memorized and partially memorized Stable Diffusion examples, with no numbers.
w54AHTqSLe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the fixed-scale dynamical-system and mean-shift view a clean, interesting framework with theory that is actually tested, supported by controlled experiments.
w54AHTqSLe.main_concern: Detection gains on Stable Diffusion are marginal (the best score does not beat a cheaper prompt-level baseline on the main task) on a small evaluation set, and novelty relative to prior early-denoising memorization work is not carefully positioned.

6egpMpGwZE.one_liner: LinQuant applies seven function-preserving transformations to linear-recurrence prefill so INT8 and INT4 quantization loses less accuracy.
6egpMpGwZE.problem: Low-precision inference for linear recurrences is far less developed than for softmax attention, and simply quantizing their chunkwise matrix multiplications in native form is fragile.
6egpMpGwZE.method: Identifies seven functional invariances (rotations, diagonal rescalings, alternative placements of recurrent decay and write factors) that preserve the full-precision computation, derives when they hold for linear, gated and delta-rule recurrences, and implements INT8 and INT4 kernels.
6egpMpGwZE.key_idea: Apply exact, output-preserving rotations, rescalings and decay or write-factor re-placements to recurrence operands so they quantize better without changing the full-precision result.
6egpMpGwZE.evidence: Evaluated on the recurrences of Nemotron-H, Qwen3.5 and Kimi Linear with INT8 and INT4 kernels, plus validity proofs, and per-invariance ablations including Mamba-2 models per reviews.
6egpMpGwZE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a rigorous, systematic characterization of which quantization-friendly invariances remain valid across recurrence families, backed by extensive numerical studies.
6egpMpGwZE.main_concern: Practical gains are small and come from components already known from QuaRot, SpinQuant and QServe (Hadamard rotation and rescaling), with evaluation limited to 2048-token prefill and little hybrid or runtime validation.

G7oo8Xl4y4.one_liner: Analyzes hitting time and optimization error of gradient descent with stochastic rounding on fixed-point grids for quadratic objectives.
G7oo8Xl4y4.problem: How gradient descent behaves when iterates are constrained to a fixed-point grid via stochastic rounding is not understood, and spectrum-based convergence analysis may not apply.
G7oo8Xl4y4.method: Proves bounds on the hitting time to a grid minimizer and on the optimization error for quadratics, comparing random-eigenbasis Hessians, diagonal and diagonally dominant Hessians, and rank-deficient Hessians.
G7oo8Xl4y4.key_idea: Hitting time depends on the Hessian's eigenbasis, not just its spectrum: random eigenbasis gives exponential-in-d hitting time, a diagonal Hessian with the same spectrum gives O(log d).
G7oo8Xl4y4.evidence: Purely theoretical proofs with matching bounds (an Omega(log d) lower bound for unique grid minimizers and an e^{O(d)} upper bound per reviews) and no numerical experiments.
G7oo8Xl4y4.claimed_gains: For a fixed spectrum, hitting time is e^{Omega(d)} for a random eigenbasis versus O(log d) for a diagonal Hessian, with optimization error of order Delta^2 d.
G7oo8Xl4y4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis is correct and tight, and that the separation between logarithmic and exponential hitting times for identical spectra is an interesting theoretical result.
G7oo8Xl4y4.main_concern: Relevance is unclear: the setting is limited to quadratics, hitting time may be a poor criterion since error can fall much earlier, and there are no numerical experiments.

xOhoguIa2K.one_liner: Local appearance purification aligns diffusion features to the residual of a pretrained encoder after removing locally predictable content.
xOhoguIa2K.problem: Choosing the encoder for representation alignment is empirical: DINOv2 gives substantial gains whereas MAE, despite retaining more reconstructive information, gives little benefit.
xOhoguIa2K.method: LAP removes locally predictable content from the alignment target and aligns to the residual, changing only the target with no change to diffusion training or inference, and is backed by a variational-bound interpretation and an exact constant-readout baseline.
xOhoguIa2K.key_idea: Align the denoiser's hidden state to the target minus its locally predictable component, so alignment emphasizes what information the target carries rather than how much.
xOhoguIa2K.evidence: Controlled interventions within a fixed encoder and ImageNet-256 experiments with SiT-B/2 across five pretrained representations, including compatibility with other alignment methods.
xOhoguIa2K.claimed_gains: On ImageNet-256 with SiT-B/2, LAP reduces FID from 53.1 to 42.3 for MAE, with gains across five pretrained representations and the largest for MAE.
xOhoguIa2K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-encoder analysis showing alignment value depends on what the target emphasizes is the strongest contribution, and the MAE gains come without added sampling cost.
xOhoguIa2K.main_concern: Gains are concentrated on weak targets such as MAE, while improvements for commonly used DINO teachers are small, within seed variation, or sometimes negative.

B7GLM1wPZR.one_liner: SHIFT: high-fidelity 3D CFD datasets (DDES and RANS) for external aerodynamics with in- and out-of-distribution splits.
B7GLM1wPZR.problem: Existing benchmarks combine high-fidelity 3D geometries, complex flow physics and engineering quantities poorly, limiting evaluation of geometry-aware neural surrogates in industrial settings.
B7GLM1wPZR.method: Provides thousands of simulations from transient Delayed Detached Eddy Simulations and steady RANS for external aerodynamics, built with domain experts and validated against experimental measurements, with predefined in-distribution and out-of-distribution sets and baseline results for neural operators (AB-UPT, DoMINO, Transolver, GeoTransolver).
B7GLM1wPZR.key_idea: Datasets pair industrial-partner-defined parametric geometries with high-fidelity DDES and solution-adaptive RANS simulations, split into in-distribution and out-of-distribution sets to test generalization to unseen geometries.
B7GLM1wPZR.evidence: About 4,000 samples per dataset with 30-46M-cell meshes for an SUV (DDES) and a wing (RANS), plus baseline evaluations of several neural operator models.
B7GLM1wPZR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark combines scale, 3D geometric variety and physical fidelity (DDES, solution-adaptive meshes, partial experimental validation) that few datasets offer.
B7GLM1wPZR.main_concern: Baselines report only in-distribution field errors with no OOD or drag/lift/moment results, and the paper does not adequately compare against related datasets such as DrivAerML, CarBench or SuperWing.

qkDfV8mPC2.one_liner: Benchmark plus RL-trained multimodal verifier that judges, explains and proposes edits for scientific image generation.
qkDfV8mPC2.problem: Verifying scientific images such as circuits, geometric constructions and function plots is hard, and existing verifiers target natural images and compress judgement into scalar scores without explainable feedback.
qkDfV8mPC2.method: SciGen-Verify is a benchmark with a three-tier protocol covering binary judgement, supporting explanation and corrective editing instruction. SciGen-Verifier is trained by cold-start supervised fine-tuning followed by a curriculum-based two-stage RL pipeline in which rubric-guided process rewards come before outcome rewards.
qkDfV8mPC2.key_idea: Train a verifier with cold-start SFT then two-stage curriculum RL, first rewarding rubric-covered reasoning and then outcome correctness, to output verdict, explanation and edit instruction.
qkDfV8mPC2.evidence: A benchmark spanning instruction following, multidisciplinary reasoning and world knowledge domains, with comparison against larger proprietary models and ablations of the training stages.
qkDfV8mPC2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find explainable verification of scientific images important and underexplored, value the combined judgement, explanation and editing-instruction output, and note the two-stage RL improves accuracy substantially.
qkDfV8mPC2.main_concern: The method mostly combines existing techniques (SFT, GRPO, rubric rewards), and the ablations, rubric-coverage reward and cascading editing metric do not isolate reasoning or editing ability.

sl18wlwHr6.one_liner: A unified benchmark of 18,000 samples for evaluating multimodal CAD program generation across modalities, complexity, and code quality.
sl18wlwHr6.problem: Progress in recovering CAD programs from images or 3D observations is hard to measure because evaluations are fragmented across datasets, modalities, and metrics.
sl18wlwHr6.method: CADBench has six benchmark families from DeepCAD, Fusion 360, ABC, MCB, and Objaverse, five input modalities, and metrics for geometric fidelity and code quality (executability, compactness, editability), stratified by B-rep face count. Eleven systems are benchmarked.
sl18wlwHr6.key_idea: Evaluate the same objects under several observation modalities with joint geometry and code-quality metrics, so rankings can be compared across inputs, complexity, and criteria.
sl18wlwHr6.evidence: Eleven CAD-specialized and general-purpose vision-language systems, generating more than 1.4 million CAD programs over 18,000 evaluation samples.
sl18wlwHr6.claimed_gains: Benchmark contribution only: 18,000 evaluation samples, eleven systems, and more than 1.4 million generated programs; no method gains are stated.
sl18wlwHr6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find CADBench fills a real gap with broad, well-presented coverage and editability metrics that reflect CAD practice.
sl18wlwHr6.main_concern: Metric and protocol gaps: complexity is tiered only by B-rep face count, edit-robustness details are unspecified, and low-executability outputs may bias other metrics.

l8tEyXhOG6.one_liner: Trains a question generator with RL whose difficulty reward is the answer entropy of a tool-using solver.
l8tEyXhOG6.problem: Challenging benchmarks need costly expert design and annotation, so they are hard to scale and update, while models risk training on similar static questions.
l8tEyXhOG6.method: Trains a generator that takes academic papers and outputs complex questions, with RL rewards including a difficulty reward from a solver model's answer distribution, where higher uncertainty means harder. The generator then builds U2-Bench with three 500-question tracks.
l8tEyXhOG6.key_idea: Use the entropy of a strong solver's sampled answer distribution as an RL reward so the generator learns to write questions the solver finds uncertain.
l8tEyXhOG6.evidence: U2-Bench with three 500-question tracks (reviewers name Fact500 and Calc500), a source-blind audit of all Fact500 questions, human review, and U2-Train results for a trained solver.
l8tEyXhOG6.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically in the available abstract, which is cut off after describing the three 500-question tracks.
l8tEyXhOG6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the RL formulation with an entropy-based difficulty signal practical and scalable, and value the audits, including the Fact500 ambiguity audit, that check benchmark quality.
l8tEyXhOG6.main_concern: Difficulty depends on a proprietary oracle (GPT-5.5) that is also evaluated on the benchmark, and scores rely on model judges without calibration against human ratings.

GkKJzkfTgQ.one_liner: Synthetic data picks a direction for a directional test, combined with a base test under a total type-I error budget.
GkKJzkfTgQ.problem: In composite hypothesis testing, alternatives can depart from the null in multiple directions so no uniformly most powerful test may exist, and synthetic data could add power but must not break validity.
GkKJzkfTgQ.method: SPDT uses synthetic data to identify a plausible direction in which to concentrate power, then combines a directional test with an existing base test, inheriting validity from the component tests within a prespecified total type-I error budget.
GkKJzkfTgQ.key_idea: Synthetic data only chooses where to concentrate power; a directional test on real data is OR-combined with the base test, so validity never depends on synthetic data.
GkKJzkfTgQ.evidence: Simulations (including Gaussian mean testing) and applications in LLM safety and treatment effect heterogeneity detection.
GkKJzkfTgQ.claimed_gains: Substantial power gains when the chosen direction is informative while retaining base power when it is misleading; no numbers stated.
GkKJzkfTgQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is simple, broadly applicable, and easy to implement, with transparent validity guarantees that do not require the synthetic and real distributions to match.
GkKJzkfTgQ.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited since the guarantees follow from the union bound and the OR combination of existing tests, and experiments do not isolate the benefit of learning directions from synthetic data.

xfUuHllNd9.one_liner: Scales empowerment maximization by reaching states that start many skills, using any underlying skill learning method.
xfUuHllNd9.problem: Empowerment, an agent's capacity to control its environment, has mostly been studied in tabular settings, so its theoretically predicted properties have been empirically elusive at scale.
xfUuHllNd9.method: The authors explain the connection between skill learning and empowerment and give a recipe in which empowerment corresponds to the number of executable skills from a state, so maximizing it means reaching states that are good starting points for many skills. The recipe applies to arbitrary underlying skill learning methods.
xfUuHllNd9.key_idea: Treats empowerment as the number of skills executable from a state and maximizes it by steering the agent to states that are good starting points for many learned skills.
xfUuHllNd9.evidence: Experiments in Crafter/Craftax-Classic and Ant continuous-control tasks (per reviews), with emergent properties such as information gathering, survival, homeostasis, and house building.
xfUuHllNd9.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports emergent behaviors such as building a house in Crafter, with no numeric results).
xfUuHllNd9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is timely and the link between skill learning and empowerment is clearly described, with a recipe that scales empowerment beyond toy settings.
xfUuHllNd9.main_concern: Evidence for the headline emergent behaviors is thin: no external baselines (e.g., RND, METRA) in the largest Craftax environment, and the behaviors are shown from a few frames and a single seed and episode.

Lp8CoFiT2L.one_liner: Adversarial image perturbation that collapses reference value-vector diversity and attracts later frames to it, degrading image-to-video diffusion outputs.
Lp8CoFiT2L.problem: Image-to-video diffusion models can animate a personal photo without consent, and existing adversarial protections struggle under common perturbation budgets because the mechanism by which later frames read the reference image is poorly understood.
Lp8CoFiT2L.method: LETHE pairs a value collapse objective that drives the reference value vectors toward uniformity with an attention attraction objective that draws subsequent frames toward the collapsed tokens, amplifying corruption. A convex geometric analysis identifies the spread of reference value vectors as the factor governing the reading process.
Lp8CoFiT2L.key_idea: Contracts the spread of the reference image's value vectors and pulls later frames' attention to the collapsed tokens, so generated videos lose faithfulness to the image.
Lp8CoFiT2L.evidence: Experiments across different I2V models and datasets against existing protections (I2VGuard, Anti-Prompt) at an l-infinity budget of 16/255, plus mechanism and robustness studies (per reviews).
Lp8CoFiT2L.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; reviews report it outperforms I2VGuard and Anti-Prompt across I2V models and datasets.
Lp8CoFiT2L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and the method is well motivated by a theoretical analysis of the reading mechanism, with consistently stronger protection than existing methods across I2V models and datasets.
Lp8CoFiT2L.main_concern: There is no quantitative evaluation of how visible the perturbation is (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS), generation is costly at about 7-8 minutes per image on an H100, and the per-attention theory does not cover the full generation pipeline.

6W54LGr4yM.one_liner: Attention heads at feature words build spatial feature maps in VLMs; their capacity limit explains conjunctive search failure.
6W54LGr4yM.problem: VLMs fail at conjunctive search, a signature of the binding problem, and it is unclear how the feature representations supplied to spatial retrieval mechanisms are constructed.
6W54LGr4yM.method: By intervening on VLM internal activations, they find that attention heads at the color word and the shape word of the question build maps of where each feature appears in the image. Patching these maps between displays makes the model attach a feature to the wrong object.
6W54LGr4yM.key_idea: While reading the question, attention heads at the color and shape tokens write per-feature spatial maps, and patching or ablating those maps causes illusory conjunctions and degraded search.
6W54LGr4yM.evidence: Activation patching and ablation on conjunctive search displays, with illusory conjunctions growing as objects get closer, and counting tasks; reviews note results are on a single model (Qwen).
6W54LGr4yM.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says supplying clean feature maps can significantly recover search accuracy, without numbers.
6W54LGr4yM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mechanistic study carefully designed, with complementary experiments that disentangle competing hypotheses, and clearly presented.
6W54LGr4yM.main_concern: Results are limited to a single model (Qwen), and the feature-map interpretation rests mainly on patching rather than a direct representation analysis.

MzpyquVCS7.one_liner: Minuet learns cross-donor RNA-ATAC representations by combining within-donor contrastive learning, shared prediction, and group-conditional donor penalties
MzpyquVCS7.problem: Contrastive loss on paired multiome data does not ensure donor-transferable representations: negatives from all donors reward donor-identifying features, within-donor negatives let each donor's representation rotate freely, and removing donor information discards phenotype.
MzpyquVCS7.method: Minuet combines within-donor contrastive learning, a prediction task shared across donors, and a donor penalty applied within groups of donors that share biological covariates. It shows these objectives determine the representation up to one shift for each group of donors connected by shared covariates.
MzpyquVCS7.key_idea: Remove donor-specific freedom with a shared prediction target and within-donor contrast, and penalize donor information only among donors that share biological covariates.
MzpyquVCS7.evidence: Six paired cohorts compared with nine methods on integration, cross-donor and cross-dataset transfer, and phenotype prediction, plus synthetic experiments over twenty seeds and ablations.
MzpyquVCS7.claimed_gains: Best average rank among nine methods in integration, cross-donor and cross-dataset transfer, and phenotype prediction across six paired cohorts.
MzpyquVCS7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a clear, technically substantive diagnosis of donor shortcuts and a carefully designed evaluation protocol with synthetic tests of the mechanisms.
MzpyquVCS7.main_concern: The theory is conditional (full-column-rank prediction head, PCA-based target) and does not guarantee biological recovery, and the writing is very dense.

bMEfHC2ob5.one_liner: Color-equivariant graph neural network that builds graph colorings sequentially so earlier assignments break node symmetries.
bMEfHC2ob5.problem: Learning-based graph coloring must exploit invariance to color permutations while still breaking symmetries between nodes, such as adjacent nodes in the same automorphism orbit.
bMEfHC2ob5.method: Scone uses a color-equivariant GNN to construct colorings sequentially, letting information from previous assignments propagate to break node symmetries. According to the reviews, decoding also uses node-selection rules, forced-assignment propagation, and beam search.
bMEfHC2ob5.key_idea: Make the GNN equivariant to color permutations to shrink the effective state space, and break node symmetries by feeding earlier color assignments back during sequential construction.
bMEfHC2ob5.evidence: Several graph coloring tasks including sudoku_extreme and register allocations, with generalization to graph families not seen in training, compared against non-equivariant models, color-permutation augmentation, and classical solvers.
bMEfHC2ob5.claimed_gains: Reports perfect solution quality with low inference times across several graph coloring tasks, including sudoku_extreme and register allocations; no numbers stated.
bMEfHC2ob5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the color-equivariant, sequential design is well motivated by the structure of graph coloring and is supported by comparisons with non-equivariant models and augmentation.
bMEfHC2ob5.main_concern: Gains are hard to attribute to the learned model because decoding adds classical solver components, and closely related methods such as GDN and ReLCol are not directly compared.

OAen4KgX4Q.one_liner: Shows VLM reward judges separate successes from gross failures but not near-misses, using boundary-bisected perturbations in LIBERO.
OAen4KgX4Q.problem: VLM reward models for robot manipulation are evaluated mostly on obvious failures such as dropped objects, yet are applied to competent policies whose rollouts nearly all end close to success.
OAen4KgX4Q.method: For each simulated task, finds how far the object can be moved before the task no longer counts as complete, then creates failures just past that limit (near-misses) and far beyond it (gross failures). Thirteen judges are tested on four LIBERO suites, with OpenVLA-generated failures, perturbed-success controls, and a blinded human study.
OAen4KgX4Q.key_idea: Make closeness to success a controlled variable by bisecting for each task's completion boundary and placing failures just past it versus far beyond it.
OAen4KgX4Q.evidence: Thirteen judges on four LIBERO suites, failures made by OpenVLA itself, a blinded human study on judge frames, and a best-of-three selection analysis.
OAen4KgX4Q.claimed_gains: Near-misses erase on average 30-61% of a judge's best-of-three advantage over picking at random, depending on the suite (the TL;DR states 24-62%).
OAen4KgX4Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clearly motivated and that the boundary-based perturbation design, with simulator-verified labels and perturbed-success controls, is sound.
OAen4KgX4Q.main_concern: Task coverage is narrow (subsets of LIBERO tasks, simulation only, one camera), and near-miss labels defined by a latent completion threshold are not validated against human labels or shown to be visually perceivable.

6v4Si7sR7o.one_liner: Task-trained RNN learns content-independent rank subspaces, a reusable ordinal schema, aligned with input and output weights by stage.
6v4Si7sR7o.problem: It is unclear how the factorized ordinal geometry seen in macaque prefrontal cortex emerges in recurrent networks and how it is dynamically deployed across encoding, maintenance, and retrieval.
6v4Si7sR7o.method: Trains an RNN on sequence working memory tasks and analyzes its dynamics: content-independent rank subspaces hold stimulus-specific representations, the relevant rank subspace aligns with fixed input weights during encoding and output weights during retrieval, and activity stays marginally stable during maintenance.
6v4Si7sR7o.key_idea: Rank-specific subspaces align with the input weight space during encoding and the output weight space during retrieval, while previously encoded subspaces keep evolving in a structured way.
6v4Si7sR7o.evidence: Per the reviews, a 400-unit RNN with six stimulus identities; the abstract adds generalization across tested sequence lengths and perturbations in a richer stroke-based task.
6v4Si7sR7o.claimed_gains: not stated; this is a mechanistic analysis with no numeric results in the abstract.
6v4Si7sR7o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analyses of RNN dynamics are comprehensive and give an interpretable link between task-trained recurrent networks and macaque prefrontal findings, with additional tasks testing generality.
6v4Si7sR7o.main_concern: Generality and novelty are doubtful: results rest on a small 400-unit RNN with task durations very short relative to the neuron time constant, orthogonal subspaces appeared in prior work, and schema is not clearly defined.

rohURXLtVo.one_liner: Compresses each base kernel by symmetric randomization, then fuses kernels in a shared low-dimensional subspace for multiple kernel clustering.
rohURXLtVo.problem: Multiple kernel clustering needs storage and spectral decomposition of several n x n kernel matrices, which limits large-scale use.
rohURXLtVo.method: Each base kernel is compressed into a low-dimensional core space, and a shared subspace captures consensus spectral structure so kernel fusion and weight learning happen in a common representation space.
rohURXLtVo.key_idea: Run kernel fusion and spectral optimization on randomized low-dimensional compressions of each kernel, aligned through a shared subspace.
rohURXLtVo.evidence: A reconstruction-error bound per compressed kernel, analysis of the shared subspace, and experiments on eight multi-view benchmark datasets.
rohURXLtVo.claimed_gains: Significant improvements in clustering performance on eight multi-view benchmark datasets; the abstract is cut off and gives no numbers.
rohURXLtVo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the compression clearly cuts computation and keeps clustering performance, with reported speedups over SimpleMKKM on eight datasets.
rohURXLtVo.main_concern: The method leans on existing randomized SVD and spectral projection, theory gives no guarantees on clustering results or kernel weights, and comparison with other kernel-reduction methods is thin.

uYVLkvGOSL.one_liner: Randomizes the corruption rate itself in randomized smoothing, mixing light and heavy perturbations, to certify LLM defenses at larger radii.
uYVLkvGOSL.problem: Fixed-rate masking or deletion in randomized smoothing caps the certifiable radius at a ceiling growing at most logarithmically with the sampling budget, so LLM jailbreak certification covers only a few token modifications.
uYVLkvGOSL.method: The corruption rate is drawn from a distribution (a Beta distribution per reviews) that preserves the expected rate, which raises the probability of removing several attack-related tokens together. They show this can cut sampling requirements for certification from exponential to polynomial in the target radius.
uYVLkvGOSL.key_idea: Sample a shared random corruption rate per smoothed input so multiple adversarial tokens are removed jointly with higher probability than under a fixed rate.
uYVLkvGOSL.evidence: LLM-based harmful-content detection experiments measuring certified suffix lengths at the same sampling budget, plus full-input attack settings (per reviews), with certificate proofs for masking and deletion.
uYVLkvGOSL.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims substantially larger certified suffix lengths at the same sampling budget and sampling requirements reduced from exponential to polynomial in the target radius.
uYVLkvGOSL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-rate bottleneck is a clearly identified limitation and the shared-rate fix has a simple, interpretable justification with consistent certificate derivations.
uYVLkvGOSL.main_concern: Large gains appear mainly in the protected-suffix setting and nearly vanish on full-input attacks, and benign utility is not measured for the final thresholded smoothed detector.

Ik6xke4qH5.one_liner: Releases a Gaussian-noised pairwise distance matrix, optionally repaired to the nearest metric, for private downstream metric learning.
Ik6xke4qH5.problem: Private learning from metrics available only as pairwise distance matrices in general metric spaces lacks a simple, reusable release mechanism under the rho-distance-based DP model.
Ik6xke4qH5.method: Independent Gaussian noise is added to the pairwise distance entries, the matrix is optionally repaired to the nearest metric, and the single privatized matrix is released and reused for minimum spanning trees, k-clustering, hierarchical clustering and coresets.
Ik6xke4qH5.key_idea: Input perturbation: add independent Gaussian noise to every pairwise distance entry so one privatized matrix serves many downstream metric tasks.
Ik6xke4qH5.evidence: Proofs of nearly tight bounds and downstream applications, plus experiments on 12 datasets against existing benchmarks.
Ik6xke4qH5.claimed_gains: Nearly tight additive error of order rho sqrt(n log(1/delta))/epsilon for (epsilon, delta)-DP metric release, with bounds for MST, k-clustering, hierarchical clustering and coresets that are tight or match the state of the art, and experiments on 12 datasets.
Ik6xke4qH5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a clearly written paper giving a simple, nearly optimal mechanism with broad downstream applications.
Ik6xke4qH5.main_concern: The error scales as sqrt(n) and some downstream uses are inefficient, so reviewers question scalability and whether the problem formulation is well posed; upper-bound technical depth is modest.

sTlt5H7zZp.one_liner: A single initialization-time quantity, slowest bank frequency times hidden pre-activation standard deviation, predicts whether sinusoidal neural fields collapse.
sTlt5H7zZp.problem: Sinusoidal neural fields with randomly drawn frequency banks either fit the target or collapse to its mean colour, and the outcome changes from one random draw to the next.
sTlt5H7zZp.method: Defines the phase scale of a hidden layer as the slowest frequency of the layer's bank times the standard deviation of the layer's input, takes kappa as the largest phase scale over hidden layers, and computes it from one forward pass at initialization without the target.
sTlt5H7zZp.key_idea: The hidden-layer phase scale kappa, the largest product of slowest bank frequency and layer input standard deviation, separates trainable from collapsing sinusoidal networks, with cutoffs fixed in advance.
sTlt5H7zZp.evidence: 300 runs on three CelebA images and, with cutoffs fixed in advance, 120 networks on three Kodak-24 images, plus layer-scaling interventions and a correlation-map analysis of a random sinusoidal layer.
sTlt5H7zZp.claimed_gains: On CelebA, all 181 runs below kappa = 1.81 train and none of the 51 runs above 4.0 trains; on Kodak-24, all 60 networks below 1.81 train and all 60 above 4.0 collapse.
sTlt5H7zZp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem relevant and some interventions clean, notably rescaling the first layer versus the hidden layers, which shows the failure comes from the hidden layers.
sTlt5H7zZp.main_concern: The study reads as ad hoc, the theory explains the form of kappa but not the threshold location or why runs collapse, and thresholds must be measured separately for each bank family.

MV1U3w5VXL.one_liner: Split federated learning exchanging smashed data and gradients once per round, with curvature-based correction for stale client gradients.
MV1U3w5VXL.problem: Auxiliary-network SFL makes the client optimize a local objective that differs from the end-to-end objective, limiting client-server collaboration, while vanilla SFL communicates every batch.
MV1U3w5VXL.method: CoeF-SFL keeps the end-to-end objective without an auxiliary network, exchanging once per round and reusing the data locally. It compensates stale gradients with a curvature correction in activation space: CoeF-D uses a diagonal gradient outer-product Hessian, CoeF-J a Jacobian-based Hessian of a surrogate upper-bound loss.
MV1U3w5VXL.key_idea: Compensate stale cut-layer gradients with a Gauss-Newton-style curvature correction in activation space instead of training an auxiliary network.
MV1U3w5VXL.evidence: Experiments against auxiliary-based SFL methods, including a perfect-compensation oracle per reviews; the abstract is truncated before results.
MV1U3w5VXL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated, the oracle comparison informative, and the compensation effective at recovering performance lost to uncompensated gradient reuse.
MV1U3w5VXL.main_concern: The advance over prior stale-gradient compensation (DC-ASGD, CELU-VFL) is unclear, and communication savings are not demonstrated end to end.

EB8U0IjPId.one_liner: Task-Environment-Agents representation coupling an agent interaction graph with a task activity graph and the environment to track LLM collaboration.
EB8U0IjPId.problem: Less structured LLM agent collaboration is less reliable and harder to understand, and agents may deviate from predefined workflows, making each agent's contribution hard to trace.
EB8U0IjPId.method: TEA couples an Agent Interaction Graph to a Task Activity Graph and the environment to form a collaboration state, without prescribing agent reasoning, behavior or communication order. It also serves as an active framework through which agents communicate, transform tasks and act.
EB8U0IjPId.key_idea: Link agent interactions to persistent, versioned task nodes and environment outcomes in one graph-based collaboration state.
EB8U0IjPId.evidence: Recovery of emergent collaboration structures, analysis of collaboration states, and a four-condition ablation of task-graph access per reviews.
EB8U0IjPId.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see practical value in tracing task progress to agent interactions through persistent task identities, version histories and evidence links.
EB8U0IjPId.main_concern: The evaluation lacks comparison against simpler shared task lists, blackboards or existing multi-agent frameworks, so TEA's added value is unclear.

edizlUgYc8.one_liner: Reweights the latent-generation loss per latent dimension by each dimension's impact on graph reconstruction.
edizlUgYc8.problem: Latent graph generation lags discrete diffusion because a few latent units dominate graph reconstruction, yet the loss weights all latent dimensions equally.
edizlUgYc8.method: The method measures how much each latent unit affects graph reconstruction and applies dimension-wise importance weights to the existing latent training loss, leaving the generative architecture unchanged and adding no inference parameters (as described by reviewers; the abstract is truncated before the method details).
edizlUgYc8.key_idea: Weight each latent dimension's loss by its measured influence on graph reconstruction instead of treating all dimensions equally.
edizlUgYc8.evidence: Experiments on graph benchmarks such as SBM, planar, tree, and molecular datasets (GuacaMol, MOSES, with LG-Flow for molecules) per reviewers; the abstract text is cut off before results.
edizlUgYc8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, clear, and focused, a dimension-wise loss reweighting that needs no architecture change and shows clear convergence benefits.
edizlUgYc8.main_concern: Reviewers say evidence is limited: molecular results cover only LG-Flow, gains depend on backbone, metric, and sampling budget with trade-offs, benefits on structured molecular datasets are small, and the importance measure is tested with a single cutoff and embedding model.

dmxUPwR9YV.one_liner: Graph anomaly detection that abstracts nodes and edges into two discrete role codebooks and passes messages over a role-induced graph.
dmxUPwR9YV.problem: Graph anomalies arise from heterogeneous mechanisms and stay fragmented, unlike node-classification classes, so recurring normal patterns need a compact summary while anomalies stay distinguishable.
dmxUPwR9YV.method: Role-GAD abstracts node semantics and edge interactions into dual discrete role codebooks via vector quantization, then runs role-aware message passing over a role-induced graph augmented with global role-triplet statistics.
dmxUPwR9YV.key_idea: Quantize node semantics and edge interactions into discrete roles so recurring normal patterns share roles while anomalies show up as rare role assignments and atypical role interactions.
dmxUPwR9YV.evidence: Five real-world GAD benchmarks, component ablations on three datasets, and efficiency comparisons, plus empirical analyses of feature-space distances and node homophily that motivate the design.
dmxUPwR9YV.claimed_gains: Role-GAD achieves the best average performance on five real-world benchmarks while converging up to 10× faster than the strongest accuracy-oriented baseline.
dmxUPwR9YV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dual-codebook role design is clear, interpretable, and efficient (linear in edges), with empirical analyses supporting the heterogeneity motivation and encouraging results across five benchmarks.
dmxUPwR9YV.main_concern: Reviewers say the motivating kNN-distance and homophily analyses may be confounded by class imbalance, the heterogeneity motivation is not new, and ablations show interaction roles alone nearly match the dual-role model.

iqPj9BbGLc.one_liner: Parallelizes nonlinear test-time-training layers by iteratively refining hidden-layer gradient trajectories with chunkwise-parallel passes.
iqPj9BbGLc.problem: Nonlinear TTT layers such as TTT-MLP are more expressive than linear memories but rely on sequential block-wise weight updates that run several times slower and only approximate token-by-token online updates.
iqPj9BbGLc.method: ParaTTT starts from a guess of the hidden-layer gradients, then each refinement runs three chunkwise-parallel passes: a forward feature pass, an exact gated-delta-rule pass for the readout and its feature gradients, and a backward pass producing a new gradient estimate. The fixed point is the exact online gradient descent recurrence, and decoding needs no refinement iterations.
iqPj9BbGLc.key_idea: Iterate on O(d) hidden-layer gradient estimates instead of O(d^2) fast weights, so each pass becomes a chunkwise linear scan that reuses gated-delta-rule kernels.
iqPj9BbGLc.evidence: A geometric-convergence proof for a two-layer nonlinear memory under contraction conditions, plus language-model experiments (reviews cite 1.3B models, SWDE, LAMBADA, NIAH) against Gated DeltaNet and LaCT.
iqPj9BbGLc.claimed_gains: States that two refinement iterations suffice in practice; no speedup or accuracy numbers appear in the available abstract.
iqPj9BbGLc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that iterating on hidden-layer gradients rather than weights is a good idea that reuses existing chunkwise kernels, and that the reported speedups and two-iteration result are encouraging.
iqPj9BbGLc.main_concern: More refinement iterations, which move closer to the exact recurrence, make results worse, so the exact-parallelization framing is overstated and the quality gain over simpler linear models like Gated DeltaNet is unclear.

HNO16jOXiU.one_liner: Fail-safe consensus over label hierarchies: output the deepest label-tree node held by more than (M+f)/2 sources.
HNO16jOXiU.problem: Coordinated source failures can flip a majority vote, yet corrupted sources often still agree on a label's ancestors, so a safe output must not claim more than the honest majority supports.
HNO16jOXiU.method: They define f-safe outputs, show that backing off to an ancestor with mean probability at least theta is f-safe exactly when theta exceeds 1/2 + f/(2M), and prove the finest safe rule is the deepest subtree holding more than (M+f)/2 reports, with certifiable depth and accuracy losses.
HNO16jOXiU.key_idea: Define safety against any f corrupted sources relative to the honest majority, then return the deepest label-tree node reported by more than (M+f)/2 sources.
HNO16jOXiU.evidence: Optimality is proved over set-valued and stream-aware rules, with experiments on four datasets (human labels included) using ten sources.
HNO16jOXiU.claimed_gains: Calibration to 95% coverage crosses the safety threshold on all four datasets, and calibrated backing off has 1.2 to 2.7 times the finest safe rule's worst-case error for two or three of ten corrupted sources.
HNO16jOXiU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the honest-majority safety notion is well chosen and the results are correct and clearly answer how much specificity survives corruption.
HNO16jOXiU.main_concern: Novelty is narrow: the rule is majority-rule consensus with a Byzantine-quorum threshold and the proofs are standard counting arguments, which the abstract does not acknowledge.

Lpxn7lc6Dz.one_liner: Shows self-play against reference-free LLM judges makes errors more convincing, and that a candidate-independent committed answer fixes it.
Lpxn7lc6Dz.problem: Self-reward and LLM-judge pipelines assume a reference-free judge's verdict on a shown answer proxies correctness, but conditioned on a candidate the judge scores plausibility.
Lpxn7lc6Dz.method: They measure the failure with a hidden-anchor audit (a held-out exact-match check the judge never sees) in GSM8K self-play, and propose that the judge commit its own answer independently of the candidate and accept only on a match.
Lpxn7lc6Dz.key_idea: Have the judge commit to its own answer independently of the candidate and accept only on a match, removing candidate-driven plausibility as the reward signal.
Lpxn7lc6Dz.evidence: GSM8K with Qwen3 policies in a reasoning-suppressed regime, transfer across Qwen, Llama and Gemma families and larger judges, ensemble judges, and a randomized-exposure test.
Lpxn7lc6Dz.claimed_gains: Self-play drives the judge's pass rate from 0.72 to 0.94 while true accuracy stays at 0.20 (a failure measurement; the fix's numbers are cut off).
Lpxn7lc6Dz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hidden-anchor measurement and randomized-exposure test are clear, well-controlled designs showing that candidate exposure drives the judge's inflated scores.
Lpxn7lc6Dz.main_concern: The headline comparison confounds anchoring with judge inference budget (256-token thinking-off versus 1,536-token thinking-on), so the false-positive basin may reflect an under-resourced judge.

Lh3RZCUS5W.one_liner: Extends Shapley attribution to probabilistic time-series forecasts by computing distributions of input contributions from the model's native probabilistic output.
Lh3RZCUS5W.problem: Scalar attribution methods explain a single summary such as the mean, which can hide inputs that change the predicted variance or shape of a forecast without changing the mean.
Lh3RZCUS5W.method: TDV is a model-agnostic method that computes distributions of input contributions directly from a model's quantiles or sampled trajectories, using paired output differences across input orders with shared randomness.
Lh3RZCUS5W.key_idea: Keep contribution distributions built from paired forecast differences across input orders with shared randomness, so they reconstruct the forecast distribution and their mean recovers scalar Shapley values.
Lh3RZCUS5W.evidence: Four forecasting models evaluated on long-term glucose, meal, and activity data including type 1 diabetes, with numerical checks that forecasts are reconstructed and scalar Shapley values recovered on average.
Lh3RZCUS5W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explaining probabilistic forecasts is a relevant problem and that the formulation is carefully developed and sound, with a clear treatment of marginal quantiles versus joint trajectories.
Lh3RZCUS5W.main_concern: Novelty is incremental, since the core construction follows Distributional Values (Franceschi et al., 2024) and most propositions restate existing results in the forecasting setting.

AcdNDic47i.one_liner: Gradually hands control from a conservative batch policy to a faster online learner using backwards expansion and off-policy estimation.
AcdNDic47i.problem: In offline-to-online RL, agents often degrade early in fine-tuning, and methods that avoid degradation can learn too slowly while faster methods do not control degradation enough.
AcdNDic47i.method: COE combines a conservative batch algorithm with a faster-learning online algorithm, using off-policy estimation to decide when to gradually hand off control. Theory supports the backwards expansion approach and the policy evaluation used to decide the hand-off.
AcdNDic47i.key_idea: Start trajectories with the conservative policy and expand the online policy's share backwards, with off-policy value estimates deciding when each hand-off is safe.
AcdNDic47i.evidence: Comparisons against several batch and offline-to-online algorithms, theory for backwards expansion and policy evaluation, and ablations of each design decision, with degradation measured by metrics such as Mean-FP and VaR-MPD.
AcdNDic47i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm is intuitive and well presented, with theory that motivates its gradual hand-off and thorough experiments and ablations against multiple baselines.
AcdNDic47i.main_concern: The mid-trajectory hand-off heuristic and its many tuned hyperparameters are not well justified, and the theory does not fully explain the method's claims.

R1DJlJnB1W.one_liner: Represents each visual part as the exact diagonal 2-Wasserstein barycenter of patch Gaussians, keeping both mean and learned scale.
R1DJlJnB1W.problem: Part-based retrieval methods summarize each part with a single mean vector, discarding distributional structure that matters when sensor, viewpoint, or modality changes wash out texture and colour.
R1DJlJnB1W.method: WBPRIOR is a lightweight plug-and-play head in which each patch predicts a mean vector and a positive variance defining a diagonal Gaussian, and each part is the 2-Wasserstein barycenter of its assigned Gaussians. This barycenter has an exact closed form, so each part keeps a mean and a learned scale vector at negligible cost.
R1DJlJnB1W.key_idea: Aggregate patch-level diagonal Gaussians into parts with the closed-form 2-Wasserstein barycenter instead of a mean, so each part retains a learned scale vector.
R1DJlJnB1W.evidence: A controlled matched study that changes only the aggregation rule, robustness gains for seven published cross-view retrievers, and standalone results on drone geo-localisation with transfer to sketch retrieval and aerial-ground person re-identification.
R1DJlJnB1W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-form barycenter adds a second-order signal beyond mean pooling at negligible cost, with competitive results across geo-localization, sketch retrieval, and person re-identification and thorough ablations.
R1DJlJnB1W.main_concern: The plug-and-play claim requires retraining host models, which costs 3 to 7 points of clean accuracy versus the tuned originals and may inflate the robustness gains.

CcitTPWccW.one_liner: Re-encodes frozen CLIP visual tokens with a single frozen LLM decoder layer, without text, to detect generated images.
CcitTPWccW.problem: CLIP features generalize across generators but come from global image-text alignment and model semantic relations among image regions and structural consistency poorly, which matters as generators suppress low-level artifacts.
CcitTPWccW.method: Treats one frozen pretrained LLM decoder layer as a semantic relation enhancement module for CLIP visual tokens, with no language prompts or text inputs. CLIP and the LLM stay frozen and only about 4.3M parameters are trained.
CcitTPWccW.key_idea: Pass CLIP patch tokens through one frozen pretrained LLM decoder layer so they are re-encoded within relational structure learned from language, then train only about 4.3M parameters.
CcitTPWccW.evidence: Training on a single generator and testing on 13 GAN and diffusion generators plus recent diffusion and autoregressive generators, with ablations against linear probing, a capacity-matched MLP, class-token-only processing, and random initialization.
CcitTPWccW.claimed_gains: Reaches 91.55% accuracy and 99.38% average precision across 13 GAN and diffusion generators, 3.05 accuracy points above the strongest prior detector, and 98.43% accuracy on recently released diffusion and autoregressive generators.
CcitTPWccW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and light, with frozen backbones and about 4.3M trainable parameters, and shows strong cross-generator generalization with informative controlled ablations.
CcitTPWccW.main_concern: It is not shown that the gains come from language-pretrained relational knowledge rather than any pretrained block, and the idea closely follows Pang et al. (2024).

LL6AvwMYXi.one_liner: Inference-only cascade allocating pairwise-verifier compute adaptively by how much of each candidate the judge reads and which pairs are compared.
LL6AvwMYXi.problem: Pairwise self-verification is the strongest aggregation for parallel reasoning but is costly, since each judgment reads two full solutions and existing methods run tens of judgments per problem regardless of whether the comparison is informative.
LL6AvwMYXi.method: CAPS allocates verifier compute non-uniformly along an evidence axis (how much of each candidate the judge sees) and a distribution axis (how comparisons are spread across the pool), as a four-stage cascade with an optional rescue subroutine. Its verifier-token cost has a closed form, with per-candidate marginal cost roughly halved versus uniform full-evidence schedules.
LL6AvwMYXi.key_idea: Filter candidates with cheap partial-evidence comparisons, such as the first and last parts of the reasoning, and reserve full-evidence pairwise comparisons for stronger candidates.
LL6AvwMYXi.evidence: Four self-verifying models (Qwen3-14B, GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3-4B-Instruct/Thinking) on five benchmarks: LiveCodeBench-v5/v6, CodeContests, AIME 2025, and HMMT 2025.
LL6AvwMYXi.claimed_gains: CAPS outperforms the leading pairwise verifier on 14 of 20 suites while using 25.4% of its verifier-token budget on code.
LL6AvwMYXi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that not every candidate deserves full verification, and that a cascade using cheap partial evidence for early filtering is intuitive and supported by fairly comprehensive ablations.
LL6AvwMYXi.main_concern: Gains over the strongest pairwise verifier are modest and inconsistent, most savings come from fewer comparisons, and simple baselines and end-to-end compute comparisons are missing.

j67A3wz3Rd.one_liner: Load-aware dropout for full fine-tuning that masks the currently most-loaded MLP neurons and attention heads at every update.
j67A3wz3Rd.problem: Fine-tuning dense language models concentrates loss-relevant computation in a small subset of attention heads, MLP neurons, and residual-stream dimensions, and this path-load imbalance predicts poorer retention of previously correct answers.
j67A3wz3Rd.method: PathBalance measures the current load (activation strength, gradient pressure, and activation-gradient attribution) before every update and masks the top-2% hot units while the rest of the network is trained with cross-entropy. It does not change the inference architecture.
j67A3wz3Rd.key_idea: Before each update, compute activation-gradient attribution load per unit and mask the most loaded units, pushing computation onto previously cold units.
j67A3wz3Rd.evidence: Three math benchmarks and five Qwen3/Qwen3.5 models, with load diagnostics on Intermediate Algebra, a random-masking control, and a matched-epoch attribution analysis.
j67A3wz3Rd.claimed_gains: Improves over SFT by up to 16 percentage points on GSM8K and 50 on MATH across three math benchmarks and five Qwen3/Qwen3.5 models.
j67A3wz3Rd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostic and intervention experiments give useful evidence that a few hot units carry the load, and that the masking method is a simple, practical training intervention.
j67A3wz3Rd.main_concern: The unusually large gains need a stronger SFT baseline and the initial model's accuracy as reference, and all major experiments use a single training seed.

hPoiz4zaEh.one_liner: Replaces a tabular generator's Gaussian latent prior with the homogeneous CLWE distribution to embed a keyed watermark with certified p-values.
hPoiz4zaEh.problem: Tabular generative models can fabricate or impute scientific datasets and evade forensics, since no statistical test on outputs alone can expose a well-trained generator.
hPoiz4zaEh.method: Tabular Pancakes is a training-free watermark whose latent prior is Gaussian except in a secret subspace where it is periodic (homogeneous CLWE). With the key, an auditor recovers the mark from a small fraction of released rows with a certified p-value, and row-level tests localize synthetic rows. The mark can also be embedded directly in released rows when samplers cannot be inverted.
hPoiz4zaEh.key_idea: Sample the generator's latent from homogeneous CLWE, Gaussian except for a secret periodic subspace, so the key holder recovers the mark while keyless removal needs larger distortion.
hPoiz4zaEh.evidence: Verified on four datasets and six generator families (including TabSyn, TabDDPM, and STaSy), with theory for certified p-values, tamper tolerance, and keyless removal cost.
hPoiz4zaEh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the scheme rests on a principled cryptographic foundation based on lattice hardness, with certified p-values and useful forensic components such as key-randomization tests and row-level localization.
hPoiz4zaEh.main_concern: The deployed data-space variant lacks the cryptographic guarantee, the latent variant fails on TabSyn, and tree-based C2ST scores of 0.746-0.993 contradict the indistinguishability claim.

hfwQ6I0yg4.one_liner: Recomputes gradient-projection protected directions and strengths after each task from consolidated activation usage via an exact spectral solution.
hfwQ6I0yg4.problem: In fixed-capacity models, protected subspaces in gradient-projection continual learning saturate over long task sequences, and soft-projection importance can ossify into effectively hard constraints.
hfwQ6I0yg4.method: SC-GPM combines activation usage across tasks in a bounded per-layer operator and recomputes protected directions and strengths after each task. It poses the protection-versus-new-learning trade-off as a convex problem with an exact spectral solution that reserves a specified capacity by relaxing protection on less-used directions.
hfwQ6I0yg4.key_idea: Solve a convex trade-off between protecting past tasks and reserving update capacity in closed spectral form, relaxing protection on less-used activation directions after every task.
hfwQ6I0yg4.evidence: DomainNet, OmniBenchmark, and ImageNet-1K streams of 100-160 tasks against gradient-projection baselines, plus PMNIST capacity-reserve studies and ablations.
hfwQ6I0yg4.claimed_gains: SC-GPM improves final average accuracy by 2.18-3.64 across DomainNet, OmniBenchmark, and ImageNet-1K streams of 100-160 tasks.
hfwQ6I0yg4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the convex capacity-allocation formulation with an exact spectral solution is interpretable and easy to implement, and that it improves final accuracy on long task sequences.
hfwQ6I0yg4.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to the capacity reserve, which does not by itself guarantee new-task learning, and old tasks decline more than under most projection baselines on DomainNet and ImageNet.

apIDAC7f2K.one_liner: Separates query-dependent residual-law estimation, via energy-score-trained retrieval, from a single global conformal threshold for adaptive prediction sets.
apIDAC7f2K.problem: Conformal prediction gives marginal coverage, but building locally reliable and efficient multivariate prediction sets is hard in high dimensions.
apIDAC7f2K.method: FacCP learns a query-specific residual law by energy-score-trained retrieval, assuming conditional residual laws admit a low-dimensional uncertainty-sufficient representation. The residual law sets the local geometry and supports multiple set families without retraining, while one global conformal quantile ensures finite-sample marginal coverage.
apIDAC7f2K.key_idea: Approximate query-dependent oracle geometries to obtain approximately pivotal nonconformity scores, so local geometry is learned separately and calibrated by one global quantile.
apIDAC7f2K.evidence: Controlled synthetic experiments on the geometry-pivotality link, and high-dimensional reachable set prediction in autonomous driving (Argoverse 2 motion forecasting) and quadcopter reachability.
apIDAC7f2K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method needs no retraining to support different set families, and that it is validated by extensive controlled synthetic studies and realistic robotics tasks.
apIDAC7f2K.main_concern: Real-world validation is limited to one non-synthetic dataset, and the theory assumes rather than proves that the energy-score objective achieves the geometry approximation that controls pivotality.

8ob671MCOK.one_liner: Compares 150 humans, computer-use agents, and text LLMs on a no-communication card game where only timing signals coordination.
8ob671MCOK.problem: It is unclear how humans use implicit temporal cues for dynamic, fine-grained social coordination, and whether AI systems can do the same without experiencing continuous real time.
8ob671MCOK.method: Uses the cooperative card game The Mind, where explicit communication is forbidden and the passage of time is the only signal. Human and model behavior is compared with a linear timing strategy, a Bayesian strategy that infers a partner's belief from timing, and a random baseline.
8ob671MCOK.key_idea: Fit human and model play to a Bayesian strategy that infers a partner's belief from timing, contrasting computer-use agents with text-prompted LLMs.
8ob671MCOK.evidence: 150 human participants plus computer-use agents and standard text-prompted LLMs playing The Mind, mostly against fixed rule-based partners.
8ob671MCOK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using time as a coordination signal is an interesting, under-studied question, and that the shared framework comparing humans, CUAs, and text LLMs shows models lack online adaptation.
8ob671MCOK.main_concern: The setting is narrow: humans and models play fixed rule-based partners rather than each other, timing is presented differently to humans and LLMs, and mental-state claims are not directly measured.

A3NX4PJc0I.one_liner: Localizes sparse-attention retrieval loss to a few blind heads, repaired training-free by full attention or a 4-bit key scorer.
A3NX4PJc0I.problem: Trained sparse attention models can lose substantial accuracy at their deployed selection budgets, and it is unclear where the loss occurs.
A3NX4PJc0I.method: Uses exact attention-mass selection as an oracle diagnostic per token and head to locate the loss in a few blind heads whose selector misses a needle they attend to, likely because mean-pooled key summaries dilute a single decisive token. It repairs them without training, using full attention in those heads or a scorer that ranks blocks with each head's full softmax over a 4-bit copy of the keys.
A3NX4PJc0I.key_idea: Use an exact attention-mass oracle to find heads whose block selector misses tokens they attend to, then give those heads full attention or rescore blocks with 4-bit keys.
A3NX4PJc0I.evidence: InfLLM-V2 checkpoints and MiniCPM4.1-8B on RULER MK3 multi-key retrieval at 64K, with controls repairing other or random heads and tests on four other selector designs.
A3NX4PJc0I.claimed_gains: On held-out prompts, the two repairs recover 31.4 and 30.1 of the 33.2 points on RULER MK3 that InfLLM-V2-8B loses, and 41.0 and 41.1 of 41.8 on MiniCPM4.1-8B at 64K.
A3NX4PJc0I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostic is well isolated with informative controls, and that the training-free repairs recover most of the lost accuracy across backbones and sparse-attention designs.
A3NX4PJc0I.main_concern: The few-head finding is strongest within the MiniCPM4/InfLLM-V2 family and RULER-style retrieval, repair latency is not measured, and full attention in those heads hurts some tasks.

ZgM6N1hmsW.one_liner: Amortizes continuous implicit neural representations across subjects with a selective state-space backbone and spherical harmonic positional encodings for scalp imaging.
ZgM6N1hmsW.problem: Conventional INRs are fitted per instance, requiring costly test-time optimization and giving representations that do not transfer across subjects, while neuroimaging models are tied to discrete acquisition geometries.
ZgM6N1hmsW.method: CANDI encodes long spatiotemporal contexts in linear time with a selective state-space backbone. It adds spherical harmonic positional encodings motivated by the differential operators of spherical spline interpolation, which capture the geometry and smoothness of fields on 2D scalp manifolds, and can incorporate modality-specific observation geometry.
ZgM6N1hmsW.key_idea: Amortize INR inference across subjects with a state-space encoder, and encode scalp positions with spherical harmonics tied to spherical spline operators so unseen electrodes can be queried.
ZgM6N1hmsW.evidence: 4D fMRI spatiotemporal reconstruction and EEG unseen-electrode spatial querying on two datasets, with up to 87.5% of electrodes held out, against amortized INR baselines (SSI, ZUNA) and classical spherical splines.
ZgM6N1hmsW.claimed_gains: CANDI outperforms current amortized INR baselines on 4D fMRI spatiotemporal reconstruction and outperforms classical spherical splines on EEG unseen-electrode spatial querying on hold-out sets of up to 87.5% unseen electrodes.
ZgM6N1hmsW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the EEG protocol, which masks held-out electrodes from all supervision, is a sound test of spatial generalization, and that CANDI beats baselines such as SSI and ZUNA in sparse settings.
ZgM6N1hmsW.main_concern: The cross-modal continuous-field claim goes beyond the experiments, ablations do not isolate gains over existing generalizable-INR components, and the manuscript has internal inconsistencies.

bVzQ1Z3T1p.one_liner: Retrieves sentences from sEEG by combining a global sentence embedding with a local word-level comparison to contextual word embeddings.
bVzQ1Z3T1p.problem: Identifying heard language from neural activity requires aligning distributed, time-varying brain signals with linguistic representations.
bVzQ1Z3T1p.method: GLANCE encodes within-lead dynamics with recurrent encoders, combines leads with spatial attention, and builds a global sentence representation, while a local pathway compares time-resolved neural features with contextual word embeddings of each candidate transcript. It is trained with a multi-positive contrastive objective, lightweight adaptation of frozen text features, and paired full and partially masked neural views.
bVzQ1Z3T1p.key_idea: Combine whole-sentence similarity with word-level evidence in embedding space, without word-onset supervision or a fixed word-to-time alignment, under a multi-positive contrastive objective.
bVzQ1Z3T1p.evidence: 13 recordings from four Brain Treebank participants during naturalistic movie viewing, with separate models per participant-movie recording and 100-way retrieval; comparison with prior models only on one movie.
bVzQ1Z3T1p.claimed_gains: Under 100-way retrieval, GLANCE achieves 26.2% subject-averaged Recall@10 and exceeds the 10% chance level in every recording.
bVzQ1Z3T1p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is well designed, combining word- and sentence-level information with sensible spatial handling of sEEG leads and a 100-way retrieval task with known chance, and that results are above chance in every recording.
bVzQ1Z3T1p.main_concern: Random within-movie train-test splits place test sentences seconds from training sentences, so slow neural drift, scene context, or duration cues could inflate retrieval scores.

Q1DX2pGLlZ.one_liner: Scores randomly grouped candidates jointly to cut self-evaluation ranking error, motivated by a bias-variance decomposition of ranking error.
Q1DX2pGLlZ.problem: More candidates do not consistently narrow the gap between final-answer accuracy and pass@N, because models cannot reliably distinguish their correct generations from incorrect ones.
Q1DX2pGLlZ.method: Shows ranking error admits a bias-variance decomposition shaped by algorithmic design choices and inference compute, where more compute generally reduces variance while bias plateaus. Scorpio jointly scores randomly grouped candidates and is applied to verification, tree search, and aggregation.
Q1DX2pGLlZ.key_idea: Score randomly grouped candidates together instead of independently, guided by a bias-variance view in which extra compute lowers variance but bias plateaus.
Q1DX2pGLlZ.evidence: Math, code, and puzzle benchmarks for verification, tree search over partial solutions, and aggregation, with analysis of group size and pairing strategy and costs that include generation and evaluation.
Q1DX2pGLlZ.claimed_gains: For verification, Scorpio improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by up to 7 percentage points while matching or exceeding its peak accuracy with 6-42% lower total inference cost; for tree search it improves accuracy by up to 10 percentage points, and for aggregation scaling by 12 percentage points.
Q1DX2pGLlZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree Scorpio is a simple, training-free method that improves verification accuracy and cost across verification, search, and aggregation, and that the persistent pass@1 to pass@N gap is an important finding.
Q1DX2pGLlZ.main_concern: The bias-variance decomposition is determined by one misranking probability and is not connected to top-1 selection accuracy, so it does not isolate why extra evaluation compute fails to close the gap.

MjqcLg39np.one_liner: Synthesizes calibration data for ViT quantization against structurally perturbed teachers using attention-head and spatial-token dropout as probes.
MjqcLg39np.problem: Data-free quantization methods optimize synthetic samples against a single deterministic teacher, so samples can be structurally brittle, giving unreliable calibration statistics and degraded quantization.
MjqcLg39np.method: DropIS applies attention head dropout and spatial token dropout to the pretrained teacher as probes during sample synthesis, so samples stay consistent across perturbed teachers. Theory links structural sensitivity of synthetic samples to the gap between real and synthetic calibration statistics.
MjqcLg39np.key_idea: Synthesize calibration samples that stay consistent under multiple dropout-perturbed copies of the teacher, exposing response variations hidden by deterministic supervision.
MjqcLg39np.evidence: ImageNet classification with ViT, DeiT, and Swin backbones at 3W3A, 4W4A, 5W5A, and 4W8A, with ablations of components, probe sampling, number of probes, dropout rates, sample count, 2-bit quantization, and dense tasks.
MjqcLg39np.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is a simple plug-in with consistent gains across backbones and bit-widths, especially at low bit-widths, backed by broad empirical coverage.
MjqcLg39np.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to perturbation-based synthesis such as DeepInversion, and the multi-probe gains are confounded with compute because no compute-matched baseline is given.

hNBtS0z51X.one_liner: Groups rubric criteria into protocol-level dimensions that earn credit only when all criteria hold, replacing additive reward aggregation.
hNBtS0z51X.problem: In rubric-based RL, additive aggregation lets criteria compensate for one another, so a policy that misses the decisive point can buy back reward with unrequested advice, scoring higher while answering worse.
hNBtS0z51X.method: ProRubric groups a checklist into a few protocol-level dimensions, where a dimension counts only when all its criteria hold and its failure clause does not fire. The grouping is done once, offline, and leaves the optimizer unchanged.
hNBtS0z51X.key_idea: Change how criterion verdicts are aggregated, not which criteria are used: require all criteria in a protocol-level group to hold before awarding credit.
hNBtS0z51X.evidence: Clinical consultation with held-out physician criteria, controlled experiments that keep criteria unchanged while varying aggregation, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, science tasks, and a seven-benchmark average.
hNBtS0z51X.claimed_gains: ProRubric raises appropriateness by 10.8 points without losing coverage and has the best seven-benchmark average at both scales.
hNBtS0z51X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled experiments, which keep criteria wording fixed and vary only aggregation, make a convincing case that the scored unit matters, especially in the medical setting.
hNBtS0z51X.main_concern: ProRubric does not fully resolve reward hacking (appropriateness still falls below the untrained model and far below SFT on medical responses), and the claim that criteria are not to blame is overstated.

GezhFCeAvR.one_liner: Regret analysis of online logistic prediction with paid noisy features, showing covariance alone no longer determines optimal loss.
GezhFCeAvR.problem: In online binary prediction with paid stochastic features the learner must trade prediction loss against acquisition cost, and the covariance-based result for online linear regression does not carry over to logistic loss.
GezhFCeAvR.method: Under a structural ordering in which larger payments remove independent noise, the paper develops algorithms for known and unknown noise structure. Per reviewers, a simulation-by-degradation idea lets all payment levels share one sample stream.
GezhFCeAvR.key_idea: Use the ordering that larger payments remove independent noise to simulate cheaper observations by degrading better ones, sharing one sample stream across payment levels.
GezhFCeAvR.evidence: Theoretical regret upper bounds with matching lower bounds in both the known- and unknown-noise regimes; a reviewer notes there are no experiments.
GezhFCeAvR.claimed_gains: Obtains O~(sqrt(T)) regret when the noise structure is known and O~(T^(2/3)) regret when it is unknown, with lower bounds matching the dependence on horizon T up to logarithmic factors.
GezhFCeAvR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, extends online linear regression with paid features to logistic loss, and gives tight regret rates in both known and unknown noise regimes.
GezhFCeAvR.main_concern: The contribution is seen as incremental relative to the linear-regression case, since the algorithms, rates, and lower-bound strategy mirror it, and there is no experimental validation or clear real-world applicability.

wlaiuSEpVJ.one_liner: Compiles repeated task-level events from offline replay into register-update rules and composes them in a planner over frozen goal-conditioned policies.
wlaiuSEpVJ.problem: Goal-conditioned policies often reach nearby goals but fail when a task requires composing many distinct changes.
wlaiuSEpVJ.method: ATQ represents task progress with persistent registers, learns how recurring task-level events update them, and compiles the learned rules into a task-event circuit whose paths are possible sequences of task changes. At test time a planner selects an event sequence, a policy executes one local request, and feedback updates the circuit state.
