wlaiuSEpVJ.key_idea: Learn event-update rules over persistent task registers from replay, compile them into a circuit, and plan event sequences that frozen policies execute one local request at a time.
wlaiuSEpVJ.evidence: All eight OGBench Puzzle tasks with eight independently trained GCIQL policies, compared with Test-Time Graph Search and cited published scores, plus navigation, object manipulation, and soccer tasks.
wlaiuSEpVJ.claimed_gains: On all eight OGBench Puzzle tasks ATQ reaches 95.3-100.0% success versus 0.2-44.1% for Test-Time Graph Search on the 4x4-4x6 layouts, and it raises success in navigation, object manipulation, and soccer by up to 27.2 percentage points.
wlaiuSEpVJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments are rigorous across diverse tasks and show composition into unseen register configurations, and that extracting explicit event rules from replay to drive frozen policies helps long-horizon tasks.
wlaiuSEpVJ.main_concern: The method relies on hand-designed candidate variables and operators, including an XOR operator that matches the Puzzle (Lights Out) structure, and no ablation separates learned rule selection from this built-in prior.

S5ZlePeOml.one_liner: Multi-stage choice models built as directed acyclic graphs of multinomial logit units, with depth-norm separation and universality results.
S5ZlePeOml.problem: Most feature-based choice models score items and apply a single softmax, so menu-independent random-utility models, including a single MNL unit, cannot represent context effects such as the compromise effect.
S5ZlePeOml.method: Source units assign probabilities to menu items, and internal units combine predecessor distributions using MNL weights computed from their probability-weighted feature summaries. The paper proves depth-norm separation and characterizes when arbitrary deterministic choice tables on finite menu families can be approximated.
S5ZlePeOml.key_idea: Stack MNL units in a DAG where internal units mix predecessor distributions with weights computed from their probability-weighted features, so added depth lowers the required taste-vector norm.
S5ZlePeOml.evidence: Proofs on a three-item compromise task and universality for deterministic choice tables, plus experiments with standalone circuits and neural output heads, including a hotel (Expedia) dataset with a temporal split.
S5ZlePeOml.claimed_gains: Increasing depth from 2 to 3 reduces the optimal maximum taste-vector norm for error epsilon from Theta(log(1/epsilon)/epsilon) to Theta(log(1/epsilon)), and depth 4 achieves optimal logarithmic norm scaling.
S5ZlePeOml.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the model is a simple, well-motivated generalization of MNL with clean theory, notably a depth-2 lower bound that holds for any width and routing biases.
S5ZlePeOml.main_concern: The theory covers deterministic choice tables and is not connected to how the models are trained or evaluated, and the empirical claims rest mostly on one Expedia dataset.

qYLljrZmmE.one_liner: Adds fluctuation-dissipation-matched Langevin noise to temporal predictive coding so inference samples per-step conditional posteriors instead of point estimates.
qYLljrZmmE.problem: Temporal predictive coding propagates a deterministic point estimate of the latent state at each step rather than a posterior distribution, so MAP inference collapses multimodal posteriors to a single mode.
qYLljrZmmE.method: Adds Langevin noise scaled by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, so Langevin tPC samples the per-step conditional posterior given each chain's propagated parent. It compares identity and transition-covariance preconditioners and derives a per-direction step size used as a diagnostic.
qYLljrZmmE.key_idea: Set the Langevin noise scale by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem so tPC's local inference dynamics have the per-step conditional posterior as their stationary distribution.
qYLljrZmmE.evidence: Synthetic targets, twelve static regression problems with exact Gaussian-mixture posteriors, two temporal benchmarks scored against the exact filtering marginal, and unimodal video, against dispersed MAP ensembles and per-frame Monte Carlo predictive coding.
qYLljrZmmE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper offers careful theoretical and empirical analysis, evaluated against exact posteriors with candid controls and failure cases.
qYLljrZmmE.main_concern: Support for recovering temporal posterior mass is weak: the strongest result is on a static problem, temporal results are mixed, and novelty over Monte Carlo predictive coding appears incremental.

TKBRCqFJmH.one_liner: Scores nodes by graph-wavelet deviation from a source memory plus uncertainty, controlling both message passing and test-time adaptation losses.
TKBRCqFJmH.problem: Under structural shift, altered neighborhoods degrade node representations and corrupt the signals used for adaptation, and predictive confidence alone cannot tell when a model is confidently wrong.
TKBRCqFJmH.method: WaveGuard keeps a compact class-degree-conditioned memory of source graph-wavelet energy as a reference for target spectral deviation, and combines this deviation with frozen-model uncertainty into a fixed node-wise score. The score drives direction-aware soft topology purification and calibrates entropy, anchor, and consistency losses.
TKBRCqFJmH.key_idea: Use one fixed node score, from graph-wavelet energy deviation against a source memory combined with uncertainty, to jointly reweight edges and weight the unsupervised adaptation losses.
TKBRCqFJmH.evidence: Five graph benchmarks covering 23 target scenarios under structural, temporal, and mixed shifts (including CSBM, ogbn-arxiv, PubMed, Twitch, and Elliptic), with five seeds and ablations.
TKBRCqFJmH.claimed_gains: Ranks first in six of eight CSBM scenarios, achieves the highest average accuracy on ogbn-arxiv, and on Elliptic surpasses the strongest baseline by 6.12 and 6.63 (metric names truncated in the abstract).
TKBRCqFJmH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear, the evaluation is broad (23 scenarios, five seeds), and the edge-selectivity analysis shows the score attenuates injected edges more than natural heterophilic ones.
TKBRCqFJmH.main_concern: Baseline quality is questionable (several baselines collapse or give near-identical numbers), and ablations do not isolate the spectral-memory score from simpler control scores.

qZzjRVKN17.one_liner: Cross-state domain adaptation (RASA) transfers concept-aligned neuronal representations from movie viewing to memory recall and sleep.
qZzjRVKN17.problem: Representations learned from sparse recordings during one-shot experience generalize poorly to recall and sleep states, which have different distributions and few or no labels.
qZzjRVKN17.method: Participant-specific region-wise attention encoders are trained with multi-label classification and contrastive alignment to learned concept embeddings, then adapted across brain states with Recall-Adapted Sleep Alignment (RASA) and validated on held-out concept-selective neurons during sleep.
qZzjRVKN17.key_idea: Cross-state domain adaptation (RASA) aligns concept-embedding encoders trained on movie viewing to recall and sleep, validated against held-out concept-selective neurons.
qZzjRVKN17.evidence: Intracranial microelectrode recordings of 452 curated single-neuron units from 13 neurosurgical participants, with movie watching as source and vocalized recall and sleep as targets.
qZzjRVKN17.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is meaningful and difficult, the recorded dataset is valuable, and RASA and the held-out-neuron validation design are well motivated.
qZzjRVKN17.main_concern: Baselines do not receive comparable adaptation, and alignment with held-out concept-selective neurons may not establish genuine concept decoding, with possible information leakage in the evaluation.

0zTjUsZYxz.one_liner: Adaptive sequences of LLM classifier queries, solved by dynamic programming, trade classification accuracy against query cost.
0zTjUsZYxz.problem: LLM classifier predictions are neither deterministic nor uniformly reliable, and it is unclear how to combine several models for reliability at a given query cost.
0zTjUsZYxz.method: Each LLM classifier is treated as a noisy measurement instrument of the target label, and 'circuits' organize classifiers into an adaptive sequence of queries and decisions. The optimal circuit is characterized with fundamental accuracy limits and realized in practice (LMCircuit).
0zTjUsZYxz.key_idea: Frame classifiers as noisy measurement instruments and choose which to query next and when to stop via an exactly solved dynamic program over cost and accuracy.
0zTjUsZYxz.evidence: Experiments across safety, healthcare, political science and preference benchmarks against routing and cascading baselines, plus a scaling-law analysis and a pool-construction study cited by reviewers.
0zTjUsZYxz.claimed_gains: Improves the cost-accuracy frontier over routing and cascading baselines; no numeric gains stated.
0zTjUsZYxz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the principled dynamic-programming formulation, consistent cost-accuracy improvements over baselines, and clear writing.
0zTjUsZYxz.main_concern: The technical development is detached from LLMs (the framing is called largely cosmetic) and the exact dynamic program scales poorly beyond small classifier pools.

H2UzE1Gjg5.one_liner: Conditional generative model of command-minus-state residuals from teleoperation labels actions for kinematic-only dexterous hand demonstrations.
H2UzE1Gjg5.problem: Motion-capture glove and exoskeleton demonstrations record observed hand motion but not joint commands, which differ from observed states during contact.
H2UzE1Gjg5.method: GAS trains a conditional generative model of residuals between commanded joint targets and observed hand states on teleoperation data, conditioned on past and future visual observations and joint states. It samples residuals to relabel kinematic-only demonstrations and trains policies on them.
H2UzE1Gjg5.key_idea: Learn the command-state residual distribution from teleoperation data with a conditional generative model and add sampled residuals to observed joint states as action labels.
H2UzE1Gjg5.evidence: Zero-shot action synthesis on mug grasping, towel folding, cap twisting, test tube insertion, USB unplugging and Rubik's cube manipulation, with policies trained on synthesized labels for four tasks and real-robot experiments.
H2UzE1Gjg5.claimed_gains: The visible abstract states high policy success on four tasks without numbers; a review cites 86% for GAS-labeled glove data versus 55% for teleoperation data under matched wall-clock time.
H2UzE1Gjg5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the missing-action-label problem is consequential and that learning command residuals from teleoperation to relabel kinematic demonstrations is a well-motivated approach.
H2UzE1Gjg5.main_concern: Baselines are insufficient to show that generative modeling or the residual formulation helps (no deterministic residual or direct action prediction), and the teleoperation comparison is confounded by 2.3-3.6x more glove data.

kNmUXermHN.one_liner: Bisimulation Information Bottleneck compresses frozen foundation-model visual features into compact states for fast model-based planning.
kNmUXermHN.problem: Planning over high-dimensional outputs of visual foundation models is too slow for real-time use, partly because they encode task-irrelevant information.
kNmUXermHN.method: S2P maps frozen pretrained visual features to a compact task-specific state with a Bisimulation Information Bottleneck objective that discards task-irrelevant visual information while keeping reward and dynamics information. A lightweight MLP world model then plans in this space.
kNmUXermHN.key_idea: Train a compression of frozen visual features with a bisimulation-based information bottleneck that retains only reward- and dynamics-relevant information for MLP-rollout planning.
kNmUXermHN.evidence: Two real-time visual manipulation tasks, robustness tests under lighting and object-colour perturbations, and a distracting-background setting; reviews cite memory and speed comparisons against DINO-WM and other DINO baselines.
kNmUXermHN.claimed_gains: Orders-of-magnitude reduction in time and memory to generate a plan, and success on two real-time tasks where prior methods generally fail; a review cites 161 MiB versus 7.51 GiB peak memory against DINO-WM.
kNmUXermHN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree planning cost drops substantially and measurably while robustness is retained, addressing a practically useful problem for visual foundation models in robotics.
kNmUXermHN.main_concern: S2P trains online while baselines use a fixed offline dataset, so success-rate gains cannot be attributed to the compression method, and blocking dynamics-loss gradients to the encoder does not hurt.

ZweFYN4Dy1.one_liner: Best-of-N over many small collaborating agent teams, instead of lone agents or one large team, scales test-time compute better.
ZweFYN4Dy1.problem: Best-of-N over independent agents saturates quickly and one large agent team stops improving as it grows, so neither scales test-time compute well.
ZweFYN4Dy1.method: Parallel agent teams sample many small teams in parallel and keep the best team's result under a verifier. A simple normal-distribution model explains the trade-off between per-sample mean and variance.
ZweFYN4Dy1.key_idea: Apply best-of-N selection at the level of small collaborating teams, balancing a higher per-sample mean from collaboration against the variance gain from many samples.
ZweFYN4Dy1.evidence: 12 long-horizon tasks from GPU kernels and formal proofs to exploit development, using a 27B model at a 100-agent budget, compared with parallel single agents, one large team and a frontier model at equal dollar cost.
ZweFYN4Dy1.claimed_gains: Parallel teams of ten beat parallel agents on 10 of 12 tasks and beat one team of 100 on all four tasks where such teams were run, and beat a frontier model on half the tasks at equal dollar cost.
ZweFYN4Dy1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is an extensive, well-documented comparison of compute allocation across independent, single-team and parallel-team sampling, and that the construction is simple to deploy.
ZweFYN4Dy1.main_concern: The numerical claims are statistically under-supported (few team runs per task, no confidence intervals), and the toy-like theory gives no practical guidance for choosing team number and size.

9PlqJbGOfE.one_liner: Web2Earth adapts a web-pretrained vision encoder to optical and SAR imagery via RGB self-distillation and cross-modal patch and relational distillation.
9PlqJbGOfE.problem: Web-pretrained vision foundation models are RGB-centric and handle other remote sensing modalities such as SAR poorly.
9PlqJbGOfE.method: Builds on a web-pretrained encoder with joint RGB self-distillation and cross-modal transfer using patch-level (CoPaD) and relational (CMRD) distillation objectives from RGB to SAR. Adaptation updates about 2% of parameters using 32k RGB images and about 5k co-registered pairs.
9PlqJbGOfE.key_idea: Transfer local patch predictions and scene-level relationships from the RGB branch to other modalities with distillation, rather than directly aligning RGB and SAR feature vectors.
9PlqJbGOfE.evidence: Evaluations across diverse optical and SAR tasks, including unseen SAR sensors and cross-modal retrieval, with ablations of the distillation objectives.
9PlqJbGOfE.claimed_gains: Leading results on the main optical evaluations and the highest average score across six SAR evaluations among compared models, using about 2% trainable parameters, 32k RGB images and about 5k co-registered pairs.
9PlqJbGOfE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad across optical and SAR tasks and that adapting an existing web-pretrained model with little data and few updated parameters is practical.
9PlqJbGOfE.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because the objectives extend existing relational, patch-level and cross-modal distillation, and there is no RGB-only adaptation baseline to isolate the optical gain.

y8UqVFDiQH.one_liner: Polyphase token reassembly and a Haar wavelet discriminator remove token-phase grid artifacts in one-step diffusion-transformer super-resolution.
y8UqVFDiQH.problem: One-step DiT super-resolution produces periodic grid-like artifacts whose prediction discrepancies vary with the token packing stride, unlike a convolutional U-Net.
y8UqVFDiQH.method: PhaDiSR adds Polyphase Token Reassembly to apply a phase-aware correction to the packed velocity prediction, a Token-Phase Wavelet Discriminator with multi-scale, multi-shift Haar supervision, and Self-Prior Projection to build training references from the frozen initialization prior.
y8UqVFDiQH.key_idea: Expose the implicit token phases in the packed velocity prediction for a phase-aware correction, and penalize residual phase artifacts with multi-shift Haar wavelet discrimination.
y8UqVFDiQH.evidence: A translation-equivariance diagnostic of packing-induced token-phase dependence, tests on paired and unpaired datasets, cross-backbone experiments and appendix quantitative analysis.
y8UqVFDiQH.claimed_gains: Substantially reduces token-phase dependence and periodic grid artifacts and achieves leading perceptual fidelity; no numbers stated.
y8UqVFDiQH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the translation-equivariance diagnosis is concrete and that the velocity-space correction and image-space wavelet supervision follow logically from it and give consistent perceptual gains.
y8UqVFDiQH.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the phase-aware design, since the main table compares full systems with different backbones, data and losses, with no matched-backbone comparison or analysis against prior GAN-based and OP4KSR approaches.

YRuBKMG5rM.one_liner: A neural Dirichlet random measure learns a continuous urban intensity field whose integral over any region gives conserved quantity predictions.
YRuBKMG5rM.problem: Data-driven urban region representations are learned on a fixed spatial partition, which limits their use across different partitions.
YRuBKMG5rM.method: Learns a continuous intensity field over the whole spatial domain with a Dirichlet-multinomial model, so integrating over any region gives its quantitative representation with conservation. The field is learned directly from observations on different partitions, using pretrained geospatial embeddings on a fixed fine lattice.
YRuBKMG5rM.key_idea: Model urban quantities as a neural intensity field under a Dirichlet random measure, so region values are integrals of the field and totals are conserved under any partition.
YRuBKMG5rM.evidence: Experiments on ten major U.S. cities with widely used urban spatial embeddings, as a predictor on arbitrary partitions and as a learner of partition-agnostic embeddings with cross-city transfer to unseen cities.
YRuBKMG5rM.claimed_gains: Guarantees quantitative conservation and generally gives better predictive quality than conventional direct prediction, and learned embeddings generally outperform fixed-partition ones; no numbers stated.
YRuBKMG5rM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers who list strengths agree partition dependence is a well-motivated problem and that the integration-based formulation gives quantity conservation within a principled probabilistic framework.
YRuBKMG5rM.main_concern: The 'continuous' field is evaluated on a fixed fine lattice and needs known regional totals, which reduces it to a per-cell weighted representation with limited novelty, additive-only applicability and missing disaggregation baselines.

JqfFBRivCE.one_liner: Follow-the-perturbed-leader with Gaussian perturbations gives oracle-efficient, parameter-free agnostic smoothed online learning with unknown base measure.
JqfFBRivCE.problem: Agnostic smoothed online learning with an unknown base measure was known to be statistically efficient only through a computationally intractable algorithm.
JqfFBRivCE.method: A simple FTPL algorithm with Gaussian perturbations needs only a weighted ERM oracle. The binary case makes one oracle call per round without knowing the base measure, smoothing parameter or horizon, and an extension handles general losses.
JqfFBRivCE.key_idea: Run follow-the-perturbed-leader with Gaussian perturbations so each round reduces to a single weighted offline optimization call, without knowing the base measure.
JqfFBRivCE.evidence: Regret analysis with square-root dependence on the horizon for the binary case and an extension to general losses; no empirical evaluation is described.
JqfFBRivCE.claimed_gains: Claims the first oracle-efficient algorithm for agnostic smoothed online learning with an unknown base measure; no numbers stated.
JqfFBRivCE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and open, the algorithm is simple and needs no knowledge of the base measure, and removing realizability and known-measure assumptions is a meaningful step.
JqfFBRivCE.main_concern: Practical value is unclear because the guarantees rely on an exact weighted ERM oracle and the general-loss extension needs t oracle calls in round t.

V5cJPBcTDM.one_liner: Midtraining a history-conditioned robot policy on adversarially perturbed human demonstrations with segment-level language relabeling improves recovery and online adaptation.
V5cJPBcTDM.problem: Human demonstrations concentrate on competent behavior, giving robot policies little coverage of off-distribution states and low-level recovery behaviors needed over long horizons.
V5cJPBcTDM.method: Collect rollouts where an adversary reversibly perturbs the environment or task while a human operates, relabel segments with natural-language annotations of the local outcome, and midtrain a pretrained history-conditioned policy on them.
V5cJPBcTDM.key_idea: Collect demonstrations while an adversary reversibly perturbs the scene, forcing recoveries, and midtrain on outcome-relabeled segments to build connected behavioral coverage.
V5cJPBcTDM.evidence: Several long-horizon tasks on three real-robot platforms and in simulation, compared with training on standard demonstration data, covering zero-shot scaling, out-of-distribution generalization, test-time compute and online finetuning.
V5cJPBcTDM.claimed_gains: Better zero-shot scaling, robustness, generalization to new configurations, gains from longer rollouts and faster online improvement; a review cites simulation success of 547/1,000 rising to 697/1,000 and real LEGO 5/20 versus 19/20.
V5cJPBcTDM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers who list strengths agree the method is simple and well explained, with experiments designed to identify useful data characteristics and substantial gains over standard demonstrations.
V5cJPBcTDM.main_concern: The gain is not attributed to connected recovery behavior versus broader state and task coverage, the contribution over prior adversarial data collection is unclear, and the only baseline is standard behavior cloning.

vJM62ASATW.one_liner: Locates visual FFN channels by normalized activation energy on forget images and learns sparse residual updates for MLLM unlearning.
vJM62ASATW.problem: Existing MLLM unlearning methods update broad parameter regions or remove target-related neurons, which damages representations shared with retained knowledge.
vJM62ASATW.method: VASE selects a small set of visual feed-forward channels by normalized activation energy on forget images and learns sparse residual updates only for them. A bounded forgetting objective plus output- and activation-level constraints preserve retained behavior, and updates are merged into the visual backbone.
vJM62ASATW.key_idea: Edit only the few visual FFN channels most active on forget images, with a bounded forgetting loss and retention constraints, and merge the updates for zero inference overhead.
vJM62ASATW.evidence: Multiple benchmarks and MLLM backbones; reviews cite two datasets and two main backbones, with ablations of localization and loss components.
vJM62ASATW.claimed_gains: Reports the lowest forgetting among compared methods while preserving retained knowledge and general multimodal capabilities; no numbers stated.
vJM62ASATW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree VASE gives a strong forgetting-retention trade-off, with substantial suppression of forget-set answers, retain performance close to the original models and thorough ablations.
vJM62ASATW.main_concern: Forgetting is measured only by multiple-choice or VQA accuracy and ROUGE-L, and examples where answers are replaced by wrong facts do not show the target information is unrecoverable under other prompts or images.

fcQaMnBdzB.one_liner: Fine-tuning a coding agent only on next-token loss over its own retrospective explanations improves later attempts without reward-based updates.
fcQaMnBdzB.problem: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards gives no signal on tasks where the base model never succeeds, wasting what failed attempts could teach.
fcQaMnBdzB.method: ROFT has the agent attempt a task, observe feedback, generate a retrospective explanation, and fine-tune with next-token prediction on the explanation tokens alone. It uses no external teacher and no reward-based policy update.
fcQaMnBdzB.key_idea: Train only on the agent's own post-attempt explanations so action improvements transfer through shared weights, giving indirect credit assignment without action-target supervision.
fcQaMnBdzB.evidence: Software-engineering experiments with Qwen3.5-4B on SWE-bench Verified and Pro against GRPO, plus a 9B extension, a no-final-verdict ablation and behavioral analyses.
fcQaMnBdzB.claimed_gains: After 20 updates ROFT reaches 49.2% and 29.0% on held-out SWE-bench Verified and Pro versus GRPO's 48.0% and 25.3% after 40 updates, and solves very difficult tasks where pass@64 is 0.
fcQaMnBdzB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ROFT learns from tasks with no observed successes, converges faster than GRPO-style baselines, and is supported by thorough ablations, cost accounting and a clear procedure.
fcQaMnBdzB.main_concern: Gains over GRPO are small (six tasks on SWE-bench Verified) with no seed uncertainty, and an SFT control on successful trajectories from the same attempts and dependence on reflection quality are untested.

tyHfHVp7cI.one_liner: Search-then-distil framework rewrites an LLM's summary so held-out attribution classifiers assign it to a chosen target model.
tyHfHVp7cI.problem: Model-attribution classifiers are treated as provenance evidence, but their robustness to deliberate rewriting toward a chosen target model is untested.
tyHfHVp7cI.method: ForgePrint searches for rewrites that move attribution toward a target fingerprint, then distils the selected rewrites into a one-pass 4B Student model. It is studied on summarisation, where different models see the same document.
tyHfHVp7cI.key_idea: Distil search-selected targeted rewrites into a single-pass student model so text moves toward a chosen model's fingerprint against held-out classifiers.
tyHfHVp7cI.evidence: CNN/DM summarisation against held-out classifiers never queried by the attack, six published rewriting baselines, and transfer from an open model toward chosen commercial models.
tyHfHVp7cI.claimed_gains: Student reaches 70.2% target success on CNN/DM versus 54.1% for its Teacher and 39.3% for the strongest of six published baselines, and 68.3% when targeting commercial models.
tyHfHVp7cI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that redirecting attribution toward a chosen model is a meaningful problem, that evaluation is separated from attack development, and that text-only attribution should not be treated as proof of origin.
tyHfHVp7cI.main_concern: Content preservation is not folded into attack success: only 37.1% of student rewrites pass an independent content judge, so a joint success metric is needed.

ga0tTULDQx.one_liner: LYCORE learns only inside a Lyapunov core and defers to a stabilizing policy outside, with matching sample-complexity bounds.
ga0tTULDQx.problem: Learning a globally stable, near-optimal policy from finite data is hard in countably infinite MDPs with unbounded states such as queue lengths and tracking errors.
ga0tTULDQx.method: LYCORE is a model-based algorithm that samples only within an accuracy-dependent Lyapunov core and uses a known stabilizing policy elsewhere. It combines uniform drift sampling with shell-dependent model sampling that allocates fewer samples to rarely visited outer regions.
ga0tTULDQx.key_idea: Negative Lyapunov drift concentrates long-run occupancy in a finite core, so learning there plus a known stabilizing fallback outside yields stable near-optimal policies.
ga0tTULDQx.evidence: Matching upper and lower sample-complexity bounds up to logarithmic factors with a phase transition between performance and stability learning, plus experiments with rate diagnostics described in reviews.
ga0tTULDQx.claimed_gains: Global stability and near-optimality among Lyapunov-stable policies, with matching upper and lower sample-complexity bounds up to logarithmic factors; no numeric values stated.
ga0tTULDQx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is well motivated, the reduction of infinite-state learning to a finite Lyapunov core is clear and rigorous, and the bounds usefully separate performance learning from stability learning.
ga0tTULDQx.main_concern: The guarantees are restricted (a fixed action at a reference state, a drift assumption stated only in the projected MDP in Lemma C.4) and experiments do not test the full shell-allocation algorithm with learned drift and dynamics.

bK8bHUlqdo.one_liner: Proves width and depth limits commute during training for linear residual networks with 1/sqrt(depth) branch scaling and gradient clipping.
bK8bHUlqdo.problem: Commutativity of width and depth limits was known for residual networks at initialization but not during training.
bK8bHUlqdo.method: For linear residual networks with branches scaled by 1/sqrt(depth), shows that for any fixed number of clipped gradient steps the output converges in L2 as min(width, depth) goes to infinity. Without clipping only convergence in probability is obtained.
bK8bHUlqdo.key_idea: Gradient clipping keeps training updates bounded enough for L2 convergence of the output as min(width, depth) grows, whereas unclipped gradient descent gives only convergence in probability.
bK8bHUlqdo.evidence: Theoretical proofs with a quantitative error bound; reviews note supporting experiments that include ReLU and other nonlinear activations.
bK8bHUlqdo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result is an interesting, clearly written theoretical contribution that clarifies which scaling guarantees survive training, with clipping restoring L2 convergence.
bK8bHUlqdo.main_concern: Scope and impact are limited to linear networks under gradient clipping with unclear practical use, and a reviewer notes prior non-rigorous work already anticipates the commutativity and rates.

oegeqwodj7.one_liner: Admission test treats self-written agent guardrails as causal claims, using counterfactual replay and e-values to bound accepted fabrications.
oegeqwodj7.problem: Agents install self-compiled failure guardrails that merely look plausible, and on an 86-task benchmark such skills lower performance by 1.3 points on average.
oegeqwodj7.method: Earned Guardrails types each failure with a frozen matcher and admits a candidate only if counterfactual replay shows the failure recurs without it and clears with it, composed into a fixed-level e-value test priced from the budget and horizon. A post-admission ledger then promotes or retracts guards using randomized-exposure evidence.
oegeqwodj7.key_idea: Admit a guardrail only if counterfactual replay shows the failure recurs without it and clears with it, tested by a prespecified e-value, then retract it on negative marginal benefit.
oegeqwodj7.evidence: An 86-task benchmark comparing self-generated and human-curated skills, AppWorld experiments, and ablations showing necessity testing keeps out false guardrails.
oegeqwodj7.claimed_gains: On an 86-task benchmark self-generated skills lower performance by 1.3 points on average while human-curated ones raise it by 16.2; the method's own gains are not stated in the visible abstract.
oegeqwodj7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating guardrail admission as statistical hypothesis testing with horizon-wide error control is a principled, previously unaddressed approach to a real reliability problem for self-evolving agents.
oegeqwodj7.main_concern: The guarantee depends on a hard-to-verify assumption bounding phantom-failure reproduction (q0 = 0.15) and does not directly cover the empirical fabrication metric, and terminology and figures are dense.

GOTdjsfYgP.one_liner: Multi-agent web-agent guardrail where a Utility Agent repairs trajectories and a Policy Agent stores policy-indexed violation cases for later judgments.
GOTdjsfYgP.problem: Safety policies cannot enumerate how violations emerge in concrete web-agent trajectories, and existing guardrails use violation evidence for either current correction or later judgment, not both.
GOTdjsfYgP.method: A Utility Agent evaluates adjacent-step transitions and guides policy-compliant revisions, while a Policy Agent structures trusted policies and retains selected violations as bounded, policy-indexed boundary cases that ground later judgments.
GOTdjsfYgP.key_idea: Dual-timescale policy grounding: one policy-grounded violation both repairs the active trajectory and is stored as a bounded boundary case to ground future judgments.
GOTdjsfYgP.evidence: Three agent safety benchmarks, with backbone, memory-budget and runtime analyses and a multi-round experiment on 84 WASP tasks.
GOTdjsfYgP.claimed_gains: Exceeds the prompt-based baseline by up to 17.8% and 23.8% in compliance and completion, leads the agent guardrail by 8.2% in accuracy, and matches trained guardrail models at the lowest false positive rate.
GOTdjsfYgP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing violation evidence for both correction and future judgments is useful, that separating fixed policies from bounded memory makes the design easy to understand, and that results on three safety benchmarks are promising.
GOTdjsfYgP.main_concern: Memory cases come from the guard's own judgments with no independent validation, and cross-task generalization is weakly tested because multi-round experiments repeat the same 84 tasks.

QEhZcAybc4.one_liner: Generates synthetic PCB boards with EDA-engine-executable routing demonstrations, then trains a routing policy by behavior cloning and RL.
QEhZcAybc4.problem: Public PCB routing datasets are few and mostly contain only final routed states, not the EDA engine actions that produce them.
QEhZcAybc4.method: CADET jointly generates synthetic boards and demonstrations built from EDA engine actions, checked by fresh-engine replay for zero design rule violations (RouteDemos, 100,000 boards). It trains a routing policy with behavior cloning and fine-tunes it with reinforcement learning.
QEhZcAybc4.key_idea: Construct boards and demonstrations jointly from native EDA engine actions, replay-verified to be violation-free, so behavior cloning starts from executable routing traces before RL.
QEhZcAybc4.evidence: Distributions over 17 statistics compared with 142 real reference boards, and evaluation on real test boards against an RL-only baseline, FreeRouting and other baselines, with averages over 4 runs.
QEhZcAybc4.claimed_gains: Abstract: complete DRV-free routing rises from 38.0% to 67.2% over an RL-only baseline (the TL;DR states 38.7% to 66.7%), comparable to FreeRouting and above other baselines.
QEhZcAybc4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the synthetic dataset with executable, replay-checked demonstrations is valuable, matches real board statistics, and helps real-board routing in the BC plus RL pipeline.
QEhZcAybc4.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to 2-layer boards with small pad counts and a single training seed, and it is unclear whether the synthetic data captures real design complexity or route quality.

pg0VOzVMwU.one_liner: Propagates per-observation reliability estimates through reconstruction, Legendre projection, integral constraints and sparse regression to discover PDEs from heterogeneously noisy data.
pg0VOzVMwU.problem: PDE discovery methods handle clean or single-source-noise data, but heterogeneous contamination makes some observations deviate from the governing equation and amplifies errors through derivative estimation.
pg0VOzVMwU.method: CARE-PDE combines Reliability-Aware Field Reconstruction (Cauchy loss with adaptive reliability estimation), Reliability-Guided Local Legendre Projection for stable derivatives, Local Integral Constraint Aggregation, and Stability-Selected Sparse Regression.
pg0VOzVMwU.key_idea: Estimate observation reliability with a Cauchy-loss reconstruction and reuse it to choose local supports and weight integral constraints before sparse term selection.
pg0VOzVMwU.evidence: Evaluation across 12 systems including high-order and coupled dynamics with one shared configuration, derivative-quality diagnostics, and ablations removing RAFR, RGLP or LICA.
pg0VOzVMwU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that propagating reliability through reconstruction, derivative estimation and sparse identification is coherent and well motivated for noisy PDE discovery.
pg0VOzVMwU.main_concern: Novelty is overstated because the robust loss, local polynomial and stability-selection components are established, and the protocol leaves model selection (clean validation split) and adaptive-scale gradient handling unclear.

O7o1Sq3h1I.one_liner: PrismLoRA splits LoRA rank into blocks trained at different learning rates and assigns each task to a rate group.
O7o1Sq3h1I.problem: MoE-LoRA comparisons used one fixed learning rate, so gains over LoRA may reflect hidden learning-rate effects, and different tasks need different optimal learning rates.
O7o1Sq3h1I.method: Tunes each method's learning rate to show MoE-LoRA mostly acts as a learning-rate multiplier, explains task-dependent optimal rates with Bayesian linear estimation, and proposes PrismLoRA, which splits LoRA rank into blocks at distinct learning rates and assigns tasks accordingly.
O7o1Sq3h1I.key_idea: Treat learning rate as a per-task adaptation gain: group LoRA rank into blocks with distinct learning rates and let tasks share parameters only when their optimal rates are similar.
O7o1Sq3h1I.evidence: Vision and language multi-task experiments with per-method learning-rate tuning, a smallNORB azimuth-versus-elevation example, and grouping and learning-rate ablations.
O7o1Sq3h1I.claimed_gains: Per-method learning-rate tuning removes 89% (vision) and 96% (language) of cross-method accuracy variance; PrismLoRA's own gains are not stated numerically in the visible abstract.
O7o1Sq3h1I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the learning-rate analysis is interesting and well supported, showing most MoE-LoRA differences at a shared rate reflect a hidden learning-rate effect.
O7o1Sq3h1I.main_concern: The comparison may be unfair: PrismLoRA receives extra validated choices (groups, shifts, evaluation-time scale), its language gain rests on a single seed, and MTL-LoRA's learning-rate search stops at the edge of its range.

uC7jTkyBnD.one_liner: Conditional-expectation projection splits the residual into a side-information-predictable part and an orthogonal remainder for distributed image compression.
uC7jTkyBnD.problem: Distributed image compression methods do not separate content inferable from decoder-side information from the residual that remains undetermined, which would motivate generative modeling.
uC7jTkyBnD.method: CRDIC estimates how much side information reduces the residual left by the compressed target and converts this into a spatial estimate of the remaining residual. A deterministic branch refines reconstruction with the SI-predictable component while a stochastic branch models the remaining uncertainty.
uC7jTkyBnD.key_idea: An orthogonal MMSE decomposition of the post-decoding residual yields an SI reliability (explained variance fraction) that allocates between deterministic refinement and stochastic residual generation.
uC7jTkyBnD.evidence: Experiments on KITTI Stereo, Cityscapes and InStereo2K across bitrates, with appendix analyses of residual orthogonality, reliability calibration and stochastic reconstruction behavior.
uC7jTkyBnD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is well presented, the theory directly drives the architecture, and results show good reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality with a controllable perception-distortion trade-off.
uC7jTkyBnD.main_concern: Learned reliability and residual-scale estimates are poorly calibrated (reliability PCC 0.57-0.65 and overestimated, scale biased low) and novelty over existing deterministic-then-generative residual codecs is limited.

vGnAPBMTDW.one_liner: Two-stage trust-game paradigm manipulates partner honesty to test how LLMs form social impressions and adapt investments.
vGnAPBMTDW.problem: It is unclear how LLMs turn social impressions of others into investment decisions and adapt those decisions as feedback accumulates.
vGnAPBMTDW.method: A two-stage paradigm first induces impressions by manipulating partner honesty, then tracks investment in repeated trust games across model families and scales, with explicit-evaluation and color-control conditions and linear probes at four points to assess impression formation and retention.
vGnAPBMTDW.key_idea: Separate impression formation from later decisions by varying partner honesty before identical trust-game returns, then probe activations to see whether impressions persist.
vGnAPBMTDW.evidence: Repeated trust games with 14B-32B Qwen models, DeepSeek V4 Pro, gemini3.5-flash and three smaller models (Qwen 9B, Ministral-3-8B, Qwen 4B), plus linear probes.
vGnAPBMTDW.claimed_gains: not stated; findings are qualitative (larger models show an initial honesty penalty, the three smallest do not).
vGnAPBMTDW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-stage design with no-evaluation and color-control conditions separates impression formation from later decisions, and the large-versus-small model difference appears robust.
vGnAPBMTDW.main_concern: Linear probe results may reflect lexical or factual-history cues (such as counts of TRUE and FALSE) rather than a social impression, and the effect of prompt cues on investment is not causally isolated.

SkNFrd2GPO.one_liner: Preconditions ill-conditioned sensing matrices with a diagonal-dominant Gaussian random rotator to lower mutual coherence in sparse recovery.
SkNFrd2GPO.problem: Compressed sensing with extremely fat sensing matrices that contain many proportional columns has high coherence, which makes sparse recovery fragile.
SkNFrd2GPO.method: DogRot is a plug-and-play preconditioner built from a diagonal-dominant Gaussian random rotator that reshapes the sensing matrix to reduce mutual coherence while preserving the sparse solution set. It can be combined with existing sparse recovery algorithms.
SkNFrd2GPO.key_idea: Precondition the sensing matrix with a diagonal-dominant Gaussian random rotator that lowers mutual coherence while preserving the sparse solution set.
SkNFrd2GPO.evidence: Theoretical results on coherence reduction and sparse-solution preservation, plus experiments across diverse applications combined with existing sparse recovery algorithms.
SkNFrd2GPO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the right-side preconditioning idea novel, the observation that it breaks sparsity but preserves compressibility clever, and the validation solid across datasets.
SkNFrd2GPO.main_concern: The theorems need clearer justification of their conditions (Theorems 3.6 and 3.7), the radii are hard to interpret, and mutual coherence is arguably not the best indicator of recovery success.

nM3treiqZO.one_liner: FVS segments multi-sentence sign language videos by fusing pose features with skeletal motion cepstral coefficients and prior-guided losses.
nM3treiqZO.problem: Sentence-level sign language translation models cannot handle long multi-sentence videos, and sign language often lacks explicit motion pauses between sentences, making vision-only boundary localization hard.
nM3treiqZO.method: FVS extracts Skeletal Motion Cepstral Coefficients (SMCC) to capture high-frequency motion beyond pose features, processes pose and motion-frequency features in two parallel branches, and fuses them with a learnable Gated Fusion module. Prior-Guided Losses address under-segmentation, over-segmentation and fragmented predictions.
nM3treiqZO.key_idea: Add MFCC-style cepstral coefficients computed on skeletal motion as a frequency-domain cue, gated-fused with pose features, to localize sentence boundaries without text.
nM3treiqZO.evidence: Experiments on PHOENIX-2014T (manually stitched), How2Sign and OpenASL with F1@10/25/50 and segment error rate (SER), plus downstream translation with a frozen sentence-level SLT model.
nM3treiqZO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the vision-only segmentation task well defined and practical, and see the pose plus motion-frequency combination as effective, with downstream translation benefiting from FVS clips.
nM3treiqZO.main_concern: Baseline comparisons are not controlled, and PHOENIX-2014T is built by concatenating clips, so concatenation artifacts may supply boundary cues that inflate results.

xfTIKbjFZz.one_liner: ECROM estimates open-vocabulary object prevalence from detector evidence weighted by observation opportunity, then uses it as an active-search prior.
xfTIKbjFZz.problem: Long-term object search must learn where objects usually appear from uneven repeated observations, and unobserved locations are easily mistaken for locations where an object is absent.
xfTIKbjFZz.method: Retrospective open-vocabulary memory is formulated as probabilistic inference from censored observations, where each detection or non-detection updates belief in proportion to the robot's opportunity to observe that location. The belief for query-time concepts is converted directly into an active-search prior, evaluated on a new LOOP-Bench in ten HM3D homes.
xfTIKbjFZz.key_idea: Treat non-detections as censored observations and weight each detector observation by the opportunity to observe the location, estimating long-term prevalence per query concept.
xfTIKbjFZz.evidence: A controlled long-term benchmark in ten HM3D homes that independently varies object placement and observation opportunity across repeated traversals, plus a small real-robot study (one office, 15 trials per reviews).
xfTIKbjFZz.claimed_gains: Improves support-level AP on held-out queries by 4.5 points and search SPL by 4.2 points over the strongest competing memory in each metric.
xfTIKbjFZz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating object absence from lack of observation opportunity is an important point, and that the probabilistic formulation and the controlled LOOP-Bench are useful.
xfTIKbjFZz.main_concern: Evidence for long-term search is limited: object placements are redrawn independently (a stationary assumption), the real-robot study is small (14/15 vs 11/15 successes), and calibration of the occurrence probabilities is untested.

zH3zNB7wmb.one_liner: Local-to-global counterfactual framework for time-series classifiers: margin-aware generator plus MDL-based selector of reusable per-transition perturbations.
zH3zNB7wmb.problem: Minimal per-series counterfactuals sit at the decision boundary and leave no margin for similar series, so summarizing them cannot give population-level explanations of class transitions.
zH3zNB7wmb.method: GALACTIC-L finds small counterfactuals crossing the boundary by a margin shared within a class transition, and GALACTIC-G selects from any local generator's perturbations a small reusable set per directed class transition, expressing coverage, sparsity, and magnitude in bits under a Minimum Description Length objective.
zH3zNB7wmb.key_idea: Require a shared decision margin per class transition when generating counterfactuals, then select a small reusable perturbation set by minimizing description length in bits.
zH3zNB7wmb.evidence: Per reviews, 14 baselines, 3 classifiers, 3 seeds, sensitivity studies, and held-out tests on UCR datasets; the abstract is cut off before the results.
zH3zNB7wmb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the margin motivation clear and the modular design with a generator-agnostic selector practical, with broad experiments over many baselines.
zH3zNB7wmb.main_concern: The headline metric MDL is the method's own objective and largely tracks coverage, global baselines show limited advantage on other metrics, and counterfactual plausibility is not measured.

1XdP9ucmAe.one_liner: Learned prefill of imperfect columns plus a learned Wentges center and GPU exact pricing to speed branch-price-and-cut roots.
1XdP9ucmAe.problem: Initial columns are thought to bias the dual and slow the root of branch-price-and-cut, and preloading the optimal root LP support fails to finish on half of the hardest instances.
1XdP9ucmAe.method: A neural edge scorer guides a constructive generator that builds a pool of ordinary routes held outside the master and priced at the current smoothed dual. A second network predicts the initial Wentges smoothing center from the instance file, and bucket-graph labeling is rebuilt for the GPU with CPU certification.
1XdP9ucmAe.key_idea: Hold a learned pool of imperfect routes outside the master LP, priced at the smoothed dual, and predict the Wentges smoothing center from the instance file.
1XdP9ucmAe.evidence: Inside RouteOpt on 95 CVRP instances with 300 to 1000 customers, plus an exact branch-price-and-cut solver for unrelated parallel machine scheduling (25 benchmarks), with appendix controls against HGS pools and permuted centers.
1XdP9ucmAe.claimed_gains: Reaches the same certified root bound in 13.2% of vanilla RouteOpt's root pricing time over 95 instances, prefill alone in 26.1%, and 17.5x faster in the best case; the TL;DR adds that all 25 scheduling benchmarks are certified 12x faster.
1XdP9ucmAe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the root pricing speedups are large and consistent on all 95 instances while preserving the certified bound, and that the idea that imperfect columns help is interesting.
1XdP9ucmAe.main_concern: Only root pricing time is evaluated, not full branch-price-and-cut, and controls show a non-learned pool or center recovers much of the speedup, so the learned components are not shown to be necessary.

ZLQQfL1oz4.one_liner: Bayesian-game negotiation benchmark where a hidden-type scripted counterpart serves as verifier, enabling failure attribution for LLM agents.
ZLQQfL1oz4.problem: Existing LLM negotiation evaluations rely on LLM-vs-LLM play or aggregate outcome metrics such as deal rate, which leave agent failures opaque.
ZLQQfL1oz4.method: TERMS-Bench specifies the counterpart's latent type, policy, and payoff structure as a Bayesian game, instantiated in bilateral price negotiation where the counterpart's private state is hidden from the agent but observable to the evaluator. This supports agent-attributable failure analysis and optimality gaps against an oracle reference policy.
ZLQQfL1oz4.key_idea: Make the counterpart a diagnostic instrument by fixing its latent type and policy, so the environment itself verifies agent behavior against an oracle reference policy.
ZLQQfL1oz4.evidence: Evaluation of 13 LLM agents spanning frontier systems from major providers on bilateral price negotiation, with ablations, LLM-vs-LLM comparisons, and robustness analysis noted by reviewers.
ZLQQfL1oz4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that an evaluator-transparent counterpart gives diagnostic evaluation beyond deal-rate and LLM-vs-LLM ranking, exposing differences in surplus extraction, belief accuracy, and constraint compliance.
ZLQQfL1oz4.main_concern: The counterpart is a hand-designed, structured opponent that ignores the agent's natural-language messages, so findings may not generalize to realistic negotiation and the 'why' attribution is not uniquely identified.

iX1z5mIkuw.one_liner: Silos share only predictive distributions from frozen tabular foundation models and iteratively add consensus pseudo-labels to local contexts.
iX1z5mIkuw.problem: Tabular data sit in silos that cannot share raw records, and each silo alone lacks coverage for accurate modeling.
iX1z5mIkuw.method: Each of K agents keeps a private context and exchanges only predictive distributions over a shared query set. Aggregated predictions form high-confidence pseudo-labels that iteratively augment local contexts.
iX1z5mIkuw.key_idea: Frozen tabular foundation models use in-context learning, so agents improve by adding aggregated high-confidence pseudo-labels to their contexts instead of sharing data or parameters.
iX1z5mIkuw.evidence: Theory (K-fold variance reduction, a break-even condition for pseudo-labels, O(1/T) convergence to a neighborhood) and experiments on tabular benchmarks, classification and regression, IID and non-IID partitions, against federated-distillation and decentralized self-training baselines.
iX1z5mIkuw.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says D-ICL improves agents on their own data and outperforms federated-distillation and decentralized self-training baselines, without numbers.
iX1z5mIkuw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the communication-light setting practical, the theoretical guarantees useful, and the empirical coverage broad across datasets, backbones, partitions, and topologies.
iX1z5mIkuw.main_concern: Gains from iterative context enrichment are not consistently shown over simple prediction ensembling, the theory rests on strong pseudo-label assumptions, and federated-distillation baselines such as FedMD are limited.

0sxcQlmQy6.one_liner: Adds controllable exaggeration to text-to-motion models by fine-tuning on graded mocap data and guiding sampling with a DMP-based signal.
0sxcQlmQy6.problem: Motion generative models overlook animation principles such as exaggeration, so generated motion is physically plausible but less expressive.
0sxcQlmQy6.method: Stage one supervised fine-tunes pretrained text-to-motion models on the curated ExMoCap exaggeration dataset. Stage two formulates exaggeration with dynamic movement primitives (DMPs) and uses it as a training-free guidance signal for diffusion and flow-matching text-to-motion models.
0sxcQlmQy6.key_idea: Express exaggeration with dynamic movement primitives and use it as a training-free guidance signal in diffusion and flow-matching samplers, alongside supervised fine-tuning on graded exaggeration data.
0sxcQlmQy6.evidence: Three backbones including diffusion and flow-matching models, the ExMoCap data (26 actions at five exaggeration levels per a reviewer), standard and exaggeration-specific metrics, ablations, and a user study.
0sxcQlmQy6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating exaggeration as an explicit animation principle is a useful perspective and that both the training-time and training-free methods are evaluated on three backbones with ablations.
0sxcQlmQy6.main_concern: The practical motivation for animation workflows is underdeveloped, naturalness degrades (for example self-penetration), and methodological novelty over LoRA-based adaptation and DMP-scaling prior work is limited.

BYfFscESp0.one_liner: Shows Fisher-based prior sensitivity fails because of residual-curvature correlation, and corrects it by shifting a single eigenvalue.
BYfFscESp0.problem: In physics-based inverse models, Fisher information is the standard tool for predicting how much of an estimate comes from the prior, but its prediction fails when the omitted curvature term matters.
BYfFscESp0.method: For a MAP fit with a near-null Fisher direction v, the omitted curvature term C multiplies every parameter's prior sensitivity by one scalar, (f1 + lambda)/(f1 + v^T C v + lambda), whose sign is the correlation between fit residual and model curvature along v. The repair shifts a single eigenvalue instead of computing the full Hessian.
BYfFscESp0.key_idea: The Fisher error is one scalar along the weakest eigendirection, set by residual-curvature correlation, so a rank-one eigenvalue shift repairs it without computing curvature.
BYfFscESp0.evidence: 4,608 clinical MRI exams with two nulls built from the cohort's own residuals, plus other application settings that reviewers mention (for example photovoltaic cells) and network experiments.
BYfFscESp0.claimed_gains: Estimates move 29-38% less than the Fisher prediction and fall short of it in 92.8% to 98.8% of exams, and shifting a single eigenvalue recovers 92-99% of the full-Hessian correction on the cohort.
BYfFscESp0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large clinical experiment gives a clear, interpretable demonstration that Fisher-based sensitivity fails, with a concrete diagnostic and a simple rank-one correction.
BYfFscESp0.main_concern: The headline first-order scalar is misstated or needs extra assumptions (it can turn negative for values the paper reports), the presentation is hard to follow, and the rank-one fix recovers less with larger null spaces.

unuABFX1QX.one_liner: Telling reasoning models which conflicting passage to report removes most of the extra reasoning tokens that source disagreement causes.
unuABFX1QX.problem: Disagreeing sources in one context make reasoning models spend many more completion tokens, a conflict premium, almost all of it in reasoning.
unuABFX1QX.method: Controlled prompt interventions, including a factorial that separates a declarative reported decision from a claim that one source is operative, and an evidence-conditional stopping rule that answers CONFLICT only when the other documents leave the answer open.
unuABFX1QX.key_idea: Naming which passage to report, as a decision rather than an authority claim, removes most deliberation cost; an evidence-conditional stop answers CONFLICT when evidence cannot settle it.
unuABFX1QX.evidence: 32 constructed notes and 23 Wikipedia contradictions for the premium, 47 further contradictions for the intervention, and 150 new unsettleable items on three transfer-test models.
unuABFX1QX.claimed_gains: Conflicting passages cost 2.0-57 times the completion tokens of agreeing ones; one sentence naming the passage to report removes 81-99% of the premium on the log scale; the stopping rule cuts cost on 150 unsettleable items by 46-88% and answers CONFLICT on 94-100% while keeping settleable accuracy within 7 points (abstract cut off).
unuABFX1QX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled interventions and factorial design cleanly isolate why reasoning cost rises, and that a single reporting sentence cutting reasoning cost is a useful practical finding.
unuABFX1QX.main_concern: The tasks are highly controlled (single-turn prompts, one differing value, small synthetic and Wikipedia sets) and the main text lacks a self-contained methods section, so claims about RAG and agents reach beyond the evidence.

hgtn4txJ8r.one_liner: Text-to-CAD LLM that predicts the next modeling action and next geometric state, re-encoding executed solids at inference.
hgtn4txJ8r.problem: LLM-based CAD generation learns to predict commands without supervision of the geometric states they should produce, so one incorrect operation compromises later steps.
hgtn4txJ8r.method: Modeling operations are actions in a CAD DSL, and surface point clouds of intermediate solids are encoded into latents by a pretrained VAE. An LLM backbone generates the next action from the description and current state, an auxiliary head predicts the next state during training, and at inference the CAD kernel executes each action and the solid is re-encoded.
hgtn4txJ8r.key_idea: Pair action generation with auxiliary next-state latent prediction, and feed back the geometry actually executed by the CAD kernel at each step.
hgtn4txJ8r.evidence: Step-wise trajectories built from DeepCAD with expert-level text descriptions, evaluated on the DeepCAD test set with an ablation of future-state prediction.
hgtn4txJ8r.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says it outperforms task-specific baselines on geometric metrics on DeepCAD, without visible numbers)
hgtn4txJ8r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the approach well motivated and report strong geometric accuracy on DeepCAD, especially on longer construction sequences.
hgtn4txJ8r.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to in-distribution DeepCAD without multi-run variance, and the components are seen as incremental over existing CAD tokenization and VAE work.

jcRpRfl47X.one_liner: Meta-evaluates text-generation metrics by regressing calibrated metric outputs onto human ratings, relative to a constant-mean baseline and human agreement.
jcRpRfl47X.problem: Metric-human correlation is an unstable and inappropriate estimate of a metric's evaluation capability across datasets and languages.
jcRpRfl47X.method: A regression-based meta-evaluation learns on calibrated metric outputs to predict human ratings and reports capability relative to a constant-mean baseline and human agreement. Tested on a new multilingual style-personalized text generation benchmark with multiple annotations over 10 languages and four dimensions.
jcRpRfl47X.key_idea: Replace correlation with a score of how well calibrated metric outputs predict human ratings, normalized between a constant-mean baseline and human agreement.
jcRpRfl47X.evidence: 32 metrics from string-based, embedding-based, and LLM-judge paradigms and their ensembles meta-evaluated over 40 settings from 10 typologically diverse languages and four dimensions.
jcRpRfl47X.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports that simple string- and embedding-based metrics can match strong LLM judges once calibrated to human ratings.
jcRpRfl47X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear critique of correlation-based meta-evaluation, the regression-based alternative, and the multilingual, multiply annotated resource with ensemble analysis.
jcRpRfl47X.main_concern: The synthetic benchmark construction and the interpretation of the score (a constant-mean baseline under absolute error) need stronger validation, and the method depends on human annotations for calibration.

RWK8bPGPA6.one_liner: Evaluates how LLMs trade off search cost against continued exploration in sequential search games with a Bayesian-optimal benchmark.
RWK8bPGPA6.problem: LLMs delegated to make decisions often face costly information acquisition, requiring them to value their own future decision-making, but their sensitivity to search costs is unmeasured.
RWK8bPGPA6.method: A sequential search game where exploration is costly, with costs charged either in reward observations or in token consumption, then extended to a real-world shopping environment and a medical diagnosis environment.
RWK8bPGPA6.key_idea: Compare LLM stopping behavior across cost regimes with a payoff-optimal Bayesian decision-maker, including costs paid in thinking tokens.
RWK8bPGPA6.evidence: A costly sequential search game, a token-cost variant, a shopping environment (WebShop per reviews), and a medical diagnosis environment, across several LLMs.
RWK8bPGPA6.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that meaningful sensitivity of exploration to search costs appears only in the most recent reasoning LLMs.
RWK8bPGPA6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it a first study of exploration over time with LLM decision-makers, with a solvable Bayesian-optimal reference, clear presentation, and fairly comprehensive experiments.
RWK8bPGPA6.main_concern: The study rests on a single sequential decision task with a narrow shopping extension, omits related work on LLM exploration-exploitation, and is purely empirical.

sBqpRheF99.one_liner: Characterizes minimax adaptive-query complexity of exact-AUC classes in noiseless group testing, with one algorithm attaining all class-wise rates.
sBqpRheF99.problem: It is unclear how many adaptive OR queries are needed to recover s positives among d items when an ordinal ranking with known exact AUC is available as side information.
sBqpRheF99.method: It defines Delta = s(d-s)min{AUC, 1-AUC}, proves matching lower bounds with hard families at every prescribed rank sum, and gives one explicit algorithm that needs neither AUC nor a candidate class and attains the class-wise rates up to universal constants.
sBqpRheF99.key_idea: Query complexity is Theta(min{Delta,s} + s log(1+Delta/s^2)) in terms of the AUC-determined Delta, and candidate counting alone under-predicts the queries needed.
sBqpRheF99.evidence: Matching upper and lower bounds, certified finite budgets and recovery experiments with up to 524,288 items, plus a held-out HIV/PCBA study noted by reviewers.
sBqpRheF99.claimed_gains: Complexity is Theta(min{Delta,s} + s log(1+Delta/s^2)) for Delta >= 2; for 2 <= Delta <= s, log-cardinality is Theta(sqrt(Delta)) yet recovery requires Theta(Delta) OR queries.
sBqpRheF99.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives tight, theoretically deep upper and lower bounds for a clean, fundamental query-complexity problem.
sBqpRheF99.main_concern: The setting is specialized with little connection to machine learning, the writing is hard for non-specialists, and the practical algorithm underperforms GBS baselines in the HIV/PCBA study.

1f2ni19HMM.one_liner: Fusion rule that carries missing and corrupted modalities as separate support and conflict masses using prototype decomposition.
1f2ni19HMM.problem: Existing fusion rules write missing and corrupted channels onto one non-negative scalar per channel, so two failures that need different repairs become hard to separate.
1f2ni19HMM.method: TwoChannel decomposes each channel's sub-views over a shared prototype dictionary into an assertion and a contradiction, fills slots of absent channels by provenance-typed transport into the support mass only, and applies a per-prototype trust product from internal dispersion and cross-channel agreement.
1f2ni19HMM.key_idea: Absence and unreliability are carried on separate support and conflict masses, and restored evidence is written to support only, so the separation holds by construction.
1f2ni19HMM.evidence: A proof that neither an absent channel nor restored evidence adds a conflict term, and experiments on synthetic cohorts Syn-MOSEI, Syn-IEMOCAP and Syn-ADNI (the third per reviews).
1f2ni19HMM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing missing from corrupted channels is a useful question and that the support-versus-conflict separation is intuitive and interpretable.
1f2ni19HMM.main_concern: All experiments use synthetic cohorts with simple author-written baselines and a dictionary initialized near ground truth, and ablations show several components are not clearly needed.

Iju8fVBzHS.one_liner: Controlled study of 24 agent workflows for code optimization, varying coding mode, feedback, tools, and history.
Iju8fVBzHS.problem: Coding agents keep adding specialized agents, tools, memory, and reasoning stages, but it is unclear whether more machinery yields faster optimized code.
Iju8fVBzHS.method: A controlled framework of 24 workflows crossing four design choices: direct versus delegated coding, raw versus analyzed execution feedback, optional tools and skills, and how earlier attempts are stored, run under a shared controller that generates, validates, and benchmarks candidates.
Iju8fVBzHS.key_idea: Cross four workflow design choices under one controller and evaluator so each component's value can be measured while the others are present.
Iju8fVBzHS.evidence: GPT-OSS-20B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Qwen3.8-27B on 54 NPBench CPU kernels, plus a five-searches-per-kernel experiment crossing reports and context rebuilding for GPT-OSS-120B on a fixed 28-kernel panel.
Iju8fVBzHS.claimed_gains: Analyzed feedback with rebuilt context makes programs 1.15-1.46x faster for the three full-suite models; direct coding gives GPT-OSS models 1.47-1.51x faster programs with 25-55% fewer tokens; enabling every component raises token usage by 48-141% without a clear speed advantage.
Iju8fVBzHS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the 24-workflow controlled design with a shared task contract and evaluator gives systematic, matched comparisons and useful efficiency findings beyond isolated ablations.
Iju8fVBzHS.main_concern: Analyzed feedback is confounded with context rebuilding, so the gain cannot be attributed to better feedback, and variability across independent searches is not quantified.

iJ2Z079oM2.one_liner: Defines cruxes as sub-questions where a model's rollouts disagree and extracts them from many rollouts using cheap reranker calls.
iJ2Z079oM2.problem: Rationales in LLM outputs are too voluminous to use for high-stakes decisions, and it is unclear whether a model can anticipate which sub-questions its own forecasts will disagree on.
iJ2Z079oM2.method: Three strategies of rising cost: ask the model for cruxes a priori, extract cruxes from one rollout's reasoning, or generate many rollouts and compare reasoning across them. The last is made tractable with calls to a reranker, estimated at 86 times less compute than a judge.
iJ2Z079oM2.key_idea: A crux is a property of the distribution of rollouts, found by comparing reasoning across many sampled rollouts with a reranker instead of a generative judge.
iJ2Z079oM2.evidence: Forecasting domains, mostly with GPT models, with robustness and sensitivity checks in the appendix; reviewers note 15 valid independent events and three open-source models for directional replication.
iJ2Z079oM2.claimed_gains: The reranker uses an estimated 86 times less compute than a judge; a model's a priori assessment of its cruxes has little relation to the questions its rollouts disagree on.
iJ2Z079oM2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, the reranker-based method is cheaper and recomputable, and the finding that a priori crux prediction fails is interesting.
iJ2Z079oM2.main_concern: The reference cruxes come from the same model family and extraction mechanism as the method, and the evaluation covers few events (15 valid independent) and only forecasting, so validity is not independently established.

X0V057L9IC.one_liner: Shared pretrained-weight coordinates encode task adapters as searchable policy memories with compact language-accessible indices.
X0V057L9IC.problem: Existing task-adaptation parameterizations lack a common compact representation for storing, comparing, and retrieving learned policies.
X0V057L9IC.method: The framework represents task-specific weight adaptations in a low-dimensional space aligned with pretrained weight structure. A compact index supports similarity retrieval and a mapping from language embeddings, enabling robot-policy selection from an adapter memory.
X0V057L9IC.key_idea: Express task adaptations in shared pretrained spectral coordinates and retrieve them through compact indices mapped from language embeddings.
X0V057L9IC.evidence: Robot-policy experiments compare adaptation against LoRA, vary representation capacity, and evaluate policy retrieval and language-guided access.
X0V057L9IC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find searchable task-specific adapter memories practical and note promising adaptation and retrieval results.
X0V057L9IC.main_concern: The paper does not establish its added value over existing spectral adapters and retrieval methods through matched adapter-memory baselines.

KPRr8wWiqO.one_liner: A frozen teacher diagnoses student failures and validates adaptive strategies and hints during reinforcement learning.
KPRr8wWiqO.problem: Unscaffolded RL rollouts on difficult tasks may provide too little learning signal, while manual training scaffolds require ongoing design effort.
KPRr8wWiqO.method: AutoScaffold lets a frozen teacher inspect training evidence and propose class-level strategies and task-specific hints. Held-out validation guides class-level revisions, and the teacher adjusts assistance as student capabilities change.
KPRr8wWiqO.key_idea: Use teacher diagnosis of evolving failures to revise training strategies and hints, validating class-level changes before adjusting their use.
KPRr8wWiqO.evidence: Experiments cover embodied ALFWorld tasks, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation, with students evaluated without scaffolds.
KPRr8wWiqO.claimed_gains: AutoScaffold reports gains of 7.2 percentage points on ALFWorld and 3.8 points in average QA exact match, and surpasses QuestA on math with approximately one-third as many student training steps.
KPRr8wWiqO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value adaptive teacher diagnosis that changes assistance with student progress and yields gains after guidance removal.
KPRr8wWiqO.main_concern: Unequal baseline conditions and teacher budgets make it difficult to isolate the benefit of adaptive diagnosis across domains.

FOYHRGkUq5.one_liner: Known causal simulators and resource budgets expose failures in agents' sequential experimentation and downstream inference.
FOYHRGkUq5.problem: Current evaluations poorly measure whether research agents can design informative experiments, allocate resources, and resolve evidence before concluding.
FOYHRGkUq5.method: Causal-Discovery-Bench provides configurable linear and nonlinear structural causal systems with resource constraints and verifiable ground truth. It analyzes action trajectories and targeted ablations to distinguish experimental-design failures from downstream inference errors.
FOYHRGkUq5.key_idea: Evaluate budget-constrained sequential experiments against known causal ground truth and attribute errors to the agent's available evidentiary state.
FOYHRGkUq5.evidence: The study covers 6,727 episodes, including 3,802 linear and 2,925 nonlinear episodes, with 13 models from 5 vendors and 40 metrics in seven families.
FOYHRGkUq5.claimed_gains: Trajectory analysis attributes 94.4% of attributed errors in the linear setting and 84.5% in the nonlinear setting to experimental design rather than downstream inference.
FOYHRGkUq5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value verifiable causal ground truth and trajectory-based diagnosis of how agents gather and use evidence.
FOYHRGkUq5.main_concern: Reviewers question how conclusions generalize beyond fully observed, unconfounded synthetic causal settings.

42Tx0HOc8y.one_liner: Adjustable token rates and nested dimension prefixes expose speech-representation capacity through a single encoder.
42Tx0HOc8y.problem: Token rate alone obscures how speech representations allocate capacity between temporal resolution and token dimensionality.
42Tx0HOc8y.method: Laconic lets users choose token rate at encoding and token width at reading through nested prefixes. A nested training objective organizes linguistic and speaker information across dimensions, supporting studies of recognition, reconstruction, and generation.
42Tx0HOc8y.key_idea: Encode speech at a selectable token rate and read nested dimensional prefixes from each token to vary representation width.
42Tx0HOc8y.evidence: Experiments map rate-dimension trade-offs for ASR, reconstruction, and zero-shot TTS, with ablations of the training setup.
42Tx0HOc8y.claimed_gains: Token rate and dimensionality partially substitute between roughly 3 and 6 tokens per second, but no tested dimensionality recovers lost content at 1 token per second.
42Tx0HOc8y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the joint study of temporal token rate and representation dimensionality useful and appreciate its empirical trade-off analysis.
42Tx0HOc8y.main_concern: The paper insufficiently relates its contribution to relevant continuous speech representations and established speech-compression literature.

cwLC1qkg0a.one_liner: Attention masking separates action prediction from current reasoning tokens while retaining reasoning supervision and asynchronous episodic memory.
cwLC1qkg0a.problem: Conditioning actions on autoregressively generated reasoning adds serial latency to vision-language-action models.
cwLC1qkg0a.method: TacitVLA trains with reasoning supervision but prevents its action expert from attending to reasoning generated for the current call. For memory tasks, it can produce reasoning-ledger entries during action execution.
cwLC1qkg0a.key_idea: Mask current-call reasoning tokens from the action expert and generate episodic-memory entries concurrently with action execution.
cwLC1qkg0a.evidence: Controlled experiments span RoboMME, RMBench, LIBERO, and PhysicalAI-AV, comparing explicit reasoning and no-reasoning variants under matched architecture and training conditions.
cwLC1qkg0a.claimed_gains: TacitVLA matches its explicit-reasoning counterpart's overall success at up to 3.4× lower latency and matches no-reasoning latency at up to +17.1% success.
cwLC1qkg0a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear latency problem and controlled attention-access comparison isolating dependence on current reasoning text.
cwLC1qkg0a.main_concern: The evidence does not fully establish why reasoning supervision helps, particularly where its benefit is confounded with textual memory.

oA4ci5CG66.one_liner: Evidence-state transitions and boundary offsets organize query-relevant video segments into temporal chains.
oA4ci5CG66.problem: Direct interval-set prediction misses temporal relations and gaps, causing omitted evidence, erroneous splits, and boundary errors.
oA4ci5CG66.method: TSL models evidence onset, continuation, and termination as a learnable state-transition process and injects structural information between multimodal decoder layers. It predicts legal state chains and refines segment endpoints with continuous offsets.
oA4ci5CG66.key_idea: Represent temporal evidence as a constrained state chain with endpoint offsets, and inject that structure into intermediate video representations.
oA4ci5CG66.evidence: The paper proves a reversible interval-to-state-offset correspondence and reports temporal evidence localization and answering experiments on GroundVideoQA and NExT-GQA.
oA4ci5CG66.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider structured temporal evidence a reasonable approach and value connecting localization to answer generation.
oA4ci5CG66.main_concern: Missing implementation details and unclear training supervision and dataset splits prevent reliable assessment and reproduction of the results.

VDd0bNTdei.one_liner: NETSPACE-BENCH tests regional traffic variation and allocation alongside downstream network-management decisions.
VDd0bNTdei.problem: Citywide aggregate errors can conceal spatial failures that undermine region-level mobile network management.
VDd0bNTdei.method: The benchmark combines spatial reference and dispersion checks with five evaluation perspectives and five operational decision tasks. It distinguishes preservation of regional variation from correct allocation of demand to locations.
VDd0bNTdei.key_idea: Measure regional dispersion and spatial allocation separately, then evaluate their consequences for operational decisions.
VDd0bNTdei.evidence: Evaluations cover 12 mobile traffic models across three cities, including generation and forecasting settings.
VDd0bNTdei.claimed_gains: Of 24 eligible main generation runs, 18 retain less than 5% of observed region-mean dispersion and 19 yield energy policies approximately no better than inaction.
