zqc9KEjVtT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the shared protocol is controlled, comprehensive, and supported by behavioral analysis and an extensible open-source framework.
zqc9KEjVtT.main_concern: The main concern is that GRPO and SDPO receive unequal attempts, optimizer steps, and rounds, confounding their comparison.

o3o1TVZmrK.one_liner: Pairs flexible multimodal chemistry reading with deterministic compilation for verifiable whole-document reaction extraction.
o3o1TVZmrK.problem: Chemical reaction details distributed across schemes, tables, captions, and procedures make faithful automated extraction difficult.
o3o1TVZmrK.method: UREA lets a VLM cross-reference sources and maintain a compound ledger while a deterministic chemistry compiler enforces structure validity, evidence pointers, one-label-one-structure authoring, and count reconciliation.
o3o1TVZmrK.key_idea: Separates permissive source interpretation from deterministic record commitment using structural validation, evidence pointers, and reaction-count reconciliation.
o3o1TVZmrK.evidence: Evaluation uses audited whole-document references, multiple model families and agent harnesses, component ablations, and 500 development images for molecular recognition.
o3o1TVZmrK.claimed_gains: UREA achieves 89.73 structure-matching F1 on whole-document reaction extraction after auditing and correcting the benchmark's reference annotations.
o3o1TVZmrK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the shared workspace and verification workflow improve extraction consistency and completeness, with strong same-model comparisons.
o3o1TVZmrK.main_concern: The main concern is that limited artifact release and unclear controls make the integrated workflow's contributions difficult to verify and distinguish from existing tools.

eloUeXbRvL.one_liner: Measures and blocks unauthorized policy expansions during LLM agent execution using an online update guard.
eloUeXbRvL.problem: Dynamic authorization policies in LLM agents can silently expand to permit initially denied actions without trusted user grants, even when attacks fail.
eloUeXbRvL.method: AuthDiff defines authorization drift by re-evaluating requests before and after each policy update against the initial policy and trusted grants. Its online guard inspects context provenance and rejects policy updates that introduce unsupported permission expansions.
eloUeXbRvL.key_idea: Audits request-level decision diffs across dynamic policy updates and blocks expansions lacking a supporting trusted user grant.
eloUeXbRvL.evidence: Evaluated across eleven agent models on Progent and DRIFT dynamic authorization systems, including utility tasks requiring legitimate expansions.
eloUeXbRvL.claimed_gains: All eleven evaluated agent models exhibit drift under Progent, and on GPT-5.6-Luna the AuthDiff guard reduces drift events per update by 86.9% while preserving the same number of successful tasks.
eloUeXbRvL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing and measuring process-level authorization drift exposes a real security gap missed by terminal outcome metrics.
eloUeXbRvL.main_concern: Reviewers note that drift attribution depends heavily on potentially over-restrictive LLM-generated initial policies, which may flag task-implied expansions and harm utility on full task sets.

wk9FnLEEV0.one_liner: Stabilizes decoupled LLM reinforcement learning by filtering token discrepancies using a symmetric binary KL divergence bound.
wk9FnLEEV0.problem: Separate inference and training engines in RLVR produce mismatched token probabilities that destabilize policy gradients, while fixed ratio masks over-filter rare tokens.
wk9FnLEEV0.method: After analyzing how softmax attenuates frequent-token noise and amplifies rare-token ratio variance, the authors replace fixed ratio clipping (IcePop) with KPop. KPop thresholds the symmetric binary KL divergence between inference and training token probabilities, naturally widening tolerance at low probabilities.
wk9FnLEEV0.key_idea: Replaces fixed importance-sampling ratio masks with a symmetric binary KL divergence threshold that adapts tolerance to token probability.
wk9FnLEEV0.evidence: Noise-scaling analysis and RLVR experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks (e.g., AIME24/25, HMMT25) across dense and MoE architectures.
wk9FnLEEV0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a real training-inference mismatch issue in LLM RL and clearly explains why fixed ratio thresholds over-filter rare tokens.
wk9FnLEEV0.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing matched-retention IcePop threshold controls, limited novelty over other token-filtering heuristics, and that DPPO outperforms KPop on dense models.

QKkJNRYyZ9.one_liner: Mitigates VQ codebook collapse by aligning codebooks via Sinkhorn divergence to a density-reweighted encoder distribution.
QKkJNRYyZ9.problem: Aligning VQ codebooks directly to the raw encoder distribution over-concentrates codewords in high-density regions and under-covers sparse regions.
QKkJNRYyZ9.method: Guided by asymptotically optimal quantizer theory, AOptSA constructs a density-reweighted target distribution online using importance sampling over encoder outputs. It minimizes Sinkhorn divergence between the reweighted target and codebook distributions without modifying nearest-neighbor lookup or latent dimensionality.
QKkJNRYyZ9.key_idea: Uses online importance sampling and Sinkhorn divergence to align VQ codebooks with a density-reweighted target rather than the raw encoder distribution.
QKkJNRYyZ9.evidence: Image reconstruction benchmarks across varying codebook sizes, tracking codebook utilization and reconstruction quality against VQ baselines.
QKkJNRYyZ9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean theoretical motivation from optimal quantizer theory and the drop-in compatibility with standard nearest-neighbor VQ.
QKkJNRYyZ9.main_concern: Reviewers note that in 128-D experiments the theoretical reweighting exponent is nearly one, kNN density estimation is noisy in high dimensions, and key baselines like MMD-VQ are missing.

kiKJs8Bqvt.one_liner: Detects anomalies on simplex-valued graphs using Dirichlet graph autoencoders trained with dual-order Renyi divergences.
kiKJs8Bqvt.problem: Graph anomaly detection on compositional simplex data must preserve simplex geometry while resisting contaminated training profiles and spotting tail anomalies.
kiKJs8Bqvt.method: RD-GAEs use simplex-preserving graph aggregation and gated probability transformations with Dirichlet latents. Training minimizes a subunit-order Renyi divergence to downweight contaminated outliers, while inference scores anomalies with a superunit-order Renyi divergence that amplifies tail discrepancies without retraining.
kiKJs8Bqvt.key_idea: Trains a simplex-preserving Dirichlet graph autoencoder with a robust subunit Renyi order and scores anomalies at test time using a tail-sensitive superunit order.
kiKJs8Bqvt.evidence: Evaluated under controlled-contamination and held-out protocols on image, microbiome, and spatial transcriptomics datasets against graph, Dirichlet, and Euclidean baselines.
kiKJs8Bqvt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the under-explored intersection of simplex-valued graph data and anomaly detection, and note strong empirical gains under controlled contamination.
kiKJs8Bqvt.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the exclusive reliance on synthetic anomaly injections aligned with the superunit score's inductive bias, lack of real labeled anomalies, and inconsistent validation selection.

8KjkiZUxbj.one_liner: Accelerates long-horizon RL by mining fast successful rollouts for adaptive temporal targets and efficiency-weighted self-imitation.
8KjkiZUxbj.problem: Standard return-maximizing RL policies can learn slow, inefficient trajectories and forget rare fast solutions discovered during training.
8KjkiZUxbj.method: Temporal Self-Imitation Learning (TSIL) tracks fast successful trajectories to derive configuration-conditioned adaptive temporal targets that guide policy updates. It simultaneously replays and imitates these efficient rollouts using efficiency-weighted self-imitation learning.
8KjkiZUxbj.key_idea: Mines fast successful trajectories to set adaptive temporal targets and weight self-imitation updates, reinforcing temporally efficient behaviors.
8KjkiZUxbj.evidence: Evaluated across 30 long-horizon manipulation and navigation tasks (including MiniGrid and Meta-World) with dense/sparse rewards and state/image inputs.
8KjkiZUxbj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical motivation of using temporal efficiency as self-supervision and the broad 30-task experimental coverage.
8KjkiZUxbj.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing baselines combining adaptive temporal targets with standard SIL, making it unclear how much fast-success selection contributes beyond existing SIL.

K2vcSsNSLa.one_liner: Replaces standard query-key projections in graph transformers with learnable graph filters to adapt denoising to varying graph spectra.
K2vcSsNSLa.problem: Standard graph attention learns an average spectral filter across the training set, making it suboptimal when input graph spectra vary widely.
K2vcSsNSLa.method: The authors derive spectral attention scores conditioned on input graph spectra and instantiate them as Graph Convolutional Attention (GCA) using graph-filtered queries and keys. They analyze GCA on asymptotic stochastic block models and evaluate it inside graph denoising and DiGress-style diffusion models.
K2vcSsNSLa.key_idea: Applies learnable graph filters to queries and keys so attention scores adapt to each input graph's spectrum during denoising and diffusion.
K2vcSsNSLa.evidence: Asymptotic SBM theory and experiments on synthetic and real graph denoising and generation datasets.
K2vcSsNSLa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the spectral perspective linking spectral diversity to denoising gains and the clean theoretical motivation.
K2vcSsNSLa.main_concern: Reviewers highlight an unequal-capacity denoising comparison (66% more parameters and extra eigenvector inputs for GCAT) and an overlooked low-rank constraint in Proposition 1/Theorem 1.

p3lWU0kg07.one_liner: Pretrains a multimodal time-series JEPA world model with stop-gradient numerical references and a decoupled probabilistic decoder.
p3lWU0kg07.problem: Time-series foundation models rarely combine textual context and auxiliary covariates into reusable latent predictive representations.
p3lWU0kg07.method: Pythia pretrains a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) that applies contextual corrections to predicted future latent states guided by a stop-gradient numerical reference. A separate probabilistic decoder is then adapted on top of the frozen predictive representations and history.
p3lWU0kg07.key_idea: Decouples JEPA latent dynamics pretraining with stop-gradient numerical-reference contextual correction from a separately adapted probabilistic observation decoder.
p3lWU0kg07.evidence: Evaluated on the MUSE benchmark leaderboard with controlled ablations on context sources (descriptions, events, covariates), freezing, and reference losses.
p3lWU0kg07.claimed_gains: On MUSE, Pythia-Tiny achieves 0.6879 normalized MASE and 0.4269 WSQL, reducing errors by 6.26% and 5.00% relative to the strongest published leaderboard model.
p3lWU0kg07.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge strong aggregate performance on MUSE and thorough controlled ablations on context modalities and freezing.
p3lWU0kg07.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over Chronos-2 and JEPA, and raise fairness concerns regarding extra pretraining data, initialization, and single-seed evaluation.

aFUiBkQyPD.one_liner: Extracts hierarchical planners, knowledge-graph memory, and user simulators from domain textbooks to train proactive dialogue agents.
aFUiBkQyPD.problem: LLMs remain reactive in long-horizon dialogues, and manually designing planners, memory structures, and user simulators for proactive agentic systems requires heavy expert effort.
aFUiBkQyPD.method: TOPAS automatically derives a hierarchical MDP planner, a knowledge-graph memory, and a user simulator from unstructured domain textbooks. It generates structured supervision via uncertainty-aware self-annotation and trains hierarchical policies with reinforcement learning.
aFUiBkQyPD.key_idea: Automatically extracts a hierarchical MDP planner, graph memory, and user simulator from domain textbooks and trains policies via uncertainty-aware self-annotation and RL.
aFUiBkQyPD.evidence: Evaluated via double-blind expert assessments (41 experts) of extracted structures and downstream experiments on psychotherapy and persuasive dialogue benchmarks.
aFUiBkQyPD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that automatically constructing planner-augmented dialogue agents from domain textbooks is an important, well-motivated problem with broad evaluation.
aFUiBkQyPD.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the sole reliance on LLM user simulators and saturated LLM judges without human dialogue evaluation, and note missing comparisons to simpler textbook-prompted or retrieval agents.

zfBxw1Z3iu.one_liner: Induces recurring procedures from successful agent traces into a library of parameterized natural-language LLM subroutines.
zfBxw1Z3iu.problem: Existing experience-induction methods format learned knowledge as sample workflows, prose skills, or rigid code tools, limiting effectiveness across reasoning and planning tasks.
zfBxw1Z3iu.method: ARISE identifies recurring procedures in successful agent traces and synthesizes them into a reusable library of parameterized subroutines executed by an LLM. It compares executing induced subroutines against retrieving the same knowledge as prose skills or rewriting it as code tools.
zfBxw1Z3iu.key_idea: Synthesizes recurring agent-trace procedures into parameterized natural-language subroutines executed separately by an LLM rather than as retrieved prose or code.
zfBxw1Z3iu.evidence: Evaluated across five tasks in narrative deduction, rule application, and constraint planning on multiple model families against prompting, skill, and code-tool baselines.
zfBxw1Z3iu.claimed_gains: ARISE scores 2.3 to 10.8 percentage points above the strongest evaluated baseline, and improves average accuracy by up to 15.6 points over skills and up to 19.1 points over code tools.
zfBxw1Z3iu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the controlled comparison between executing LLM subroutines, retrieving prose skills, and rewriting as code tools is a useful, well-performing empirical study.
zfBxw1Z3iu.main_concern: Reviewers note modest novelty over prior library-learning methods (AWM, ASI, ACE), single-run results without significance testing, and missing comparisons to multi-agent handoffs or prompt optimization.

WBLF08hpqs.one_liner: Identifies aligned multi-layer SAE feature circuits via co-activation and geometric similarity to synthesize coordinated steering vectors.
WBLF08hpqs.problem: Single-layer activation steering such as CAA applies one static direction that fails to persist cleanly across layers for diverse inputs.
WBLF08hpqs.method: CircuitSteer uses pretrained Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to build multi-layer co-activation circuits ranked by contrast specificity and decoder geometric alignment. It synthesizes dense per-layer steering vectors from the selected sparse features to apply coordinated multi-point residual-stream interventions at inference time.
WBLF08hpqs.key_idea: Synthesizing dense per-layer steering vectors from geometrically aligned, contrast-specific SAE co-activation circuits guides multi-layer trajectories at inference.
WBLF08hpqs.evidence: Evaluations test toxicity, emotion intensity, and sycophancy steering on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
WBLF08hpqs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the motivation and multi-layer SAE circuit framing are clear and well-explained.
WBLF08hpqs.main_concern: Reviewers point out wider steering-coefficient tuning ranges for CircuitSteer than baselines, lack of causal validation for co-activation circuits, and inconsistent baseline wins.

Q4gS70AH9E.one_liner: Uses warm-start magnitude scoring to isolate sparse (<2.5%) full-rank subnetworks driving DPO and GRPO preference optimization.
Q4gS70AH9E.problem: It is unclear whether preference-optimization weight updates are structured by the RL objective or data, and how to certify sparse subnetwork masks.
Q4gS70AH9E.method: The authors derive a loss-retention bound and certifiability condition for parameter importance scoring, and propose warm-start magnitude scoring with threshold estimation to train sparse subnetworks at >=97.5% sparsity. They analyze subnetwork overlap and capabilities via Jaccard similarity, CKA, and linear probing across DPO and GRPO.
Q4gS70AH9E.key_idea: Warm-start magnitude scoring under a certified loss-retention bound recovers dense DPO and GRPO dynamics while updating fewer than 2.5% of parameters.
Q4gS70AH9E.evidence: Experiments span Llama, Qwen3, and OLMo-3 across math, coding, syntax, and semantics, using Jaccard, CKA, and probing diagnostics.
Q4gS70AH9E.claimed_gains: Updates fewer than 2.5% of parameters (>=97.5% sparsity) while recovering dense DPO and GRPO training dynamics.
Q4gS70AH9E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that investigating objective- vs. data-driven subnetwork structure with certified sparsity bounds across multiple model families is interesting.
Q4gS70AH9E.main_concern: Reviewers flag that DPO vs. GRPO differences are confounded by 10x learning-rate differences, and that CKA/probing zeroed out frozen pretrained weights rather than evaluating the actual subnetwork.

lmBI0rWxso.one_liner: Compresses LLM embedding tables by learning orbit-guided local tight-frame codebooks allocated sequentially via global reconstruction residuals.
lmBI0rWxso.problem: Existing embedding compression methods rely on fixed coding geometries like coordinate blocks or low-rank subspaces rather than discovering data-adaptive geometry.
lmBI0rWxso.method: OrBIT learns overlapping local charts from orbit dynamics to constrain shared codewords, allocates coding capacity sequentially from global reconstruction residuals, and compiles away the orbit machinery into a compact decoder.
lmBI0rWxso.key_idea: Constrains shared codewords with overlapping tight-frame charts learned from orbit dynamics and allocates capacity using global residual errors.
lmBI0rWxso.evidence: Theoretical distortion bounds and empirical compression evaluations across four LLM embedding tables (including GPT-2 and 7B models).
lmBI0rWxso.claimed_gains: Achieves 37.9x compression on GPT-2 and over 23x on each 7B embedding table relative to 16-bit storage.
lmBI0rWxso.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the transparent accounting of all decoder storage overhead and the tight-frame error decomposition theory.
lmBI0rWxso.main_concern: Reviewers find that learned orbit scaffolds are full-rank and impose no real subspace constraint, while evaluation is limited to 10k-token subsets with high reconstruction error and no perplexity results.

7iccUQ2Se9.one_liner: Formalizes KV cache eviction as expectation estimation and applies self-normalized importance sampling for decode-time correction.
7iccUQ2Se9.problem: Existing KV cache eviction methods rely on heuristics without formal theoretical grounding or correction for dropped entries during decoding.
7iccUQ2Se9.method: The authors prove KV eviction is NP-complete, frame it as estimating attention expectations via sampling, and reinterpret prior heuristics as zero-variance biased estimators. They propose a probabilistic eviction scheme with self-normalized importance sampling for decode-time correction.
7iccUQ2Se9.key_idea: Frames KV cache eviction as importance-sampled expectation estimation and uses self-normalized importance weights to correct for evicted entries at decode time.
7iccUQ2Se9.evidence: Theoretical hardness and bias-variance bounds alongside experiments on Llama3.2-3B and Qwen3-4B on RULER and LongBench subsets.
7iccUQ2Se9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear probabilistic formalization unifying prior eviction heuristics and enabling decode-time correction.
7iccUQ2Se9.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited empirical scope (small 3B/4B models, partial benchmarks, marginal gains) and lack of end-to-end throughput or latency measurements.

buhynGpe8l.one_liner: Benchmarks indirect prompt injection with 38,675 paired attack/control web views and trains 0.8B detectors plus adaptive attacks.
buhynGpe8l.problem: Existing prompt injection benchmarks lack paired control pages and broad coverage of web domains, languages, and browser views.
buhynGpe8l.method: BrowseSafe++ pairs production-derived attacked webpages with identical control pages across HTML, Markdown, accessibility tree, and screenshot views, trains 0.8B BrowseSafe-Guard detectors, and evaluates adaptive attacks via BrowseSafe-Adapt.
buhynGpe8l.key_idea: Constructs matched attack/control webpage pairs across four browser views from rewritten wild captures to train compact detectors and adaptive attackers.
buhynGpe8l.evidence: Evaluations across 38,675 entries spanning 12 domains, 24 attack types, and 18 placements for detection and executing browser agents.
buhynGpe8l.claimed_gains: BrowseSafe++ extends BrowseSafe from 14,719 to 38,675 entries, and BrowseSafe-Adapt increases attack success from a few percent on replay to up to 95% after adaptation.
buhynGpe8l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the paired attack/control design for eliminating topic/style confounds and the multi-view plus adaptive attack evaluation.
buhynGpe8l.main_concern: Reviewers raise circularity concerns because frontier LLMs (GPT-5.5, Claude Sonnet 5) filter/rewrite the dataset and are then evaluated on it, and note BrowseSafe-Guard is not tested on external benchmarks.

oMgvjTBD53.one_liner: Inverts a single logged activation layer back to tokens and flags steering via calibrated reconstruction residuals.
oMgvjTBD53.problem: Activation steering alters LLM behavior without modifying weights or prompts, evading weight and prompt inspection.
oMgvjTBD53.method: The auditor inverts a single logged hidden layer back to token preimages and compares reconstruction residuals against calibrated clean-reference distributions without needing the prompt, steering vector, or injection site.
oMgvjTBD53.key_idea: Detects activation steering from a single layer's activations by optimizing token-preimage reconstruction and thresholding calibrated residuals.
oMgvjTBD53.evidence: Experiments across five open models from Qwen, Gemma, and Llama families covering PGD attacks, jailbreaks, and adaptive attacks.
oMgvjTBD53.claimed_gains: The final layer flags every PGD attack at relative budget 0.02+ (0.0085 on three models) with 0–2% clean false positives, catches all 46 judge-positive Qwen jailbreaks, and blocks adaptive attacks (0/270 vs. 91/210 unconstrained).
oMgvjTBD53.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the prompt-free, single-layer auditing formulation and the finding that differentiating through the detector cripples adaptive PGD jailbreaks.
oMgvjTBD53.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the high inversion latency (9–28s per prompt/layer) that precludes real-time use, narrow evaluation scope (PGD at last prompt token, 50 prompts), and unclear practical threat model.

gTHscIAr6Y.one_liner: Solves federated robust matrix completion via multi-block AltGDmin and mergeable KLL quantile sketching for outlier thresholding.
gTHscIAr6Y.problem: Distributed robust low-rank matrix completion and PCA suffer from high communication overhead when estimating global outlier thresholds.
gTHscIAr6Y.method: The authors extend Alternating Gradient Descent and Minimization (AltGDmin) to multiple blocks and integrate mergeable KLL quantile sketches to compute global row thresholds for outlier support estimation.
gTHscIAr6Y.key_idea: Combine multi-block AltGDmin with mergeable KLL quantile sketches to estimate global outlier thresholds communication-efficiently in federated settings.
gTHscIAr6Y.evidence: Theoretical convergence, communication, and sample complexity proofs are paired with experiments on simulated data and real videos.
gTHscIAr6Y.claimed_gains: The proposed approach is proven to be r-times more communication efficient than, and order-wise as fast as, the fastest existing robust LRMC solution, where r is the rank.
gTHscIAr6Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the federated robust recovery problem is well motivated and the theoretical analysis linking KLL sketch error to recovery guarantees is solid.
gTHscIAr6Y.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the paper and appendix presentation, severe condition-number dependence in bounds, and mismatch between fresh-sample theory and full-data implementation.

qhy3yS1iSu.one_liner: Inserts a discrete codebook adapter into a frozen MLLM residual stream to make fusion contributions inspectable on the forward path.
qhy3yS1iSu.problem: Dense latent representations fused by multimodal LLMs are opaque, obscuring which domain features the fusion carries during inference.
qhy3yS1iSu.method: AFTERIMAGE inserts a lightweight adapter with 0.20-0.71% added parameters that discretizes the residual stream at multiple depths into shared codebook sequences, from which domain-associated motifs are extracted.
qhy3yS1iSu.key_idea: Discretize an MLLM adapter's residual-stream updates at multiple depths into shared codebook tokens to record inspectable domain motifs on the forward path.
qhy3yS1iSu.evidence: Evaluations span 3D brain MRI counterfactual synthesis, LIBERO-Pro robotic manipulation, and video question answering, plus causal code interventions.
qhy3yS1iSu.claimed_gains: With 0.20-0.71% added parameters, AFTERIMAGE lowers counterfactual-age FID on 3D brain MRI synthesis from 1.93 to 0.43, raises pi_0.5 robot success by 26.0 points averaged over shifted LIBERO-Pro suites, and improves video QA accuracy by 16.0 points.
qhy3yS1iSu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note strong downstream performance across diverse tasks with very few added parameters and appreciate the causal code intervention tests.
qhy3yS1iSu.main_concern: Reviewers question the interpretability claims because residual bypass paths still carry uninspected information and MRI attribute motifs may trivially reflect templated text inputs.

l7MusOHIxR.one_liner: Defines punctuality to measure whether SAE or crosscoder features emerge abruptly in discrete layers rather than gradually.
l7MusOHIxR.problem: Circuit interpretability assumes features correspond to discrete computational steps, but feature dictionaries are rarely evaluated for step-wise emergence.
l7MusOHIxR.method: The authors introduce punctuality, derived from layer-wise feature availability and participation ratio, to audit Bias-in-Bios circuits, residual-stream SAEs, neuron bases, and crosscoders.
l7MusOHIxR.key_idea: Quantify how abruptly a feature emerges across layers via the participation ratio of layer-wise availability increments.
l7MusOHIxR.evidence: Experiments analyze Gemma models, Gemma Scope SAEs and crosscoders on Pile data, and a Bias-in-Bios circuit case study.
l7MusOHIxR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that operationalizing discrete step-wise feature emergence is an interesting and underexplored interpretability question.
l7MusOHIxR.main_concern: Reviewers note that high punctuality is anti-correlated with causal importance, random directions also score high on punctuality, and no circuits are built to show punctuality improves faithfulness.

9ZszP5r7Qd.one_liner: Mitigates visual modality collapse in interleaved VLA models by injecting discrete noise into historical action tokens during fine-tuning.
9ZszP5r7Qd.problem: Temporally correlated historical actions in interleaved VLA fine-tuning create a low-entropy shortcut that starves visual encoder gradients.
9ZszP5r7Qd.method: The authors analyze visual modality collapse via information-bottleneck and gradient dynamics, propose Modality Information Gain and KL Divergence Shift diagnostics, and introduce Historical Action Noise Injection (HANI) to corrupt action-history tokens during SFT.
9ZszP5r7Qd.key_idea: Injects discrete, semantically mismatched noise into historical action tokens during SFT to break temporal action shortcuts and restore visual gradient flow.
9ZszP5r7Qd.evidence: Information-theoretic analysis and supervised fine-tuning experiments on gaming and embodied VLA tasks.
9ZszP5r7Qd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the historical-action shortcut in interleaved VLAs is an important failure mode and HANI is simple with zero inference overhead.
9ZszP5r7Qd.main_concern: Theoretical claims of inevitable gradient starvation overreach the simplified assumptions, and empirical evaluation is narrow and lacks direct verification of gradient awakening.

wP4S5y5o0N.one_liner: Generates parameter-perturbed linear programming test variants via inverse optimization to maximize constraint coverage and expose hidden LLM modeling errors.
wP4S5y5o0N.problem: Testing LLM-generated optimization models only on original numerical instances leaves inactive constraints untested and hides constraint-level modeling errors.
wP4S5y5o0N.method: The authors formulate constraint coverage for linear programs, search prescribed parameter domains via KKT-based optimization to activate uncovered inequality constraints, and reconstruct the variants into natural-language problems.
wP4S5y5o0N.key_idea: Uses KKT-based optimization over parameter domains to synthesize natural-language LP test variants that activate previously untested inequality constraints.
wP4S5y5o0N.evidence: Experiments on public optimization-modeling benchmarks measuring constraint coverage and newly exposed modeling errors.
wP4S5y5o0N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting software-testing coverage to expose hidden constraint errors in automated LP modeling is well-motivated and clearly presented.
wP4S5y5o0N.main_concern: The method is restricted to linear programs with reference models, exposes errors on only ~0.6% of tested formulations, and lacks comparisons against alternative verification or mutation baselines.

iOc4wguGH4.one_liner: Shows cross-corpus layer-ablation differences can stem from target-token composition (such as whitespace) rather than depth specialization.
iOc4wguGH4.problem: Cross-corpus layer-ablation studies interpret differential early-layer damage as task specialization without controlling for target-token composition differences.
iOc4wguGH4.method: Decomposes early-late layer damage interactions between corpora by target-token type, recomputes effects under matched target mixtures and position matching, and derives a tokenizer-only pre-run risk screen.
iOc4wguGH4.key_idea: Stratifies cross-corpus layer-ablation damage by target-token class and matched target mixtures to isolate token-composition artifacts from depth specialization.
iOc4wguGH4.evidence: Tested across five model instances on GSM8K vs. Wikitext and additional held-out corpus pairs with position matching and continuous readouts.
iOc4wguGH4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a real measurement confounder in depth-specialization ablations and explains the mechanism clearly.
iOc4wguGH4.main_concern: Reviewers question how prevalent the tested three-token-ahead mean-blending protocol is in prior work and whether the artifact affects standard next-token evaluations.

uC5CVLtnwe.one_liner: Uses a frozen discrete diffusion model as a conditional-entropy surrogate for budget-constrained active pixel acquisition.
uC5CVLtnwe.problem: Acquiring high-fidelity measurements is costly, and task-specific active sensing policies do not generalize across downstream tasks.
uC5CVLtnwe.method: Formulates pixel selection as minimizing conditional entropy H(C | Y) given side information z, approximating the likelihood with a frozen Discrete Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (D3PM) to train a mask generator via DisARM/Gumbel-Softmax.
uC5CVLtnwe.key_idea: Approximates mutual-information pixel acquisition using a frozen D3PM as a differentiable conditional-entropy surrogate for mask-network training.
uC5CVLtnwe.evidence: Evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and FastMRI datasets with mask-state and side-information ablations.
uC5CVLtnwe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear writing, model-agnostic mutual-information framing, and thorough diagnostics of surrogate vs. true objectives.
uC5CVLtnwe.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over Active Diffusion Subsampling, weak empirical gains on FastMRI and CIFAR-10 (where variance-greedy replaces entropy), and missing DPS baselines.

RCcvuOH08I.one_liner: Rewrites pre-norm Transformer blocks as an exact advection-diffusion-reaction system to measure layerwise transport, dissipation, and FFN responses.
RCcvuOH08I.problem: Dynamical-systems interpretations of Transformers often approximate or omit nonlinear feed-forward layers and normalization, leaving block-level computation unclear.
RCcvuOH08I.method: The paper derives an exact advection-diffusion-reaction (ADR) decomposition of sequential pre-norm Transformer blocks, separating attention into skew-adjoint transport and self-adjoint diffusion while retaining the nonlinear FFN response as a reaction term.
RCcvuOH08I.key_idea: Decomposes pre-norm Transformer blocks algebraically into exact skew advection, symmetric diffusion, and native nonlinear FFN reaction operators.
RCcvuOH08I.evidence: Analyzed depth profiles and ran attention-approximation interventions across seven pretrained decoder models.
RCcvuOH08I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact ADR algebraic decomposition is mathematically clean and reveals interesting depth-profile differences across models.
RCcvuOH08I.main_concern: Theoretical novelty is viewed as limited—amounting to standard operator splitting and algebraic rewriting—and the motivation and connection to downstream task computation remain unclear.

QcxfKgKX3D.one_liner: Learning goal-conditioned actions from OCT volumes enables closed-loop soft-tissue shape control with explicit and diffusion policies.
QcxfKgKX3D.problem: Microscale soft-tissue deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based shape-control models can be expensive and hard to adapt.
QcxfKgKX3D.method: The framework learns from user demonstrations and closes the loop with OCT feedback, comparing full volumes, sparse tissue-masked volumes, and voxelized point clouds. It tests residual conditioning with deterministic explicit and generative diffusion action models.
QcxfKgKX3D.key_idea: Representing current and target tissue morphology in the same OCT space supports goal-conditioned closed-loop control from demonstrations.
QcxfKgKX3D.evidence: Evaluation covers 12 configurations and 576 phantom rollouts on 3-DoF depth and 6-DoF directional tasks, with additional ex vivo experiments reported in reviews.
QcxfKgKX3D.claimed_gains: Residual conditioning reduces directional Shape RMSE from 0.748 to 0.555 mm for full-volume Diffusion.
QcxfKgKX3D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the physical OCT-guided system and substantial hardware evaluation are useful, including its reporting of negative results.
QcxfKgKX3D.main_concern: All reviewers emphasize that ex vivo rollouts do not improve the primary shape-matching metric, so reliable target-shape control remains unproven.

AqJ1ikaGN2.one_liner: Maintaining a geometry-conditioned target state grounds multi-turn dialogue in persistent entities and timestamped 3D trajectories.
AqJ1ikaGN2.problem: Dynamic-scene dialogue requires language references to remain tied to an entity's physical time and changing metric position across turns.
AqJ1ikaGN2.method: Track4D-Bench pairs dialogue with calibrated observations and timestamped entity tracks. LMM-Track4D preserves a geometry-conditioned target state across turns and selects spatial-temporal evidence while separating dialogue order from queried physical time.
AqJ1ikaGN2.key_idea: A persistent geometry-conditioned target state links conversational references to entity identity and physical timestamps for trajectory recovery across turns.
AqJ1ikaGN2.evidence: Track4D-Bench contains 526 clips, 23.5k frames, and 7.5k entity tracks, with language, geometric, external QA, and grounding evaluations.
AqJ1ikaGN2.claimed_gains: LMM-Track4D improves CIDEr by 0.247, BLEU-4 by 10.2 points, METEOR by 10.5 points, and trajectory-step accuracy by 19.4 percentage points over the stated baselines.
AqJ1ikaGN2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that paired dialogue and trajectory supervision is useful and that the target-state architecture is coherent and experimentally supported.
AqJ1ikaGN2.main_concern: Reviewers most often see an integration of existing tracking and video-QA techniques without clear evidence of new joint capabilities or modeling advances.

g1Z808o5i1.one_liner: Diagnoses asymmetric music-style steering hysteresis and adds styles by transporting hidden states and projecting onto real target-style trajectories.
g1Z808o5i1.problem: Activation-steering vectors and affine maps remove musical styles effectively but fail to add styles in text-to-music models.
g1Z808o5i1.method: The authors measure addition-versus-removal asymmetry via a two-arm protocol, model styles as thin sets of trajectories in state space, and propose transporting hidden states and projecting them onto the nearest real target-style trajectory from a bank.
g1Z808o5i1.key_idea: Treats musical styles as thin trajectory sets and achieves style addition by transplanting hidden states onto the nearest real target-class trajectory.
g1Z808o5i1.evidence: Experiments on a text-to-music model evaluated by an automatic listener, comparing vector translation, affine maps, optimized pushes, and state transplantation.
g1Z808o5i1.claimed_gains: Steering removal recovers most of the distance between two styles whereas addition recovers only about a tenth.
g1Z808o5i1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the sharp, under-explored question of steering reversibility and the clean two-arm hysteresis evaluation protocol.
g1Z808o5i1.main_concern: Overwriting hidden states with bank trajectories at every step after commitment resembles clip retrieval rather than steering, and source-content preservation versus bank similarity is not measured.

vAMQi4NC5L.one_liner: Proves a signed deterrence law for RL audit certainty and shows task-timing shifts reverse proxy-calibrated verifiers in deployment.
vAMQi4NC5L.problem: Classical deterrence assumes only expected penalty matters and that verifier audit rates tuned on a proxy task transfer reliably to deployment.
vAMQi4NC5L.method: The authors derive the stationary variance of learned violation values under constant-step-size RL, establish a signed law for audit certainty at fixed expected penalty, and test timing-dependent sign flips between proxy and delayed-reward deployment tasks.
vAMQi4NC5L.key_idea: Shows sparse-audit variance creates a signed audit-certainty effect whose flip boundary shifts with reward timing, reversing proxy-calibrated verifier behavior.
vAMQi4NC5L.evidence: Theoretical derivation under a Gaussian approximation, deep-RL phase diagrams, and controlled timing- and gap-matched proxy-versus-deployment experiments (including GRPO).
vAMQi4NC5L.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers value the controlled timing and gap-matched interventions showing proxy-to-deployment deterrence reversal and the transparent variance analysis.
vAMQi4NC5L.main_concern: Presentation is very dense with unclear notation, and statistical claims in the GRPO regression and cap-free controls are overstated or underpowered.

cnaYLnpsAV.one_liner: REUSE certifies recursive self-improvement on reused benchmarks by restricting search feedback and budgeting error across possible promotion histories.
cnaYLnpsAV.problem: Repeatedly reusing a fixed benchmark during recursive self-improvement causes adaptive overfitting because candidate proposals depend on prior evaluation feedback.
cnaYLnpsAV.method: REUSE (Risk-controlled Evaluation Under Sequential Evolution) restricts the evaluation feedback returned to the proposer to promotion decisions and allocates statistical error budgets across possible promotion histories to guarantee genuine population improvement with probability at least 1 - alpha.
cnaYLnpsAV.key_idea: Restricts feedback to accept/reject decisions and allocates hypothesis-testing error across all possible sequential promotion histories to control adaptive overfitting.
cnaYLnpsAV.evidence: Statistical guarantees paired with empirical experiments using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct searching over scikit-learn classification pipelines on the covertype dataset.
cnaYLnpsAV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptive overfitting from benchmark reuse in recursive self-improvement is an important problem and appreciate accounting for decision-history leakage in the error budget.
cnaYLnpsAV.main_concern: Empirical validation is too narrow—limited to one classification dataset and one LLM tuning scikit-learn configs—and assumes agents cannot inspect detailed error feedback.

zm4shNFc6u.one_liner: AutoDataBench isolates agentic data intelligence across three fixed-pipeline tasks—tool use, retrieval, and knowledge injection—with pre-training effect prediction.
zm4shNFc6u.problem: Existing auto-research benchmarks entangle data improvements with training frameworks, hyperparameters, and compute budgets, preventing clean attribution of data-centric agent capabilities.
zm4shNFc6u.method: AutoDataBench holds training pipelines and non-data factors fixed while evaluating LLM agents on iterative data diagnosis, organization, and construction across three tasks, measuring both optimization outcomes and pre-training prediction of data-intervention effects, plus trajectory reuse for mid-training.
zm4shNFc6u.key_idea: Fixes model architectures and training recipes across three learning paradigms so agents can only improve performance via iterative training-data interventions.
zm4shNFc6u.evidence: Evaluates frontier LLMs on tool use (SFT), retrieval (contrastive learning), and knowledge injection (distillation) with hidden OOD tests and downstream coding mid-training.
zm4shNFc6u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value fixing the training pipeline to isolate data-centric capabilities across three paradigms and including hidden OOD evaluations.
zm4shNFc6u.main_concern: Positioning relative to Curation-Bench is under-developed, and experiments lack no-feedback search controls to separate iterative feedback learning from repeated trial-and-error selection.

4aRS4d3TRM.one_liner: Formalizes Functional Alignment for time-series–language models, proving an identification limit of similarity metrics and testing Executable Claim Alignment.
4aRS4d3TRM.problem: Retrieval and representational similarity metrics do not certify whether text descriptions are historically supported, add predictive information about the future, or improve forecasting.
4aRS4d3TRM.method: The authors formalize Functional Alignment across four targets (correspondence, historical support, predictive innovation, and fitted-model assistance), prove an identification limit for fixed-encoder correspondence, and evaluate Executable Claim Alignment (ECA) checking typed interpretations against observations.
4aRS4d3TRM.key_idea: Separates representational correspondence from historical support, predictive innovation, and forecasting utility, and verifies typed time-series claims via executable checks.
4aRS4d3TRM.evidence: Theoretical identification proof plus experiments across 20 encoder configurations, 11 held-out CaTS domains, TRUCE factual-reversal tests, and Time-MMD forecasting.
4aRS4d3TRM.claimed_gains: Retrieval reaches 51.8 to 156.4 times chance across 20 encoders yet the strongest retriever scores 0.4984 on temporal factual reversal, while ECA achieves 0.9874 domain-macro verification accuracy across 11 CaTS domains.
4aRS4d3TRM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the conceptual distinction between representational similarity, factual support, and forecasting utility, supported by factual-reversal and random-projection controls.
4aRS4d3TRM.main_concern: Pooled forecasting confidence intervals ignore correlation across shared datasets and representations, and presentation/code issues (including a sign mismatch in evaluation code) undermine key claims.

vfmwgrHqfP.one_liner: Diagnoses LLM opponent modeling in repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with known recursive beliefs via live play and interventions.
vfmwgrHqfP.problem: Successful adaptive play in interactive games does not reveal whether an LLM genuinely tracks an opponent's mental states or relies on behavioral heuristics.
vfmwgrHqfP.method: The authors introduce a repeated hide-and-seek benchmark against algorithmic opponents with ground-truth recursive beliefs, separating payoff, action prediction, and belief tracking through live interaction, fixed-history tests, information interventions, and probability-supervised fine-tuning.
vfmwgrHqfP.key_idea: Evaluates LLMs against algorithmic opponents with explicit ground-truth recursive beliefs using fixed-history forecasting and belief-information interventions.
vfmwgrHqfP.evidence: Experiments with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (including behavioral and probability SFT) and frontier models such as GPT-5.4 against algorithmic opponents (RB, QL, WSLS, ToM0–2).
vfmwgrHqfP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate using algorithmic opponents with ground-truth beliefs and information-intervention controls to decouple game payoff from belief tracking.
vfmwgrHqfP.main_concern: The benchmark is restricted to a simple two-action hide-and-seek game against a closed set of known opponent families, and probability-SFT checkpoints are not tested in live play.

0THBONJE24.one_liner: VL-DE generates variable-length multimodal data via an insertion-based continuous-time diffusion framework with a higher-order sampler.
0THBONJE24.problem: Most diffusion and flow models assume fixed data dimensions, forcing variable-length multimodal tasks like layout generation to use padding or separate length models.
0THBONJE24.method: Variable Length Diffuse Everything (VL-DE) models variable cardinality through an auxiliary insertion-based stochastic process with a tractable training objective and exploits its additive generator structure to build a higher-order sampler.
0THBONJE24.key_idea: Handles variable-length multimodal generation on arbitrary state spaces via an insertion-based continuous-time generator paired with a higher-order sampler.
0THBONJE24.evidence: Theoretical derivation of the training objective and sampler, validated empirically on layout generation benchmarks including RICO.
0THBONJE24.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the insertion-based continuous-time formulation for variable-length generation well-motivated and note solid results on RICO.
0THBONJE24.main_concern: Claims of generating arbitrary lengths on arbitrary state spaces exceed the empirical scope, which is restricted solely to layout generation with modest gains over strong baselines.

42aNZtufj0.one_liner: Formulates recurrent sequence memory via probabilistic design models and Kalman filtering, yielding Bayesian Layers that propagate mean and covariance.
42aNZtufj0.problem: Existing fixed-state recurrent sequence architectures specify recurrence equations whose underlying probabilistic assumptions about memory dynamics and interference remain implicit.
42aNZtufj0.method: The paper introduces auxiliary probabilistic design models defined by an initial distribution and input-dependent dynamics and evidence factors, where Bayesian filtering determines the recurrent update. A linear-Gaussian design model yields the Bayesian Layer maintaining a memory estimate and dense covariance via a Kalman update, while resetting covariance recovers Delta-rule updates and another design model recovers linear attention, GLA, and Mamba-2.
42aNZtufj0.key_idea: Applies Kalman filtering to linear-Gaussian probabilistic design models so recurrent layers maintain both a memory mean and covariance matrix to shape writes and reduce interference.
42aNZtufj0.evidence: Supported by theoretical derivations, controlled associative recall tasks, multi-query associative recall (MQAR), WikiText-103 language modeling, and distillation into a pretrained 340M Gated DeltaNet evaluated on RULER.
42aNZtufj0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the probabilistic design-model framework cleanly unifies recurrent memory updates and that the covariance-based interference derivation is well supported in controlled recall tests.
42aNZtufj0.main_concern: Reviewers note that comparisons do not match recurrent state size or compute budget, and that the pretrained Gated DeltaNet distillation experiment is confounded by differing objectives and trainable parameters.

FTwTdy3Tw4.one_liner: Reconstructs hidden screens from wall reflections using a learned sparse light-transport coupling and counterfactual verification of local edits.
FTwTdy3Tw4.problem: Diffuse wall propagation spreads and mixes light from hidden screens across camera pixels, causing ambiguity that lets unsupported strokes and textures enter reconstructions.
FTwTdy3Tw4.method: Transport Coupling and Counterfactual Recovery Learning (TCCRL) learns a scene-shared nonnegative sparse transport matrix for a fixed capture geometry to both predict wall measurements and route wall evidence back to an initial screen state. Counterfactual Transport Verification and Selective Write-back then tests bounded local additions and deletions against complementary measurement partitions and sequentially writes back accepted edits.
FTwTdy3Tw4.key_idea: Pairs a scene-shared sparse screen-wall transport matrix for reverse evidence routing with counterfactual testing of local edits against complementary wall measurements.
FTwTdy3Tw4.evidence: Evaluated across five screen-content benchmarks and two physical capture setups against 19 baselines with ablations.
FTwTdy3Tw4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the route-then-verify formulation with a dual-orientation sparse transport coupling is well motivated and broadly evaluated.
FTwTdy3Tw4.main_concern: Reviewers note that the learned transport matrix overfits to a single static capture geometry requiring retraining for any scene change, and that presentation is dense and hard to read.

8NIfou0DkK.one_liner: Guides LLM catalyst design via Monte Carlo Tree Search over chemical actions scored by property predictors and expert preference rewards.
8NIfou0DkK.problem: LLMs applied to open-ended material and catalyst design frequently violate domain-specific chemical and synthetic constraints during intermediate reasoning steps.
8NIfou0DkK.method: CataPath formulates catalyst design as Monte Carlo Tree Search over a chemically informed action space using an LLM agent guided by a hybrid reward combining property-prediction signals with an Expert Preference Reward Model trained from domain feedback. The authors also curate CataDesignQR, a dataset of literature-grounded design goals, verified solutions, and expert-scored reasoning trajectories.
8NIfou0DkK.key_idea: Combines MCTS over a chemically structured action space with a hybrid reward merging property predictors and an expert-preference reward model.
8NIfou0DkK.evidence: Evaluated on CO2 reduction electrocatalyst generation and organic structure-directing agent optimization using the curated CataDesignQR dataset.
8NIfou0DkK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that enforcing practical chemical constraints in LLM catalyst design is well motivated and that combining property predictors with expert preference rewards is sensible.
8NIfou0DkK.main_concern: Reviewers question the technical novelty over existing search-and-reward agent frameworks and note that experiments do not isolate the necessity of MCTS versus simpler search under matched compute.

E7yJynhpMZ.one_liner: Links public blockchain transfers and swaps with traditional equity prices, news, and fundamentals across 890 tokenized equities.
E7yJynhpMZ.problem: Existing finance and blockchain datasets observe traditional equity markets and public on-chain activity separately, preventing joint study of tokenized equities.
E7yJynhpMZ.method: The authors build a ticker-aligned dataset covering 890 tokenized equities, 249.5M transfers, and 31.3M swaps paired with exchange prices, news, and fundamentals. Using this linked dataset, they analyze off-hours price discovery and account co-holding and formulate two tasks: dark-window equity forecasting and open-world next-asset prediction.
E7yJynhpMZ.key_idea: Aligns on-chain tokenized-equity transfers and swaps by ticker with off-chain exchange prices, news, and fundamentals to enable off-hours forecasting and next-asset prediction.
E7yJynhpMZ.evidence: Empirical analyses and benchmark tasks on 890 tokenized equities with 249.5M transfers and 31.3M swaps linked to traditional equity market data.
E7yJynhpMZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that aligning on-chain tokenized-equity activity with traditional equity data addresses a timely gap and yields a useful dataset.
E7yJynhpMZ.main_concern: Reviewers flag internal inconsistencies in dataset counts and timeline dates (e.g., 140.1M vs 156.7M minute bars and September 2024 vs June 2025 start dates) and weak validation of forecasting gains.

SNWGuphcc3.one_liner: Compresses cross-agent KV-cache deviations into low-rank states and chains corrections along multi-agent workflows without an extra reference prefill.
SNWGuphcc3.problem: Agent-specific prefixes alter KV caches for shared context in multi-agent LLM serving, causing redundant prefills or high memory overhead from online delta correction states.
SNWGuphcc3.method: KVCMAS represents cross-agent KV-cache deviations using compact low-rank anchor states (via truncated SVD) and chains corrections directly along the agent workflow using preceding agents' caches rather than computing a separate external reference prefill. This supports dynamically changing shared context while keeping the first agent's cache exact.
SNWGuphcc3.key_idea: Stores cross-agent KV-cache deltas in low-rank form and chains corrections from preceding agents' caches without constructing a separate reference prefill.
SNWGuphcc3.evidence: Evaluated across language and vision-language multi-agent workloads (including MMLU) against KV cache sharing baselines like KVComm, measuring accuracy, memory, and TTFT.
SNWGuphcc3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the low-rank deviation observation is clean, the chained reference reuse is practical, and the reported memory savings over KVComm are meaningful.
SNWGuphcc3.main_concern: Reviewers note that the method is incremental over KVComm and that headline memory comparisons are confounded by using different anchor pool sizes (V=10 vs V=20).

lhyKkgg8IL.one_liner: Uses SVD-free Chebyshev-guided subspace sketching and nullspace compensation in a multigrid-inspired unfolding network for efficient pansharpening.
lhyKkgg8IL.problem: Existing pansharpening networks repeatedly transform high-dimensional spatial-spectral features, incurring high computational cost that scales with feature dimension and resolution.
lhyKkgg8IL.method: OSSNet restricts principal transformations to compact spatial and channel subspaces using sketch operators (CSS and CCS) inside a multigrid-inspired unfolding architecture with residual-correction blocks. To avoid unstable in-network SVD, a Chebyshev-Guided Approximation Mechanism builds approximately row-orthogonal projections from Gram statistics, paired with nullspace compensation to preserve out-of-subspace details.
lhyKkgg8IL.key_idea: Constructs adaptive orthogonal spatial-channel sketch projections from Gram statistics via Chebyshev approximation with nullspace compensation to avoid repeated SVD in pansharpening.
lhyKkgg8IL.evidence: Evaluated on pansharpening benchmarks comparing reconstruction accuracy, cross-sensor transfer, parameters, FLOPs, and latency, plus subspace energy and PCA-distance analyses.
lhyKkgg8IL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SVD-free Chebyshev-guided subspace sketching achieves a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off with low parameter and FLOP counts.
lhyKkgg8IL.main_concern: Reviewers note that OSSNet shows weak performance on full-resolution evaluations and point out missing spectral-radius normalization details for Chebyshev and Newton-Schulz convergence.

y0ggdjsHSw.one_liner: Injects per-iteration randomization into Taylor and Hessian-free Runge-Kutta Langevin Monte Carlo schemes to improve dimension dependence without third-derivative Lipschitzness.
y0ggdjsHSw.problem: Existing high-order Langevin Monte Carlo algorithms require a Lipschitz third-order potential derivative and suffer O~(d eps^(-2/3)) dimension dependence in mixing time.
y0ggdjsHSw.method: The paper introduces two randomized higher-order LMC algorithms: a Hessian-based Taylor scheme and a Hessian-free Runge-Kutta variant that inject extra randomness at each iteration. Under gradient and Hessian Lipschitz conditions beyond log-concavity, the authors derive non-asymptotic W2 error bounds and mixing time complexities.
y0ggdjsHSw.key_idea: Adds per-iteration randomization to second-order Taylor and Hessian-free Runge-Kutta LMC discretizations to achieve order-1.5 convergence without third-order Lipschitz assumptions.
y0ggdjsHSw.evidence: Supported by non-asymptotic W2 convergence theory under log-Sobolev-type/beyond-log-concavity settings and small-scale numerical experiments (d=8 to 16).
y0ggdjsHSw.claimed_gains: Achieves non-asymptotic W2-error bounds of O(d h^(3/2)) and mixing time complexity O~(d^(2/3) eps^(-2/3)), improving over O~(d eps^(-2/3)) for existing high-order LMC algorithms.
y0ggdjsHSw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the randomized second-order LMC variants are mathematically well motivated and potentially improve dimension dependence without third-derivative assumptions.
y0ggdjsHSw.main_concern: Reviewers flag a potential missing sqrt(d) factor in the proof's Gronwall step, close similarity to randomized midpoint discretization, and limited low-dimensional empirical evidence.

41iwjBHVGe.one_liner: Characterizes marginal-preserving coupled autoregressive decoding and proves that independent sampling from fixed arithmetic path strata never lowers expected batch success.
41iwjBHVGe.problem: Coordinating multiple autoregressive samples to improve batch coverage (pass@k) without distorting individual output distributions lacks clear theoretical guarantees on when coupling helps or hurts.
41iwjBHVGe.method: The paper separates complete-answer marginal fidelity from synchronous next-token conditional fidelity and analyzes coupled samplers via arithmetic decoding. It proves that independent sampling from fixed path strata preserves individual answer distributions and cannot reduce expected batch success, while showing counterexamples for random-shift lattices and per-token refreshed strata.
41iwjBHVGe.key_idea: Uses arithmetic decoding over fixed path strata with independent per-stratum sampling to guarantee marginal preservation and non-degradation of expected batch success.
41iwjBHVGe.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs, counterexamples, and experiments on two Qwen2.5 checkpoints across GSM8K, MATH-500, and a synthetic Countdown task at K=8.
41iwjBHVGe.claimed_gains: A held-out Countdown study finds a 5.1-percentage-point improvement in pass@8 for a lattice.
41iwjBHVGe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the distinction between path-level and synchronous conditional fidelity is insightful and that the guarantees and counterexamples are well defined and candidly evaluated.
41iwjBHVGe.main_concern: Reviewers note limited practical impact and experimental scope: the theoretically protected path-stratified method shows no statistically significant gains on GSM8K or MATH-500, and positive gains appear only for an unprotected lattice on synthetic Countdown.

3z13wAq89c.one_liner: Fine-tunes a 4B LLM world model to predict ML experiment logs and scores from code, gating real executions by confidence and UCB.
3z13wAq89c.problem: Machine learning engineering agents struggle to scale test-time search because executing every candidate script to obtain feedback is slow and expensive.
3z13wAq89c.method: MLE-World fine-tunes Qwen3.5-4B on code-to-execution trajectories to predict error traces, training logs, and validation scores along with a confidence score, using a confidence gate for selective real execution and a UCB-inspired rule to balance exploration.
3z13wAq89c.key_idea: Predict terminal logs, exception classes, and validation scores from code with a 4B world model and use its token-level confidence for selective execution gating and UCB candidate selection.
3z13wAq89c.evidence: Evaluated offline and inside AIDE search across three seeds per task with corpus-memorization controls and multiple search policies.
3z13wAq89c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree predicting full execution records and exception classes with a built-in confidence signal is cleaner and more actionable for debugging than scalar score prediction.
3z13wAq89c.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the lack of true out-of-distribution generalization—training and testing on the same benchmark tasks where 26%-48% of test programs share their exact parent in training—making the cost savings circular.

4ApH4ZkzXP.one_liner: Reshapes flow-model RL rewards using regularized D-optimal diversity weights computed directly from reward-model embeddings within each prompt group.
4ApH4ZkzXP.problem: Per-sample scalar rewards in text-to-image flow RL ignore visual redundancy within a prompt group, encouraging visually repetitive high-scoring samples.
4ApH4ZkzXP.method: The method extracts embeddings already computed during reward evaluation, applies SVD reduction and regularized D-optimal experimental design to compute within-group diversity weights, and reshapes scalar rewards before advantage computation without extra encoders or RL rule changes.
4ApH4ZkzXP.key_idea: Compute within-prompt-group diversity weights via regularized D-optimal design on existing reward-model embeddings to reweight scalar rewards before advantage calculation.
4ApH4ZkzXP.evidence: Evaluated on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium with Advantage Weighted Matching (AWM) and DiffusionNFT on DrawBench (including three held-out reward models) and Pick-a-Pic.
4ApH4ZkzXP.claimed_gains: Reaches each baseline's highest evaluation reward on Pick-a-Pic 1.38x faster for AWM and 4.32x faster for DiffusionNFT in GPU hours.
4ApH4ZkzXP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree reusing reward-model embeddings for diversity reweighting is lightweight, clean, avoids extra encoder passes, and plugs directly into existing flow RL algorithms.
4ApH4ZkzXP.main_concern: Reviewers warn that diversity is measured in the same PickScore embedding space being optimized (without independent features or human diversity checks), lacks empirical validation of the redundancy assumption, and tests only one backbone (SD3.5-M).

ripiVbV3k3.one_liner: Combines residual-quantization facet discovery with turn-aware hierarchical RL to ask early-gain clarification questions in domain-specific retrieval.
ripiVbV3k3.problem: Underspecified domain-specific retrieval queries require multi-round clarification that adapts to dialogue history and prioritizes questions yielding early retrieval gains.
ripiVbV3k3.method: CLEAR uses Progressive Residual Facet Discovery (PRFD) with residual quantization over retrieved documents, domain facts, and dialogue history to propose candidate facets, and trains a question-selection policy via Turn-aware Hierarchical Policy Optimization (THPO) over a per-round retrieval-gain return matrix.
ripiVbV3k3.key_idea: Discover clarification facets from residual-quantized document contrasts and optimize question selection via turn-aware hierarchical RL over stopping-weighted per-round retrieval gains.
ripiVbV3k3.evidence: Evaluated across legal, medical, and patent interactive retrieval benchmarks on NDCG@10 at round 4 and mean NDCG@10 over rounds 1-4.
ripiVbV3k3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree tying a stopping-weighted per-round retrieval-gain return to document-grounded facet discovery is well-motivated and improves both final and average NDCG@10 across three domains.
ripiVbV3k3.main_concern: Reviewers question whether shared residual-quantization prefixes actually yield coarse-to-fine clarification facets, note missing concrete method/IO details, and flag inconsistent simulator settings across component comparisons.

XJlIuBObvp.one_liner: Reweights on-policy distillation tokens by accumulated student-teacher distributional discrepancy to emphasize earlier positions.
XJlIuBObvp.problem: Standard on-policy distillation averages token-level KL losses uniformly even though teacher supervision degrades at later positions as student rollouts diverge.
XJlIuBObvp.method: The authors analyze position bias via constrained optimization and derive Importance-Weighted On-Policy Distillation (IW-OPD). IW-OPD assigns each token a weight based on the accumulated discrepancy between student and teacher distributions, upweighting earlier tokens and downweighting later ones.
XJlIuBObvp.key_idea: Weight each token's on-policy distillation loss by the accumulated student-teacher distributional discrepancy so prefixes with reliable teacher supervision dominate updates.
XJlIuBObvp.evidence: Controlled prefix-versus-suffix studies, constrained-optimization analysis (Proposition 1), and multi-scale evaluations including same-size and cross-scale settings on benchmarks such as AIME-2025.
XJlIuBObvp.claimed_gains: Improves performance over standard OPD by 6.9 points on AIME-2025 while converging faster in same-size and cross-scale settings.
XJlIuBObvp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the position-bias phenomenon is clearly demonstrated through the prefix-versus-suffix diagnostic and tested across multiple scales and ablations.
XJlIuBObvp.main_concern: Reviewers cite a gap between the constrained-optimization theory and the practical cumulative-disagreement weighting heuristic, plus missing comparisons to published OPD token-reweighting baselines.

HU8zsOj2dy.one_liner: Retains unlabelable active-learning samples as k-center CoreSet distance anchors to steer later picks toward rare classes.
HU8zsOj2dy.problem: Active-learning annotators searching image archives for rare species waste budget on unlabelable frames such as empty camera-trap images, and skipping them discards spatial information.
HU8zsOj2dy.method: The authors propose Anchored k-center CoreSet, which keeps each failed pick as a distance anchor that lowers the priority of nearby unlabeled images without removing them from the pool. They test three preregistered hypotheses and a fourth partly retrospective selector benchmark across camera-trap and exploratory drone pools.
HU8zsOj2dy.key_idea: Store unlabelable annotation attempts as distance anchors in k-center CoreSet so subsequent queries avoid neighborhoods around empty or unusable images.
HU8zsOj2dy.evidence: Preregistered 16-seed experiments on unfiltered iWildCam and Snapshot Serengeti pools with DINOv3 and CLIP embeddings, plus exploratory drone-pool experiments with simulated failures.
HU8zsOj2dy.claimed_gains: Anchoring raises rare-class discovery AUC over ten rounds by +9.5% on iWildCam and +32.3% on Snapshot Serengeti over skipping alone, with exact sign-flip p = 2^-16 across 16 seeds.
HU8zsOj2dy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the practical focus on failed-pick pool conventions and the strong preregistered statistical protocol with paired tests and multiple seeds.
HU8zsOj2dy.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological change beyond standard CoreSet and narrow external validity, as the confirmed gain holds only on two unfiltered camera-trap datasets and fades with pretrained filtering.

SSGh9taU3O.one_liner: Trains an 8B language model via SFT and RL on lossless TVM schedule traces to write and refine GPU kernels.
SSGh9taU3O.problem: GPU kernel optimization requires coordinating interacting compiler transformations to preserve correctness while improving runtime, which is difficult for small language models.
SSGh9taU3O.method: The authors design a compact, lossless representation that deterministically decodes into TVM MetaSchedule compiler traces while preserving transformation parameters and dependencies. They train a small language model (LITTLE DRAGON) with supervised fine-tuning on 108,594 search-derived construction and refinement examples across 54,116 workloads, followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable execution feedback.
SSGh9taU3O.key_idea: Encode TVM MetaSchedule traces in a lossless deterministic format and train a small language model with SFT and execution-feedback RL to generate and refine full optimization scripts.
SSGh9taU3O.evidence: Training and evaluation on 54,116 distinct TVM MetaSchedule workloads split by workload and program hash, comparing an 8B trained model against search baselines and larger models.
SSGh9taU3O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the careful engineering of the lossless schedule representation, the execution-verified reward design, and the clean workload-and-hash train/test split.
SSGh9taU3O.main_concern: Reviewers question practical value given tight coupling to one compiler, TVM version, and GPU after expensive data collection, and flag weak numerical correctness checks using only one random input per workload.

T29eizddcM.one_liner: Prunes LLM vocabulary heads offline using calibration top-K participation rates and nearest-neighbor logit substitution costs.
T29eizddcM.problem: Large multilingual and multimodal vocabularies make LLM decoding heads expensive on edge devices, while standard frequency-based static pruning drops rare-but-critical tokens and ignores token substitutability.
T29eizddcM.method: The authors propose PASS (Participation And Substitution Selection), a calibration-guided, training-free two-stage static vocabulary-head pruner. Stage one tags tokens as keep, prune, or uncertain using their decode-time top-K participation rate; stage two ranks uncertain tokens by a mass-weighted logit deficit incurred when substituting each token with its nearest surviving neighbor.
T29eizddcM.key_idea: Combine decode-time top-K token participation filtering with nearest-neighbor logit-deficit substitution cost to select a static surviving vocabulary subset offline.
T29eizddcM.evidence: Training-free static pruning experiments across three LLM architectures up to 2B parameters at 50% keep fraction on downstream evaluation tasks.
T29eizddcM.claimed_gains: Reduces decode-time head cost from O(Vd) to O(|S|d) per token and retains nearly full-head quality at a 50% keep fraction.
T29eizddcM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the deployment bottleneck is practical and well motivated, and that the training-free participation-and-substitution approach is simple and interpretable.
T29eizddcM.main_concern: Reviewers point to missing baselines (such as probability-mass-only ranking and dynamic vocabulary pruning), undefined perplexity retention metrics, and evaluation limited to models at or below 2B without multimodal tests.

zbVkh7mMk1.one_liner: Reranks candidate chains of thought with a user-conditioned cross-attention evaluator to balance debiasing and informativeness.
zbVkh7mMk1.problem: Conservative LLM debiasing reduces harmful outputs but often produces unnecessary refusals or generic, uninformative answers that ignore user context.
zbVkh7mMk1.method: The authors propose PersonaBias, which generates candidate chains of thought using strategy-guided prompting and scores them with a trained User-Conditioned Reasoning Evaluator using bidirectional cross-attention between user profiles and reasoning trajectories. The evaluator classifies candidates into biased, acceptable-but-underinformative, or unbiased-and-informative, and the highest-scoring trajectory guides a frozen base LLM.
zbVkh7mMk1.key_idea: Train a bidirectional cross-attention evaluator over user profiles and candidate chains of thought to select an unbiased, informative reasoning trajectory for a frozen base LLM.
zbVkh7mMk1.evidence: Experiments on FairMT, BBQ, and a human-annotated dataset comparing PersonaBias against single-generation and random-selection controls.
zbVkh7mMk1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the three-level reasoning quality formulation beyond binary bias checks and the flexibility of keeping the base LLM frozen.
zbVkh7mMk1.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations do not isolate the benefit of user personalization from generic quality reranking or simpler personalized prompting, and raise fairness and jailbreak risks from user-conditioned outputs.

dXh3eRyudc.one_liner: Decomposes compositional diffusion errors into source estimation and inference approximation, deriving sensitivity bounds and an estimator.
dXh3eRyudc.problem: Conditional diffusion models often fail at compositional generation from geometric combinations of source distributions, and it is unclear how source estimation error and inference-time approximation error interact.
dXh3eRyudc.method: The authors prove that arbitrarily small source estimation errors can cause arbitrarily large errors in geometric compositions, derive sufficient conditions and local sensitivity bounds to prevent error blowup, and propose a diagnostic metric based on effective sample size (rESS) without ground-truth targets. They evaluate analytical versus learned scores in diffusion experiments on synthetic and realistic data.
dXh3eRyudc.key_idea: Separate source distributional estimation error from inference-time approximation error via local sensitivity bounds to diagnose when accurate inference correction worsens out-of-distribution compositions.
dXh3eRyudc.evidence: Theoretical sensitivity bounds, Gaussian constructions, and diffusion experiments comparing analytical and learned scores on synthetic and realistic data.
dXh3eRyudc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical characterization showing that small source estimation errors can blow up under composition and that more accurate inference-time correction can worsen results when source error dominates.
dXh3eRyudc.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the limited practical relevance due to artificial source setups, the sensitivity of the rESS diagnostic to density-ratio estimation, and the lack of an actionable algorithm to improve the tradeoff.

YykuecnXiS.one_liner: Establishes minimax rates for submodular minimization from noisy 1-local comparisons via sequential unbiased log-odds and multilevel estimators.
YykuecnXiS.problem: Existing upper bounds for submodular minimization under noisy sigmoid pairwise comparisons leave a rate gap, and minimax complexity for general nonlinear preference transfer functions is unknown.
YykuecnXiS.method: The authors design an algorithm combining sequential unbiased log-odds estimation and antithetic multilevel Monte Carlo with stochastic subgradient optimization over the Lovasz extension under a hard budget of T 1-local queries. They derive matching upper and lower minimax bounds jointly in n and T for sigmoid and general regular transfer functions, plus fixed-n rates via the inverse modulus of continuity.
YykuecnXiS.key_idea: Pair sequential unbiased log-odds and antithetic multilevel marginal estimators with Lovasz-extension optimization to match minimax lower bounds under noisy 1-local preference queries.
YykuecnXiS.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower minimax proofs for sigmoid, power, logarithmic, infinite-order flat, and arbitrary transfer functions, accompanied by illustrative numerical experiments.
YykuecnXiS.claimed_gains: Establishes the minimax rate Theta_b(min{1, n^(3/2)/sqrt(T)}) for fixed sigmoid strength b > 0, improving the previous upper bound O_b(n^(7/5) T^(-2/5)), and proves Theta_rho(min{1, n psi_cl(sqrt(n/T))}) for general regular transfer functions.
YykuecnXiS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a well-defined theoretical question, closes the sigmoid rate gap with matching bounds, and provides technically sound mathematical analysis.
YykuecnXiS.main_concern: Reviewers point to limited algorithmic originality over existing unbiased log-odds and multilevel estimators, weak practical motivation for 1-local submodular queries, and overly simplified numerical experiments.

6uL7mSo94t.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM program search methods across 10-20 seeds to measure gains relative to seed-to-seed noise floors.
6uL7mSo94t.problem: LLM-in-the-loop program discovery systems report gains over plain sampling from only one or a few runs, leaving unclear whether improvements exceed random seed variance at practical call budgets.
6uL7mSo94t.method: Holding model, task, call budget, and selection rule fixed, the authors compare best-of-N sampling, two island-evolution methods (FunSearch and a lighter island model), reflect-then-sample, and an EXP3 router across 15 verified construction and solver tasks with 10 to 20 seeds per method. They also test a pre-registered ladder of covering designs and cross-model checks with weaker and stronger models.
6uL7mSo94t.key_idea: Evaluate LLM program search methods against best-of-N sampling using 10-20 independent seeds at fixed call budgets to quantify the seed-variance noise floor.
6uL7mSo94t.evidence: Controlled multi-seed experiments across 15 construction and solver tasks at 100, 300, and 1,000 LLM calls, primarily with DeepSeek V4-Flash plus 4-task checks on Qwen2.5-7B and gpt-4.1-mini.
6uL7mSo94t.claimed_gains: At 100 calls no method beats best-of-N sampling by more than 1.03 seed standard deviations (1.15 without island resets), while at 1,000 calls evolution beats sampling by about 2 seed standard deviations on two of four tasks.
6uL7mSo94t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper investigates an important statistical reliability question in LLM program search using disciplined multi-seed comparisons across six methods.
6uL7mSo94t.main_concern: Reviewers argue the conclusions are broader than the evidence because 11 of 13 main tasks are isomorphic covering-design problems, the main grid uses one model and small budgets, and cross-model checks cover only four tasks.

G3dhpqopdT.one_liner: Analyzes feature-novelty and residual-error data selection in a linear continual-learning teacher-student model under task similarity.
G3dhpqopdT.problem: Data-selection theory typically assumes stationary objectives, leaving open how sample prioritization affects new-task learning versus catastrophic forgetting across sequential tasks.
G3dhpqopdT.method: The authors derive closed-form forgetting and transfer effects for feature-novelty and residual-error sample scoring in a two-task structured linear teacher-student model, extending the ordering from soft reweighting to hard budgeted selection.
G3dhpqopdT.key_idea: Derive closed-form continual-learning trade-offs in a linear teacher-student model showing novelty scoring consistently aids retention while residual-error scoring flips sign across a task-similarity threshold.
G3dhpqopdT.evidence: Theoretical analysis on a two-task linear teacher-student model supported by experiments on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, AwA2, and nonlinear CIFAR-100.
